210.intro: The 210 has a 22-key keypad (page 26 of the book). Here is what every key does, how the menus move, and what the little lights on the display mean. Tap HEAR and lord Mathew will read it to you.

keys.does: Turns the indicator on and off. Press it when the indicator is off to apply power; press it again to turn it off.

In normal operation, pressing it zeroes the weight display right away, up to the limit picked during setup: 4 percent or 100 percent of the scale's capacity. Press it after the asterisk key and you are in Review mode, where you can look at the setup without changing it.

Two jobs. Pressed by itself, it stores the current gross weight as the tare and switches the display to net weight, and the NET light turns on. Or type a number first, then press it, and that number becomes the tare instead. A tare equal to or over the scale's capacity will not take.
Shows the current tare weight on the display for three seconds.

Switches the display between net weight and gross weight. The NET or GROSS light shows which one you are looking at. If no tare has been entered, this key flashes a short error and the indicator stays in gross mode.

In normal operation it picks the weighing units: tons, pounds, pound-ounces, ounces, tonnes, kilograms, or grams, whichever units setup has turned on. Press it after the asterisk key and you enter Test mode, which runs the display test.

The 'show me' and 'take it' key. While you are looking through setup, pressing ENTER shows the current setting of the item on the display. After you type a value, pressing ENTER tells the indicator to accept and process it.

The backup and get-out key, and the door to the extra features. Inside setup, pressing it backs up to the previous prompt, and it is how you leave setup when you are done. In normal operation it shows the feature prompt; the key you press next picks the feature: asterisk then ZERO is Review mode, asterisk then UNITS is Test mode, asterisk then NET/GROSS works with the accumulators, and asterisk then PRINT changes the print ticket format.

These type numbers and letters during setup and normal operation. The 1 and 0 keys also answer questions: 1 means YES and 0 means NO. For letters, press a key over and over until the letter you want shows, like an old cell phone keypad.

Sends the weight and other data out the printer port. The indicator will not print until the weight on the display is stable. Showing gross, it prints gross; showing net, it prints gross, tare, and net. To change the ticket format, press asterisk, then PRINT.
Opens the clock settings so you can set the time, the date, and the consecutive ticket number. Press ENTER at each prompt to keep what is shown, or type the new value and press ENTER.

A multi-job key whose work depends on the mode of operation picked in setup: counting pieces with sample sizes, weigh-in and weigh-out ID storage, starting, pausing, and resuming a digital fill, or entering a livestock head count for the next ticket.

Also mode-dependent: it sets the alarm weight, the stored fill presets for the digital fill control, the preset weight comparator values (there can be up to 8), or the checkweigher accept and over values.

menus: Getting into setup is done at the back of the indicator: take out the calibration access screw, reach through the hole with a small tool, and press the calibration switch. The display shows SETUP. (Breaking a legal-trade seal ends Legal for Trade status until the scale is tested and resealed by the proper authority.)
Keep pressing and releasing the calibration switch to rotate the starting menu: SETUP, CAL, PRINT, SERIAL, and the rest. When the menu you want shows, press ENTER.

Inside a menu, ENTER shows the current setting. Type a new value with the number keys and press ENTER to take it, or just press ENTER to keep what is there and move on. The 1 key answers YES and the 0 key answers NO.
The asterisk key backs up one prompt at a time. To leave setup, press the asterisk key, or turn the indicator off and on twice.

If you only want to look: asterisk then ZERO opens Review mode, which displays every setup and calibration setting without changing anything. The Test mode (asterisk then UNITS) runs six display checks and ends by showing the C1 to C4 calibration numbers for about four seconds each. Write them down: they are the fingerprint of a good calibration.

lights.does: On when the displayed weight is within a quarter of a division of the center of zero. If this light is not on with the scale empty, the scale is not truly at zero.
On when the weight display is steady. Off means the weight is still moving more than the motion limits picked in setup. The indicator will not print while this is off.
On when the display is showing gross weight: everything on the scale, with nothing taken away. Gross shows whenever no tare is stored.
On when the display is showing net weight: the gross weight minus the tare weight.
On when the display is showing the tare weight itself.

The checkweigher lights, only active when the Checkweigher feature is turned on: UNDER means below the minimum acceptable weight, ACCEPT means inside the acceptable range, and OVER means at or above the over value. With the preset weight comparator feature instead, the same three lights mean the weight has reached preset 1, 2, or 3 (PWC1, PWC2, PWC3).
On when the display is in Count mode, so the number shown is a piece count, not a weight.

lights.key: Unit lights: lb, kg, tn, t, oz, g
lights.does: The lit unit light tells you the units of the displayed weight: pounds, kilograms, tons, tonnes, ounces, or grams. Check this before you believe a number.
A flashing annunciator means the indicator is waiting for you: it wants keypad input for the mode that is flashing.

ideas.h: What this box actually does
ideas.text: The load cells under the scale turn weight into a tiny electrical signal. The 210's whole job is to read that signal, turn it into the number on the display, and remember how that number was taught to it during setup and calibration. Every feature in this book — tare, counting, filling, printing — is arithmetic built on top of that one measured weight.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything sitting on the scale. Tare is the part you want to ignore, like the truck or the bin. Net is what is left: gross minus tare. The GROSS, NET, and TARE lights exist so you never have to guess which of the three numbers you are looking at — and the NET/GROSS key walks between them, so long as a tare has been stored.

ideas.h: Zero is a promise, span is the ruler
ideas.text: Calibration teaches the indicator two anchor points. Zero says: this empty scale means nothing, remember it. Span says: this known test weight means exactly this much. Between those two anchors the indicator stretches a straight ruler and reads every other weight against it. That is why the setup holds both a zero value and a span value, and why changing either one bends every reading until you prove it again with a known weight.

ideas.h: The C numbers are the fingerprint
ideas.text: When a calibration finishes, the indicator keeps four numbers, C1 through C4. Together they are the fingerprint of that calibration. Write them down after any good calibration: if the scale is ever damaged or a board is swapped, typing the C numbers back in restores the calibration without test weights. They only show themselves at the end of the Test mode run (asterisk, then UNITS), about four seconds each. They cannot fix a scale whose parts were changed, and they are not a shortcut for a legal-for-trade recalibration.

ideas.h: Look all you want, touch carefully
ideas.text: Setup is where the scale's behavior is decided, and getting in means opening the calibration switch at the back, so it is a deliberate act. Review mode is the safe pair of eyes: asterisk then ZERO walks you through every setup and calibration setting without changing a single one. When something behaves strangely, look in Review first, compare it to what you expect, and only open real setup when you are sure what you are changing.

ideas.h: Stable means you can trust it
ideas.text: The indicator samples the load cell signal many times a second. When the samples stop changing beyond the motion limit picked in setup, the STABLE light turns on. Nothing prints and no weight is locked in until the scale is stable, so if the light will not settle, the scale is telling you something: vibration, wind, a bind, or a load still moving. Believe the light first and go find the cause.

1040.intro: The Model 1040/XL is a feed-mixer batching indicator with a full alphanumeric keypad and twelve annunciators across the top of the display (Recipe, Ingredient, Alarm, Usage, Motion, Hand-Add, Gross, Load, Auto, Pen, lb, kg). Its menus are reached through the front panel keys, each behind its own password.
menus: The menus are accessed through the front panel keys. There are four of them, each behind its own password: Setup Menu (1040 password), Test Menu (111 password), History Menu (999 password) and Calibration Menu (01010101 password) (p.1).
Inside a menu, press MENU to step from item to item: in the Test menu, pressing MENU moves from VOLTS through LCD, KEYPAD, A/D, SERIAL, INPUTS, RELAY and SOFT (p.23).
Press SELECT to accept an entry: for CONFIG, after the number is established you simply enter it, and you must press SELECT. An invalid number shows CAN't and returns to CONFIG (p.7).
Press the GROSS key to return to the Gross weighing mode when a menu procedure is finished (pp.19, 23, 32).

keys.does: Press the GROSS key to return to the Gross weighing mode at the end of menu procedures (pp.19, 23, 32).

Press SELECT to accept what you have entered. For the CONFIG configuration number, you must press SELECT after entering the number; an invalid number shows CAN't and returns to CONFIG (p.7). SELECT also steps into test items such as the keypad test (p.23).
Press MENU to step from item to item inside a menu — in the Test menu, pressing MENU moves from VOLTS on through LCD, SERIAL, INPUTS, RELAY and SOFT (p.23).
The ZERO key is part of the Zero Clear function listed in the operational keys (p.1), and the keypad test shows ZERO as the display name for this key (p.23).
The CLEAR key appears on the keypad with the other operating keys; the key functions list includes the Zero Clear function (p.1).

PRINT is one of the operational keys (p.1). The serial settings decide what printing sends: standard printouts, TDM delimited transfers, or broadcast data, configured under RS232.1 and RS232.2 in Setup (pp.1, 19).
HOLD is one of the operational keys (p.1). Two programmable TTL inputs can also be set to act as std, zero, menu, hold, or print (p.4).

RECIPE is one of the operational keys (p.1). In Recipe mode the ingredient name stops flashing at the NAME percentage set in Setup (p.12), and the serial output can transfer the same RECIPE information being displayed (p.19).
The LOAD/UNLOAD keys are in the operational keys list (p.1); LOAD and UNLOAD are the display names shown for them in the keypad test (p.23).
USAGE is one of the operational keys (p.1), and USAGE is the display name shown for it in the keypad test (p.23).
ON and OFF appear on the keypad with the operating keys (p.32 outline drawing).

lights.does: One of the twelve annunciators; lights when gross weight is being displayed, alongside the Gross mode returned to by the GROSS key (pp.1, 32).
One of the twelve annunciators (p.1); the Setup menu configures the motion window under STABLE, off to 10.0 divisions (p.1).
One of the twelve annunciators; the Setup menu's ALARM item sets the pre-alarm target value, in percent or weight (pp.1, 1).
One of the twelve annunciators; the serial output has a RECIPE layout that transfers the same information being displayed when the RECIPE mode is active (pp.1, 19).
One of the twelve annunciators; in Recipe mode the NAME setting controls the point where the ingredient name stops flashing (pp.1, 12).
One of the twelve annunciators; LOAD is also the display name the keypad test shows for the LOAD/UNLOAD key (pp.1, 23).
One of the twelve annunciators (p.1).

ideas.h: Passwords guard the doors
ideas.text: Setup (1040), Test (111), History (999) and Calibration (01010101 per the manual's menu list) each have their own password. The deeper the door, the longer the password — calibration sits behind the longest one.

ideas.h: One number sets up the whole scale
ideas.text: The CONFIG item takes a 4-5 digit configuration number that sets up the indicator for the type of Weigh Bar, capacity, increment, pre-alarm mode, units and auto hold/mix. Get that one number right and most of the setup follows from it.

ideas.h: The digit keys can trim the span
ideas.text: When adjusting span from the CONFIG screen, each press of 1, 2, 4 or 5 raises the weight one division and 6, 7, 9 or 0 lowers it (hold a key to move faster); 3 or 8 returns to the factory calibrated value.

ideas.h: The annunciators read the job state
ideas.text: Twelve annunciators across the top — Recipe, Ingredient, Alarm, Usage, Motion, Hand-Add, Gross, Load, Auto, Pen, lb and kg — tell you what mode the batch is in before you read the weight. Motion is the one that says do not trust it yet.

pre.short: The take-it key — after you key in a value like the CONFIG number, SELECT accepts it.
Steps from menu item to menu item once you are inside a menu.
Your way back out — returns to the Gross weighing mode when a procedure is done.
Works with the Zero Clear function on the weighing screen.
One of the operating keys; what it sends depends on the serial layout set in Setup.
One of the twelve annunciators across the top — the scale is moving, so do not trust the weight yet.

1080.intro: The 1080's display is ringed with annunciators — motion, center of zero, gross/net/tare, units and outputs — and its menus are worked with the same handful of keys: TARE and UNITS change things, F1 accepts, ZERO gets you out.
menus: Change settings with the UNITS and TARE keys, and press the F1 key to accept the desired setting once it is displayed (p.101). For values, scroll in a new value using the numeric entry procedure and press F1, or press F1 to accept the displayed choice (p.39).

In Enquire mode, use the TARE and/or UNITS keys to scroll through the items, press the PRINT key with an item displayed to open it, change it, and press F1 to accept. When all the items are set, press the SELECT key and the menu label is displayed again (p.57).

At the end of the Service menu, press the ZERO key to return to normal weighing mode. You will be prompted to save the changes you've made: press the ZERO key to abort any changes, or press F1 to accept them. buSY flashes on the display while the unit saves data (p.101).

keys.does: F1 is the accept key in the menus: use the UNITS and TARE keys to change the setting, and press the F1 key to accept the desired setting once it is displayed. At the end of the Service menu, press F1 to accept changes and return to normal operating mode (p.101).
Press the ZERO key to return to normal weighing mode. You will be prompted to save the changes you've made; press the ZERO key to abort any changes made and return to normal operating mode (p.101).
Use the TARE and UNITS keys to scroll through menu items and to change settings — for example, to toggle YES or no on the STABLE item (p.57), or to change a setting before F1 accepts it (p.101).

Use the UNITS and TARE keys to scroll through menu items and change settings, then press F1 to accept. In remote display Mode 3, the keys that work on the remote are TARE, SELECT, ZERO, PRINT and UNITS (p.45).
In the menus, pressing the PRINT key opens the item shown — for example with P-ft or POLL displayed in Enquire mode, press PRINT to get into the setting (p.57).
When all the items have been set correctly, press the SELECT key and the menu label (for example Enq) is displayed again — SELECT backs you out to the item's name (p.57).

lights.does: Lights during scale motion. Goes out when the scale is stable.
Lights when the weight on the scale is within the zero range.
Lights when gross weight is displayed.
Lights when net weight is displayed.
Lights when a tare weight is displayed.
Lights when a print format is sent through the serial port.
Lights when a preset tare is active.

Configurable to show the status of Network 1, Network 2 or SensorComm: Red means an error (check the error or ghost log), Green on SensorComm means a sensorcomm error and on a network means connected, Amber means the network is ready for a connection but none has been established (pp.14, 101).

ideas.h: F1 takes it, ZERO walks away
ideas.text: Inside the menus, F1 is the key that accepts what is on the display. At the end of a menu, ZERO asks the save question: press ZERO to abort the changes or F1 to accept them, and buSY flashes while the unit saves.

ideas.h: The truth is written around the edge
ideas.text: The annunciators around the edge of the display tell you what the number in the middle means — Gross or Net, Tare stored, motion, which unit. Read the edge first, then trust the digits.

ideas.h: Center of zero is the settled test
ideas.text: The center-of-zero window is ±1/4 or ±1/2 division. When the weight falls inside that window, the center-of-zero annunciator lights — that is the box telling you the scale is sitting still at zero.

ideas.h: One box can be another box's face
ideas.text: The 1080 can act as a remote display for another Evolution indicator in four modes: weight only, weight plus annunciators, plus working keys (Print, Zero, Tare), or all of it together. What the keys and lights do then is whatever the host indicator sends.

pre.short: The take-it key — after TARE or UNITS shows the setting you want, F1 accepts it.
Returns to normal weighing; at the save prompt it throws your changes away instead of saving.
Steps through menu items and changes settings (UNITS does the same job).
Steps through menu items and changes settings (TARE does the same job).
Opens the menu item shown on the display so you can change it.
Lit when the scale is inside the zero range — the settled sign.

120 Plus.name: 120 Plus
120 Plus.intro: The 120 Plus is a portable, battery-powered indicator with a backlit six-digit LCD and nine keys: Power/Zero, Tare, Preset Tare, Hold, Gross/Net, Units, Enter/Print, Clear, and a numeric keypad. The arrow symbols on the keys double as menu navigation in configuration mode.
menus: Enter configuration mode by pressing the setup switch in the back of the indicator (a recessed switch, pressed with a thin non-conductive object); the display reads CONFIG. This mode should only be used by a qualified technician, and the indicator should be sealed afterward.

Scroll with the 6 key until the menu you want appears (for calibration, CALIBR), then press the 8 key to navigate down to the parameter. The keys marked with up, down, left, and right symbols move you through the menus and pick digits.
To edit a numeric value, press Enter so the last digit blinks, press Clear to clear it, type the value with the numeric keys (0-9), and press Enter to save and return to the level above.

To leave configuration, press the 2 key until the display reads EXIT Y, then press Enter. Holding the setup switch for three seconds instead enters test mode (display changes from CONFIG to A/DTST) for diagnostics.

keys.does: Turns the indicator on or off. Its secondary use is the zero function: in gross mode, remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, and press it to zero the scale; the center of zero annunciator lights.
Acquires the weight on the scale as tare, so the display switches to net.
Short press recalls the preset tare data; long press enters a preset tare value into memory.
Activates the hold function; the HOLD annunciator shows while hold is active.
Toggles between gross weight and net weight displays.
Toggles through the user defined units; the lit unit annunciator (Lb, Oz, Kg, t, or g) shows the units of the displayed value.
Press to print. In configuration and panel modes the enter symbol on this key makes it the confirm key: it opens a numeric value for editing and saves it.
Clears the value, except in normal weighing mode. When editing, press Enter, then Clear, then type the new value with the numeric keys.
The 0-9 keys type values and, with the arrow-symbol keys (2, 4, 6, 8), navigate menus, select digits within numeric values, and increment or decrement values.

lights.does: The icon indicates the level of the rechargeable battery — important on an indicator meant to work anywhere.
The 1 and 2 icons indicate the status of set point 1 and set point 2.
The NET icon is shown if the displayed weight is the net weight; otherwise the display is gross.
The 0 icon is shown if the gross weight is within 0.25 graduation of zero.
Shows the scale is at a standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including tare and printing, can be done only when the standstill symbol is displayed.
The HOLD icon indicates that hold is active.
The Lb, Oz, Kg, t, and g icons indicate the units of the displayed value: pound, ounce, kilogram, tons, and gram.

ideas.h: The setup switch is a deliberate act
ideas.text: Configuration and calibration hide behind a recessed switch on the back that takes a thin object to press. That is by design: changing how the indicator weighs should never be an accidental key press, and the book says the indicator should be sealed after initial configuration.

ideas.h: Standstill first, then tare or print
ideas.text: Tare and printing only work while the standstill icon is displayed. The indicator will not freeze a moving weight, so if a key seems ignored, the scale probably has not settled yet.

ideas.h: Preset tare remembers the container
ideas.text: A short press of Preset Tare recalls a stored tare; a long press stores one. For a container you use every day, that means net weight without weighing the empty container each time.

ideas.h: Remote switches are pocket copies of the keys
ideas.text: External push buttons wired to the remote switch inputs can be given the same jobs as the front panel keys — Zero, Tare, Print/Enter, Units — so a scale can be run from a button at the platform instead of at the indicator.

pre.short: The confirm key in setup: opens a value for editing and saves it; prints in weigh mode.
Zeroes the scale once the standstill icon shows; also the power key.
Acquires the weight on the scale as tare and switches to net.
Clears a value while editing so you can type the new one.
Type values digit by digit after Enter makes the last digit blink.
Tare and print only work while this shows — let the scale settle first.

120.intro: The 120 has a large six-digit LED display and a five-button keypad: ZERO, TARE, GROSS/NET, UNITS, and PRINT. In setup mode those same five keys turn into directional arrows, printed under each key, for walking the menus.
menus: Put the indicator in setup mode and the display reads CONFIG. Four front panel keys become directional keys: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, while ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down to different menu levels. The TARE key serves as the Enter key.

To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group you want appears (CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, P FORMT, TIME, DATE, VERSION), then move down to the submenu or parameter. The default or previously selected value appears first.

To change a value, scroll left or right to view the choices and press Enter (TARE) to select it and move back up one level. You must press Enter to save — the 120 does not automatically save the last-displayed value.
To edit a numeric value, press Enter so the rightmost digit flashes, use the navigation keys to pick the digit and raise or lower it, then press Enter again to save the edited value.

keys.does: In gross mode, with all weight removed and the standstill annunciator shown, press ZERO to zero the scale; the center of zero annunciator lights. In setup mode it is the up/down navigation key, and in test mode it exits to normal operation.
Press TARE to acquire the tare weight of the container; the indicator switches to net mode. In setup mode TARE is the Enter key used to select parameter values and save edits.

Press the GROSS/NET key (labeled B/N) to switch the display from gross to net or back. If a tare has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. In setup mode it moves between menu levels.
Press UNITS to switch between primary and secondary units; the units LED to the right of the display is lit. In setup mode it scrolls left and right on the same menu level.
Requests a print of the displayed weight. In setup mode it scrolls left and right together with UNITS.

lights.does: The Gr annunciator is lit to show the displayed weight is a gross weight.
The Nt annunciator is lit to show the displayed weight is a net weight (gross minus tare).
Lights when gross weight is within ±0.25 graduations of zero — the scale is truly zeroed.
Shows the scale is at standstill or within the motion band. Some operations, including tare functions and printing, can only be done when the standstill symbol is shown.
Unit annunciator for pounds; also used as the primary units annunciator when the configured units have no LED of their own.
Unit annunciator for kilograms; also used as the secondary units annunciator for combinations like short tons.
Unit annunciator for ounces.
Unit annunciator for grams.

ideas.h: Nothing happens until the scale stands still
ideas.text: The standstill annunciator is the gatekeeper: tare and printing only work while it is shown. That is the indicator refusing to capture a weight that is still moving, so the number it freezes is one you can trust.

ideas.h: Enter means save — nothing saves itself
ideas.text: Scrolling to a new value only shows it. The 120 does not automatically save the last-displayed value; you must press Enter (the TARE key) or your change is lost when you leave the menu.

ideas.h: Gross and net are the same weight, two ways of looking
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale. Once a tare is acquired, net is gross minus the container. The Gr and Nt annunciators always tell you which one is on the display, and GROSS/NET flips between them without changing anything on the scale.

ideas.h: Unit lights sometimes stand in for other units
ideas.text: There are only lb, kg, oz, and g lamps, so for unit pairs like pounds and short tons the lb lamp means primary units and the kg lamp means secondary. The lit lamp shows which of the two configured units you are viewing, even when the lamp's own label is borrowed.

pre.short: In setup this is the Enter key — press it to select and save, or the change is lost.
Zeroes the scale in gross mode; moves between menu levels in setup.
Flips between gross and net; moves between menu levels in setup.
Switches units in weigh mode; scrolls left/right through menus in setup.
Prints the weight; scrolls left/right through menus in setup.
Must be shown before tare or print will work — wait for the scale to settle.

1280.intro: The 1280 is a color touchscreen indicator. Its Zero, Tare, Gross/Net, Print, Units and Diagnostics work from a virtual keypad on the screen the same as the physical keys on the keyed front panel, and configurable softkeys are displayed as digital buttons at the bottom of the display in weigh mode (pp.15, 83).
menus: Use the main menu to get around: for example, navigation softkey designations are entered by navigating to the main menu and selecting Configuration/Features/Softkeys (p.17). To enter the Softkey menu itself, press the menu control and select Softkeys (p.83).
When a setting needs data entry, a keyboard or numeric keypad displays on the screen. Cancel exits the keyboard without taking the entry; Done completes the entry (p.12).

While typing, Clear deletes everything in the prompt line, and the backspace deletes one character at a time (p.12). The front panel also has a numeric keypad for entering numbers or keyed tares (p.17).

Softkeys are digital buttons at the bottom of the display in weigh mode; press a softkey to use its assigned function. When Auto-Populate Softkeys is on, the default or last set softkeys display (p.83).
Navigation keys are primarily linked to iRite handlers; if no iRite handlers exist, the navigation keys toggle through a selection of displayed scales (p.17).

keys.does: Zeros the indicator. On the virtual keypad, Zero functions the same as the physical Zero key on the front panel of the keyed 1280.
Tares the scale using the on-screen numeric keypad. Keyed Tare is the equivalent of the keyed tare softkey: press it and a numeric keypad displays to enter a tare value.
Toggles the display mode between gross and net. If a tared value is in the system, Net is displayed (net equals gross minus tare); if there is no tare in the system, Gross is displayed.
Toggles between primary, secondary and tertiary units. The Units softkey is functionally equivalent to the keypad Units key.
Prints the configured print format. The Print softkey is functionally equivalent to the keypad Print key.
Saves entries made from the numeric keypad. In the on-screen keyboard, Done completes the entry and Cancel exits without it.

Configurable on-screen buttons at the bottom of the display that provide additional operator functions, such as Time/Date, Display Tare, Display Accumulator, Setpoint, Batch Start/Stop/Pause/Reset, Diagnostics, and Alibi. Up to 10 softkeys can be created using the user defined options.

lights.does: One of the status annunciators shown in the on-screen scale widget, which is the Legal for Trade representation of the configured scale.
Shown in the on-screen scale widget along with the Center-of-Zero, Tare and Units annunciators, as part of the Legal for Trade representation of the scale.
Shown in the on-screen scale widget to give the status of the scale along with the Center-of-Zero, Standstill and Units annunciators.
Shown in the on-screen scale widget with the Center-of-Zero, Standstill and Tare annunciators to represent the configured scale's status.

ideas.h: The screen keys are the real keys
ideas.text: The 1280's virtual keypad is not a picture of a keypad: its Zero, Tare, Gross/Net, Print, Units and Diagnostics function the same as the physical keys on the front panel of the keyed 1280. The Zero, Gross/Net, Tare, Units and Print softkeys are also functionally equivalent to the keypad function keys, which is what lets key-less panel mounts and web browser remote connections work the scale.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: The display shows Net when a tared value is in the system, and net equals gross minus tare. When there is no tare in the system, the display shows Gross instead, so the mode on the screen is itself telling you whether a tare is active.

ideas.h: Softkeys are built for the job
ideas.text: Softkeys are configured to provide additional operator functions for specific applications, and up to 10 can be created with the user defined options. That means two 1280s on different jobs can legitimately have different buttons at the bottom of the same screen.

ideas.h: The scale widget carries the legal status marks
ideas.text: Scale widgets on the 1280 display are Legal for Trade representations of the configured scales and include the Center-of-Zero, Standstill, Tare and Units annunciators. Those marks travel with the weight display on screen, so the operator reads scale status from the same widget that shows the weight.

185 Rival.name: 185 Rival
185 Rival.intro: The 185 and 185B Weight Indicators (Rival) use a 7-key keypad, and calibration is accomplished entirely by the keypad. The 185B adds battery operation, with a battery status indicator on the display.
menus: Getting in: setup and calibration are entered by the keypad, but the door is a jumper — with the rear panel removed and the indicator ON, remove the calibration jumper J3 (CAL) on the main printed circuit board. Refer to Figure No. 13 for the jumper location.

Moving and entering: when a prompt for a value is displayed, press the TARE (Enter) key to display the current setting; pressing it again keeps the data and advances to the next prompt. The functions of numeric keys are replaced by using the UNITS/(Left Arrow) and the Fn/(Up Arrow) keys: the cursor is the blinking character, UNITS/(Left Arrow) advances it to the left, and Fn/(Up Arrow) changes the blinking character to the next value or toggles between the available values.
Backing up: pressing the Fn/(Up Arrow) key when a setup parameter (not a parameter value) is displayed will back up to the previous prompt.

In calibration: with the CAL prompt displayed, press TARE (Enter); at the first calibration weight use the UNITS and Fn keys to set the display to the weight on the platform, make sure the platform is stable, and press TARE (Enter). For the Fine Span Adjustment, the FINE SPAN annunciator turns on, Fn/(Up Arrow) increases the displayed weight, UNITS/(Left Arrow) decreases it, and TARE returns to the CAL prompt.
Just looking: the Fn key's other uses open the look-around features — Piece Count, Setup Review, and the millivolts display (a diagnostic that shows the millivolts reading at the load cell input).

keys.does: Pressing this key when the indicator is off will apply power to the indicator. Pressing this key when the indicator is on will turn the indicator off.

Performs a zero-load adjustment. The adjustment will not take place unless the weight display is stable. There is a setup option to limit the amount of adjustment to plus or minus two percent of scale capacity.

Sets the tare weight to the current gross weight; the display indication will switch to net weight display mode if the tare weight is not zero, and the weight display must be stable for the operation to occur. In setup it is also the Enter key: it displays the current setting and retains the data while advancing to the next prompt.
If the tare weight is greater than zero, pressing this key toggles between the gross and net weight display modes.
If more than one weighing unit was selected in setup, pressing this key toggles between the selected weighing units. During setup it advances the blinking cursor to the left to the next position.

If the tare weight is greater than zero, pressing this key followed by the TARE key will briefly display the tare weight. It is also the door to the Piece Count, Setup Review, and Display Millivolts features. In setup it changes the blinking character to the next value, toggles between the available values, and backs up to the previous prompt at a parameter.

If continuous serial output was not selected in setup, pressing this key initiates the transmission of ASCII data via the serial port. The indicator will not respond to the print command unless the weight display is stable. If gross weight is being displayed only gross will print; if net is displayed, the gross, tare, and net weights will be printed.

lights.does: The annunciator to the right of the weight display shows the displayed weight unit: lb pounds, oz ounces, kg kilograms, or g grams.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale, tare is the stored container weight, and net is gross less tare. The GROSS, NET, and TARE lights tell you which number you are seeing — and NET/GROSS only toggles when a tare weight greater than zero exists.

ideas.h: The jumper is the seal
ideas.text: There is no calibration switch on the back of the 185. Setup begins when the calibration jumper J3 is removed and re-installed while the indicator is on, with the rear panel already removed — opening the case is part of what makes the seal meaningful.

ideas.h: Batteries report themselves
ideas.text: On the Model 185B, the battery status indicator shows the level of charge in bars (4 bars is 100%). The bars scroll while the AC adapter is charging the batteries, and as the battery approaches full discharge, the outline of the battery starts to flash.

ideas.h: Millivolts: the raw signal
ideas.text: As a diagnostic function, the 185 can display the millivolts reading at the load cell input — the raw electrical signal before it becomes a weight number. If the displayed weight is wrong, the millivolt view separates a bad signal from a bad conversion.

ideas.h: Stable first, then it listens
ideas.text: ZERO and TARE both refuse to act unless the weight display is stable, and PRINT will not respond either. The STABLE annunciator is the indicator's way of saying the number can be trusted.

190.intro: The 190 uses a 7-key capacitive touch keypad that requires a finger touch to function — pens, pencils, and tools will not operate it. The Fn/▲ key is the first half of most two-key features, and the display adds checkweigher arrows and a battery gauge on battery models.
menus: Getting in: calibration and setup are accomplished entirely by the keypad, with no switch to press. Note that sealed parameters cannot be changed with the calibration inhibit jumper J4 installed on the main board, so know which sealing method your job uses before you start.

Moving and entering: there are no number keys. Pressing TARE shows the current setting of a parameter; pressing it a second time (after a change) signals the entry is complete and the indicator processes it. During entry, UNITS/◀ advances the blinking cursor left to the next position, and Fn/▲ changes the blinking character to the next value or toggles between the available settings.
Backing up: pressing Fn/▲ when a setup parameter (not a parameter value or setting) is displayed backs up to the previous parameter prompt.
Getting out: to exit Setup, press the Fn/▲ key with any of the menu selections displayed.
Just looking: the 190 allows several operational parameters to be reviewed and changed without breaking the calibration seal. Press Fn/▲, then ZERO to enter the Review mode of Setup and Calibration.

keys.does: Used to turn the scale on and off. Press it when the scale is off to turn it ON — the indicator performs a display test (all segments on), then shows the model number and software version. If the scale is already on, press and hold it for 2 to 3 seconds; when OFF is displayed, release the key to turn the scale off.

Zeroes the weight display, up to the selected limit of 4% or 100% of the scale's capacity chosen during setup. The indicator will not respond unless the weight display is stable. It also clears what is showing in special displays: a tare value back to Gross, the peak weight, or the gross or net accumulator.

During normal operation it stores the current gross weight as the new tare weight; the display changes to net weight and the Net annunciator turns on. During setup it displays the current setting of the parameter, and pressed a second time after changing values it signals the entry is complete so the indicator processes the data.

Toggles between the Gross and Net weight modes; the appropriate annunciator shows the selected mode. If no valid tare weight has been entered, it causes a momentary "notArE" error and the indicator remains in Gross mode. When in Hold, Count, Peak weight, Live weight, or Accumulator display mode, it returns the display to normal weight display.

In normal operation it selects the units in which the weight is to be displayed (from the units selected in setup: pounds, ounces, kilograms, grams). During setup it advances the cursor left to the next position when inputting setup parameters.

During setup it backs up to the previous parameter prompt at a parameter, and toggles between the different available values or settings at a value. In normal operation it is used with the other keys to access additional features, and alone it selects enabled functions such as Hold, Count, Peak Hold, Checkweigher, and Live Weight.

Pressing PRINT during a weighing operation adds the displayed Gross weight, or Net weight, to the associated accumulator and sends the print data to the serial interface. The indicator will not respond to the PRINT key unless the weight display is stable.

Signals that the displayed weight is equal to or greater than the minimum value of overweight used in the Checkweigher feature. Also indicates preset 3 is active.

lights.does: The lit annunciator to the right of the weight display shows the displayed weight unit: lb pounds, oz ounces, kg kilograms, or g grams.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale, tare is the stored container weight, and net is gross less tare. The NET, GROSS, and TARE lights tell you which number you are seeing, and NET/GROSS refuses to show net — flashing "notArE" — when no tare has been stored.

ideas.h: One big function at a time
ideas.text: Hold, Count, Peak Hold, Checkweigher, and Live Weight share a single slot: only one of them can be active at a time. Hold, Count, and Live Weight cannot be enabled at all when Legal-For-Trade was selected in setup.

ideas.h: The checkweigher talks in lights and colors
ideas.text: With the Checkweigher function enabled, the 190 compares the displayed weight with the preset values and reports UNDER, ACCEPT, or OVER on the arrows — and the display backlight changes to the color selected for that result.

ideas.h: The seal is a jumper
ideas.text: The calibration inhibit jumper J4 on the main board is the padlock on the sealed settings. With the jumper installed, parameters such as capacity, weighing units, interval, and Legal-For-Trade cannot be changed at all.

ideas.h: Touch keys want a finger
ideas.text: The keypad is capacitive touch: it requires a finger touch and will not operate with pens, pencils, or tools. Pressing too firmly during the setup entry method may even prevent the unit from entering Setup.

200 Panel Mount.name: 200 Panel Mount
200 Panel Mount.intro: The 200 Panel Mount is equipped with a 7-key keypad (color-coded membrane, 6-digit LED display) used to enter commands and data into the indicator. The ASTERISK key teams up with the other keys to open extra features.
menus: Getting in: the calibration switch is located on the enclosure rear panel, behind the calibration switch access cover (remove the 2 screws securing the cover). To enter the setup mode, with the indicator ON, insert a small screwdriver or other tool through the access hole, press and release the calibration switch, and the SETUP menu will be displayed. Continue to press and release the switch to rotate through the beginning point for entering the setup mode.

Moving and entering: pressing the TARE/ENTER key will cause the data entered or displayed to be retained and the indicator to advance to the next prompt. The functions of numeric keys are replaced by using the UNITS/LEFT ARROW and the ASTERISK/UP ARROW keys: the cursor location is identified by the blinking character, UNITS/LEFT ARROW advances it to the next position at the left, and ASTERISK/UP ARROW changes the blinking character to the next value or toggles between the available values.

Backing up and skipping: pressing the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key when a setup parameter (not a parameter value) is displayed will back up to the previous prompt. Pressing the calibration switch at any prompt will return you to the SETUP menu, and pressing TARE/ENTER twice at a section prompt skips that section.

Getting out: to exit setup, press the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key with any of the menu selections displayed, or cycle power at any time (press the ON/OFF key twice). Setup may be interrupted at any time — all data previously entered and finalized with the TARE/ENTER key will be retained in the nonvolatile memory.

Just looking: pressing the ASTERISK key before the ZERO KEY/REVIEW key enters the Review mode of Setup and Calibration, and ASTERISK before the UNITS/TEST key enters the Test mode — settings can be reviewed without the calibration switch.

keys.does: This key performs two functions. Pressing it when the indicator is off will apply power to the indicator. If the indicator is already on, pressing this key will turn the indicator off.

Pressing this key will cause an immediate zeroing of the weight display up to the selected limit of 4% or 100% of the scale's capacity (selected during setup and calibration). The indicator will not respond to this command unless the weight display is stable. Pressing the ASTERISK key before this key enters the Review mode of Setup and Calibration.

Pressing the TARE key alone will store the current gross weight as the new tare weight and the weight display will change to the net weight display mode (Net annunciator will turn on). Pressing ASTERISK before it displays the current setting when reviewing parameters, and it signals completion of the entry of data so the indicator processes the data entered.

Used to toggle between the Net and Gross weight modes; the selected mode is indicated by turning on the appropriate annunciator on the display. If no valid tare weight has been entered, pressing this key will cause a momentary "noTArE" display error and the indicator will remain in the Gross weight mode.

In normal operation it is used to select the units in which the weight is to be displayed (tons, pounds only, pound-ounces, ounces only, Tonnes, kilograms, and grams selected in setup). During setup it advances the cursor left to the next position when inputting setup parameters. Pressing the ASTERISK key before this key enters the Test mode.

During setup, when a setup parameter (not a parameter value) is displayed, pressing this key will back up to the previous prompt; when a parameter value is displayed, it will toggle between the different available values. In normal operation it combines with the other keys: with ZERO for Review mode, with TARE to display the tare weight for three (3) seconds, with NET/GROSS for the accumulators, and with PRINT to change the print ticket format.

Pressing this key will add the displayed gross or net weight to the associated accumulator and initiate the transmission of weight and other data via the selected printer output port, unless the continuous data feature of this port was enabled. The indicator will not respond to this command unless the weight display is stable. If displaying gross weight, the only weight printed is gross; if displaying net weight, the gross, tare, and net weights will print.

Turned on when the weight display is stable. When off, it means that the change in successive weight samples is greater than the motion limits selected during setup.
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the net weight (gross weight less tare weight).
Turned on to show that gross weight is displayed. Gross weight will be displayed when no tare weight is stored.
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the tare weight.

lights.does: The lit annunciator shows the displayed weight unit: lb pounds and kg kilograms to the left of the weight display; T tons, oz ounces, t Tonnes (metric tons), and g grams to the right of the display.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale, tare is the stored container weight, and net is gross less tare. The NET, GROSS, and TARE annunciators tell you which number is on the display, and gross is what you get whenever no tare weight is stored.

ideas.h: The seal is a two-screw cover
ideas.text: On this panel-mount box, the calibration switch lives on the rear panel behind a small access cover held by two screws. That covered switch is the physical gate between normal weighing and setup and calibration.

ideas.h: High-resolution mode is the magnifier
ideas.text: The Display High Resolution Weight mode shows the active weight in 1/10 intervals — the fine view used with Fine Span Adjustment, where the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key increases the span and the UNITS/LEFT ARROW key decreases it. You can even print from it, and the ticket is followed by the text TEST.

ideas.h: Nudge the span instead of recalibrating
ideas.text: Fine Span Adjustment lets you trim the span against a calibrated test weight with two arrow keys instead of redoing the whole calibration: place the test weight, raise or lower the displayed amount until it matches, and TARE/ENTER exits back to the SETUP menu.

ideas.h: Stable is the gatekeeper
ideas.text: PRINT will not respond unless the weight display is stable, and ZERO/REVIEW ignores the command on an unstable display. The STABLE annunciator is the machine's way of saying the number can be trusted.

Prints and adds the weight to the accumulator — only when stable.

204.intro: The 204 is the battery-powered member of this family, set up and calibrated entirely by the keypad. In setup, the PRINT key does the saving, and the ASTERISK key can lock a stable reading on the display.
menus: Getting in: calibration of the 204 indicator is accomplished entirely by the keypad. Follow the setup and calibration sequence in the book to reach the prompts, starting with the scale interval (int=).

Moving and saving: during the setup and calibration process it will be necessary to enter operational parameters via the 204's keyboard. Pressing the PRINT key will cause the data entered or displayed to be retained and the 204 will advance to the next prompt. The cursor location is identified by the blinking character and can be advanced to the left to the next position by pressing the ASTERISK key. Pressing the UNITS key will change the blinking character to the next value.

Typing a number: for values like scale capacity (CAP=), press the ASTERISK key to show the current setting, press UNITS to enter the proper digit at the blinking location, press the ASTERISK key to step to the left and the next digit location, and repeat until all digits have been entered; then press the PRINT key to store the value and proceed to the next step.

Review without calibration: the 204 allows several operational parameters to be reviewed and changed as necessary without having to enter the setup and calibration mode (battery charging, power-up zero, automatic shutoff, sleep mode, baud rate, print format, continuous output, end-of-print line feeds). Several setup settings also carry the note that they may be revised without having to enter the calibration mode.
Done: when the indicator display shows dOnE, the setup and calibration process has been completed. Remove the power from the indicator and re-assemble for use.

keys.does: Turns the indicator on and off. When the 204 is to be turned off while connected to the AC adapter for charging, pressing the ON/OFF key once displays dashes scrolling across the display (batteries charging); pressing it again displays OFF and turns the 204 off.

Pressing the TARE key alone will cause the current gross weight to be stored as the new tare weight and cause the weight display to change to the net weight display mode (Net annunciator will turn on).

This key is used to toggle between Net and Gross weight modes; the selected mode is indicated by turning on the appropriate annunciator on the display. Note that if no valid tare weight has been entered, pressing this key will cause a momentary display noTArE and the indicator will remain in the Gross weight mode.

This key is used to change the weighing units to the alternate units of measurement if selected during setup of the indicator (for example, with pounds displayed pressing this key will change the weighing units to kilograms). This feature must be enabled during setup and calibration for this key to be operational. It is also used during setup and calibration to increment the value.

This key is used to lock and unlock the display. If enabled during setup and calibration (Hold Key Enable), pressing this key after obtaining a stable weight value will cause the indicator to lock onto the weight and turn on the asterisk annunciator; pressing it a second time will unlock the display. It is also used during setup and calibration to select the digit to change. Note the lock feature is for non-commercial (not Legal for Trade) applications.

Pressing this key will initiate the transmission of weight data via the serial I/O port, unless the continuous data output feature was enabled (in which case this key is disabled). The indicator will not respond to the Print command unless the weight display is stable: if displaying gross weight, the only weight printed is gross weight; if displaying net weight, the gross, tare, and net weights are printed. This key is also used to save the current setting during setup and calibration.

lights.does: Located to the right of the weight display; turned on to indicate that the weight is within +/- 1/4 division of the center of zero.

Located to the right of the weight display; turned on when the weight display is stable. When off, it means that the change in successive weight samples is greater than the motion limits selected during setup and calibration of the indicator.

Turned on to show that the weight displayed is the net weight. Net weight is determined by subtracting the stored tare weight from the gross weight; the NET annunciator is only active when a tare weight value is stored.
Turned on to show that the weight displayed is the gross weight. Gross weight will be displayed when no tare weight value is stored.
Turned on to show that the indicator is in a weight mode in which a known tare (container) weight value is stored.
Turned on to show that the indicator is locked onto the weight (display hold). The lock feature (Hold Key Enable) must be enabled during setup and calibration.

Used with battery operation; it will turn ON to indicate that the batteries will soon need to be replaced (if using Alkaline) or recharged (if using NiCad or NiMH). If the battery voltage drops too low for accurate weighing, the indicator will automatically turn itself off.

lights.key: Unit lights: lb, kg, oz, g
lights.does: The lit annunciator on the right of the weight display shows the displayed weight units: lb pounds, kg kilograms, oz ounces, or g grams.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Net weight is determined by subtracting the stored tare weight from the gross weight, where the tare weight is usually the weight of the empty container. The NET annunciator is only active when a tare weight value is stored; otherwise the display is gross.

ideas.h: Lock is a photograph, not a weighing
ideas.text: The ASTERISK lock lets the indicator hold onto a stable weight value and freeze it on the display (asterisk annunciator on) until the key is pressed again. The book is clear the lock feature is for non-commercial applications only — it must be set to disabled for Legal for Trade.

ideas.h: Two battery kinds, two rules
ideas.text: Alkaline batteries get replaced; NiCad or NiMH batteries get recharged (about 15 hours on the AC adapter, and the 204 can still be operated while charging). The niCAd= setting tells the indicator which kind is installed — the book warns: do not select charging when using Alkaline batteries.

ideas.h: The scale sleeps to save itself
ideas.text: Automatic Shutoff turns the 204 off after a predetermined period of inactivity to prolong battery life. Sleep Mode instead reduces the load cell excitation while the indicator remains at center of zero (showing SLEEP), and weight placed on the scale will activate the indicator and return it to the weight mode.

ideas.h: The percentage on power-up
ideas.text: If batteries are used, the indicator shows the battery status on power up: the display shows "battry" then the remaining battery voltage expressed as a percentage of the total battery voltage. The low battery annunciator is the early warning before the voltage drops low enough to affect operation.

Stores the container weight so the display shows net.
Changes the blinking digit or setting to the next value.

Powers the indicator; with the adapter connected it also controls the charging display.

205.intro: The 205 has a 7-key keypad used to enter commands and data into the indicator. Many keys do two jobs, and the * key teams up with the other keys to open extra features.
menus: Getting in: setup is opened with the calibration switch behind the calibration switch access screw on the rear panel. With the indicator ON, press and release the switch and the SETUP menu shows; keep pressing and releasing it to rotate through the beginning point for each section (Setup, Analog to Digital Filtering, Calibration, Serial Input/Output, Print Tab Settings, Fine Span, and more).

Moving and entering: TARE/ENTER keeps the data entered or displayed and advances to the next prompt. There are no number keys — the blinking character is the cursor. UNITS/LEFT ARROW advances the cursor left to the next position, and */UP ARROW changes the blinking character to the next value, or toggles between the available values of a setting.

Backing up and skipping: pressing */UP ARROW when a setup parameter (not a value) is displayed backs up to the previous prompt. At a section prompt, pressing TARE/ENTER twice skips that section and advances to the next menu selection.

Getting out: pressing the calibration switch at any prompt returns you to the SETUP menu. To exit setup, press */UP ARROW with any of the menu selections displayed, or cycle power (press ON/OFF twice) at any time. Setup may be interrupted at any time — everything finalized with TARE/ENTER is retained in nonvolatile memory.

Just looking: Setup Review lets several operational parameters be reviewed and changed without breaking the calibration seal (power-up zero, sleep mode, serial setup, print tabs, and more). Press * then ZERO/REVIEW to get in.

keys.does: This key performs two functions. Pressing it when the indicator is off will apply power to the indicator. If the indicator is already on, pressing this key will turn the indicator off.

In normal operation, pressing this key zeroes the weight display immediately, up to the limit selected during setup — 4% or 100% of the scale's capacity. Pressing this key after the * key enters the Review mode of Setup and Calibration.

Pressed alone, it stores the current gross weight as a new tare weight and the display changes to net weight mode (NET annunciator turns on). It is also the enter key: when reviewing setup parameters it displays the current setting, and it signals the completion of data entry so the indicator processes the data entered.

Toggles between Net and Gross weight modes; the selected mode is shown by the appropriate annunciator. If no valid tare weight has been entered, pressing it causes a momentary "notArE" display error and the indicator remains in Gross mode.

In normal operation it selects the units in which the weight is displayed (the units selected in setup). During setup it advances the cursor left to the next position. Pressing the * key before this key enters the Test mode.

During setup, at a parameter it backs up to the previous prompt; at a value it toggles between the available values. In normal operation it is the first half of two-key features: *+ZERO/REVIEW enters Review, *+TARE shows the tare weight for 3 seconds, *+UNITS enters Test mode, and *+PRINT changes the print ticket format.

Prints the displayed weight through the selected printer output port — in high-resolution mode the printout is followed by the text TEST. If motion is present when a print is attempted (an Unstable error), wait for the STABLE annunciator before printing.

lights.does: On when the weight display is stable; the troubleshooting section calls for waiting for the STABLE annunciator before performing a print operation. Off means the change in successive weight samples is greater than the motion limits selected during setup.
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the net weight (gross weight less tare weight).
Turned on to show that gross weight is displayed. Gross weight will be displayed when no tare weight is stored.
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the tare weight.

lights.key: Unit lights: lb, kg, oz, tn, t, g
lights.does: The lit unit annunciator shows the displayed weight unit: lb pounds and kg kilograms to the left of the display; oz ounces, tn tons, t tonnes (metric tons), and g grams to the right of the display.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale. Tare is the container's weight, stored with the TARE key. Net is what is left — gross less tare. The NET, GROSS, and TARE lights tell you which of the three numbers you are looking at, and with no tare stored the display can only be gross.

ideas.h: Zero has a limit
ideas.text: The ZERO key does not swing the whole scale back to zero. Setup picks whether it may take up to 4% or all 100% of capacity. That limit keeps a loaded scale from being zeroed away by one careless press.

ideas.h: Look without breaking the seal
ideas.text: Setup Review lets you review and change everyday operating parameters — power-up zero, sleep mode, serial configuration, print tab settings — without breaking the calibration seal. The sealed calibration itself stays behind the calibration switch.

ideas.h: The C numbers are the fingerprint
ideas.text: The calibration numbers C1 to C4 are the stored record of the last calibration. The Test mode even displays them, so today's numbers can be compared against the recorded ones to prove the calibration has not changed.

ideas.h: High-resolution mode is the magnifier
ideas.text: Display High Resolution Weight shows the active weight in 1/10 intervals — the fine view used to watch small changes while adjusting span. There, the */UP ARROW key increases the span and the UNITS/LEFT ARROW key decreases it.

pre.short: The take-it key — keeps what you entered and moves to the next prompt; alone, it stores a tare.
Backs up one prompt and changes the blinking value — the adjust and get-out key in setup.
Moves the blinking cursor left while you type a value; in fine span it lowers the span.
Zeroes the empty scale, up to the 4% or 100% limit picked in setup.
Prints the weight — only when the STABLE light is on.
On when the weight is steady. Do not print or trust a reading until it is lit.

220.intro: The 220 adds batching and identification to the indicator panel: membrane keys that also type letters, eight preset weight comparators, ID storage, and fill and batch operations. The ASTERISK key is the door to its extra features.
menus: Getting in: to enter the setup mode, with the indicator ON, insert a small screwdriver or other tool through the calibration switch access hole on the rear panel and press and release the calibration switch. The menu SETUP will be displayed; continue to press and release (or hold) the switch to rotate through the beginning point for each section (SETUP, ANALOG, CALIBRATE, SERIAL, PRINT TABS, FINE SPAN, HIGH RES, KEY LOCK OUT).

Moving and entering: pressing the ENTER key without entering a new value will retain the current setting and advance the 220 to the next prompt. To change a setting, enter a new value with the numeric keys and press ENTER — this saves the new value and advances to the next prompt. The 1 and 0 keys also answer prompts: 1 = YES, 0 = NO.
Backing up: pressing the ASTERISK key will back up to the previous prompt, or return to normal operation. Pressing it during entry of data toggles the keypad to the alpha mode for entering letters.
Getting out of review: to exit Setup Review, press the ENTER key to step through the remaining prompts, or at any prompt cycle the power (press the ON/OFF key twice).

Just looking: ASTERISK then ZERO/REVIEW enters the Review mode of Setup and Calibration, and ASTERISK then UNITS enters the Test mode used to test all the display elements — no calibration switch required.

keys.does: Pressing this key when the indicator is off will apply power to the instrument; if the indicator is already on, pressing it turns it off. In the alphanumeric mode it is used to enter the letter K.

In normal operation it zeroes the weight display immediately, up to the selected limit of 4% or 100% of scale capacity made during setup. Pressing this key after the ASTERISK key enters the Review mode of Setup and Calibration.

A dual function key. Pressed alone (Pushbutton Tare) it stores the current gross weight as the new tare weight and the display changes to net weight mode (Net annunciator on). Pressed after entering a numeric value (Keypad Tare) the entered value is accepted as the new tare. Tare weights equal to or greater than scale capacity cannot be entered, and the division value must match the scale division value.
Pressing this key displays the current tare weight for three seconds.

Toggles between the Net and Gross weight modes; the selected mode is indicated by the appropriate annunciator. If no valid tare weight has been entered, pressing it causes a momentary NO TARE display error and the indicator remains in Gross mode.

In normal operation it selects the units in which the weight is displayed (the combinations enabled in setup). Pressing it after the ASTERISK key enters the Test mode, used to conduct a test of all display elements.

During setup, at a parameter it backs up to the previous prompt; during data entry it toggles the keypad to alpha mode. In normal operation it works with the other keys: with ZERO/REVIEW for Review mode, with NET/GROSS for the accumulators (again for Gross), with UNITS for Test mode, and with PRINT to change the print ticket format.

Used to enter numeric data during setup and calibration and during normal operation. The 1 and 0 keys have dual functions: they enter numeric data and also answer yes (1 = YES) or no (0 = NO) to various prompts. In alphanumeric mode they enter letters.
Saves the value you entered (or keeps the current setting if nothing was entered) and advances to the next prompt. In the fill and batching operations it answers START=YES to begin the operation.

Adds the displayed gross or net weight or piece count to the associated accumulator and transmits the weight and other data selected in the Print menu to the selected printer output port. The indicator will not respond to the Print command unless the weight display is stable. If displaying gross weight only gross prints; in net weight, the gross, tare, and net weights are printed.

Enters the preset weight comparator values (and trim values). With the indicator in Gross Weight mode, press PRESET, then if the value displayed is acceptable press ENTER to save it, otherwise use the numeric keys to enter a new value and press ENTER to save it.

Starts and controls the fill, discharge, and batch operations: the display shows START=YES (ENTER starts, 0/NO aborts), and pressing it during a run suspends the operation (CONTINUE=YES) so it can be resumed or stopped.

lights.does: Turned on to indicate that the weight is within +/- 1/4 division of the center of zero.
Turned on when the weight display is stable, meaning the change in successive weight samples is less than the motion limits selected during setup and calibration.
Signals that the displayed weight is less than the minimum value of acceptable weight used in the Checkweigher feature. Active only when the Checkweigher feature is enabled.

Signals that the displayed weight is within the acceptable weight limits for the Checkweigher feature — equal to or greater than the minimum acceptable weight and equal to or less than the maximum acceptable weight.
Signals that the displayed weight is equal to or greater than the minimum value of overweight used in the Checkweigher feature. Active only when the Checkweigher feature is enabled.
Located to the right of the weight display; turned on to show that the displayed weight is the net weight (gross weight less tare weight).
Located to the right of the weight display; turned on to indicate that the displayed weight is the gross weight.
Displayed to show that the displayed weight is the tare weight.

These numeric annunciators above the display show the status of the eight preset weight comparators, or (up to) seven batch ingredients and the dump gate (preset 8). A lit annunciator signals that the discharged weight is equal to or less than the corresponding preset value.

lights.key: Unit lights: lb, kg, tn, t, g
lights.does: The lit annunciator shows the displayed weight units: lb pounds and kg kilograms to the left of the display; tn avoirdupois tons, t metric tons, and g grams to the right of the display.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale, tare is the stored container weight, and net is gross less tare. The N, G, and T annunciators to the right of the display tell you which number you are seeing, and the accumulator displays reuse those same lights.

ideas.h: Trim is the material still in the air
ideas.text: When a preset shuts off a fill, material already falling still lands on the scale. The trim weight compensates for material in transit: the preset turns on when the displayed weight equals or exceeds the preset value less its trim, so the scale lands on target instead of overshooting.

ideas.h: Every fill teaches the next one
ideas.text: When a fill or batch operation finishes, the trim weight is recalculated, stored in non-volatile memory, and the displayed weight is added to the preset and gross or net accumulators. Run after run, the cut-off is reworked from what actually happened.

ideas.h: An ID turns a weight into a record
ideas.text: A weight by itself is just a number. The ID storage feature ties weighings to a container or truck string: temporary IDs print a two-pass transaction (first pass stores the weight, second pass prints and deletes), while permanent IDs carry a stored tare for a single-pass weighing.

ideas.h: Flashing means it is waiting on you
ideas.text: Annunciators flash on and off to indicate that the 220 is waiting for an input from the keypad for the mode indicated by the flashing annunciator. A flashing light on this panel is a question, not a status.

pre.short: Keeps or saves the value and advances to the next prompt.
Backs up one prompt — and the first key of every two-key feature.
Zeroes the empty scale (4% or 100% limit from setup).
Stores the container weight so the display shows net.
Prints the ticket and adds the weight to the accumulator — only when stable.
On when the display is steady; print and calibrate only when it is lit.

225.intro: The 225 (Navigator) has the richest panel in this family: standard function keys, alpha-numeric keys, soft keys that answer YES or NO on the display, and a navigation cluster with the red ENTER key in the middle. Calibration and setup of the indicator are accomplished entirely by this keypad.
menus: Getting in: with the indicator ON, press the SHIFT key and then press the Navigation ENTER key (the red square key in the center of the Navigation arrows). The display changes to show the SETUP/REVIEW MENU: 1. ENTER CALIBRATION AND SETUP, 2. VIEW AUDIT TRAIL COUNTERS, 3. CALIBRATE SCALE 1.

Picking a menu: selections are made by number — with a menu displayed, press the number key and then the ENTER key (for example, 1 then ENTER opens SETUP MENU #1; 3 then ENTER goes straight to calibration).

Changing a setting: pressing the ENTER key without entering a new value will retain the current setting and return the display to the menu display. To change a setting, enter or select a new value and then press ENTER; the new setting will be saved and the display returns to the menu display. On prompts requiring a value, pressing the ←/ESC key clears the value; on YES or NO prompts it backs up to the previous selection.

Getting out: the navigation arrows walk you back out — EXIT (Navigation UP Arrow) returns from sub-menus toward the SETUP MENU #1 and then the SETUP/REVIEW MENU. Several prompts answer on the soft keys: press the number, the ENTER key, YES or NO (on the soft keys), and then the ENTER key to save.

The sealed door: no calibration switch or jumper is needed to enter calibration and setup. If local metrology laws require physical sealing, the calibration seal jumper must be removed; with the seal jumper installed, attempting to change a sealed parameter gives a long error beep with CAL SEAL displayed.

keys.does: Pressing this key when the indicator is off will apply power and turn it ON. If the indicator is already on, pressing this key will turn the indicator OFF.

Used to reset the gross weight to zero. If the gross weight exceeds the preset limit for this key, an error message is displayed. The zero limit may be set to either 4% or 100% of scale capacity during Calibration and Setup.

A dual function key. Pressed alone (Pushbutton Tare mode) it stores the current gross weight as the new tare weight and the display changes to net weight mode (NET shown). Pressed after entering a numeric value (Keypad Tare) the entered value is accepted as the new tare weight. Tare weights equal to or greater than scale capacity cannot be entered, and the value must match the scale division value.

Toggles between the Net and Gross weight mode; the selected mode is indicated by showing G for Gross or NET for Net on the display. If pressed and no valid tare weight has been entered, the display shows -NO TARE- and the indicator remains in Gross mode.

Changes the weighing units to the alternate units if selected during calibration and setup of the indicator (tons, pounds only, ounces, tonnes, kilograms, grams, and custom; not all combinations are supported).
The red square key in the center of the Navigation arrows. It accepts the setting or selection and returns the display to the menu display; pressed with SHIFT it opens the SETUP/REVIEW MENU.
On YES or NO prompts it backs up to the previous selection. On prompts requiring a value to be entered, pressing it clears the value.

Adds the displayed Gross or Net weight or Piece Count to the associated accumulator and initiates transmission of weight and other data to the printer output port. The indicator will not respond to the Print command unless the weight display is stable. If displaying Gross weight, only gross prints; in Net, the Gross, Tare, and Net weights are printed.

The partner key for feature combinations: SHIFT then ENTER increases the LCD contrast, SHIFT then SPACE decreases it, SHIFT & TARE displays the current tare weight for 3 seconds, SHIFT+UNITS enters the Test mode, and SHIFT, ESC, PRINT together select the print ticket format.

Enter numeric data during setup and calibration and during normal operation, and pick numbered menu selections. In the alphanumeric mode, combined with the SHIFT key, their alternate meanings (letters and symbols) are output.
Displays the contents of the 32 ID accumulators and the total Gross and Net weight accumulators. The Total Gross, Total Net, and Count accumulators are updated with every print command.
Used to enter the Preset Weight Comparators' (PWC) weight and trim values.

lights.does: Turned on to show that the weight is within +/- 1/4 division of the center of zero.
Turned on when the weight display is stable, indicating the change in successive weight samples is less than the motion limits selected during Calibration and Setup.
Turned on to indicate that the displayed weight is the Gross weight.
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the Net weight (Gross weight less Tare weight).
Turned on to indicate that the displayed weight is the tare weight.

lights.key: Unit lights: lb, kg, oz, tn, t, g
lights.does: The lit annunciator shows the displayed weight measurement: lb pounds, kg kilograms, oz ounces, tn tons, t tonnes (metric tons), or g grams.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale, tare is the stored container weight, and net is gross less tare. The G, NET, and T annunciators tell you which number you are seeing, and NET/GROSS shows -NO TARE- instead of a fake net when no tare has been stored.

ideas.h: The seal keeps a diary
ideas.text: A Category 1 audit trail keeps two counters — one for calibration changes, one for configuration changes — each able to record 999 changes in non-volatile memory. An inspector can view or print them, so the indicator itself records how often its sealed settings were touched.

ideas.h: ENTER means keep it or take it
ideas.text: Throughout setup, pressing ENTER with nothing typed retains the current setting and returns you to the menu, while typing a value first means the new value is saved. ENTER with no entry is the safe look-and-leave key.

ideas.h: The C numbers are the fingerprint
ideas.text: The 225 has seven calibration modes; the last two use parameter values or the calibration "C" numbers from a previous calibration. Those recorded numbers let a scale be restored from its documented fingerprint instead of starting over with test weights.

ideas.h: A password can guard the door
ideas.text: On indicators programmed for international use (USA=NO), a password of up to 12 characters can be required to enter Calibration and Setup; a wrong password shows ERROR and returns to weight mode. The book warns that a forgotten password means the indicator must be reprogrammed, erasing all memory.

pre.short: The red center key — accepts the value and returns you to the menu.
Backs up one selection, or clears a typed value.
Zeroes the empty scale (4% or 100% limit from setup).
Stores the container weight so the display reads net.
Prints the ticket and adds to the accumulator — only when stable.
On when the display is steady — trust it before you print or calibrate.
