250.intro: The Model 250 is a six-digit LCD indicator with a bright backlit display and a simplified menu system. All models use the same six keys in the same layout, and each key does one job in Weigh mode and a different job in Setup mode.
menus: To make changes or calibrate, press the setup button to access the Setup Mode. In Setup Mode the display shows editing annunciators (GRP, ITM, SEL, EDT and OK) above the front panel keys, and you press the key below the annunciator you want.

Move through the menus with GRP and ITM: the ZERO key (GRP) steps through the list of Groups and the TARE key (ITM) steps through the list of Items. In the book example, press ZERO (GRP) again and again to show the BUILD group, then press TARE (ITM) again and again to show the CAP item.

Show and change a setting with SEL and EDT: the GROSS/NET key (SEL) displays the current setting for the chosen item and moves the editing cursor or flashing digit, and the PRINT key (EDT) steps through the available options or cycles a digit from 0 through 9. In a number, the flashing digit is the one that will change, and the left most digit can be changed to a dash (-) for a negative number.

Accept and step back with OK: the f key (OK), and also the TARE key (ITM), accepts the displayed option or all of the displayed digits and re-displays the menu item name. Some entries have upper and lower limits, and an entry outside that range makes the indicator display dashes (- - - - - -).

keys.does: Turns the Model 250 on and off: press and hold to turn it on (the segments light then clear, then the software version and calibration counter show), and press and hold for three seconds to turn it off with a countdown. A short press turns the backlight back on when running on batteries.

Performs a gross zero when an empty scale has drifted away from true zero, limited by the Z.RANGE setting; the zero is stored when power is removed and re-used at the next power up, and a long press in Industrial mode removes the stored zero. In Setup Mode this key is GRP and steps through the list of Groups.

Performs an auto-tare that temporarily sets the scale to zero, for example cancelling the weight of a carton, so the display shows Net weight with the NET annunciator lit; the tared weight is deducted from the allowable range and is stored when power is removed. In Setup Mode this key is ITM, steps through Items, and can accept changes and return to the menus.

Switches the display between Gross weight and Net weight when a tare has been taken with the TARE key. A long press toggles the GSE-LINK infrared link on and off (the display briefly shows opto-L while the editing annunciators flash), and in Setup Mode this key is SEL, displaying the current setting and moving the editing cursor or flashing digit.

Prints the current weight reading when a printer or computer is attached and manual print is selected, showing the PRINT prompt while it waits (up to 10 seconds if the printer is offline); each printed weight is added to an internal total, and a long press prints the accumulated total then clears it. In Setup Mode this key is EDT and steps through the available options or cycles a digit 0 through 9.

User defined function key that leaves the factory with no function programmed; its primary function is chosen in setup from options such as peak hold and counting, with an overlay sticker to label it, and a long press may be used for certain functions. In Setup Mode this key is OK and accepts changes and returns to the menus.

lights.does: On when the gross reading is within plus or minus one quarter of a division of true zero.
On when the displayed reading is NET weight.
On when the displayed reading is not stable.
On when the displayed weight is within the zero dead band setting; the symbol shows near the top right corner of the display.
On when the displayed reading is held.
On when battery voltage is too low and the batteries need replacing or recharging; the symbol shows in the top right corner of the display.
Red annunciator on when the setpoint weight is over the setpoint target.

ideas.h: Wait for a still reading
ideas.text: After you press ZERO, TARE or PRINT, the indicator waits for a stable, valid reading before it does the job. If the reading stays unstable, or a diagnostic error keeps it invalid for longer than 10 seconds, the job is cancelled and STABLE ERROR is displayed. More filtering or a smaller motion detection value can make the reading settle.

ideas.h: Zero and tare are remembered
ideas.text: A zero taken with the ZERO key is stored when power is removed and used again at the next power up, but only within the Z.RANGE limit. A tare is also stored across power off, and because the tared weight comes off the scale range, it lowers the biggest weight the display can show.

ideas.h: A locked key beeps long
ideas.text: Single keys can be disabled in setup, though all keys are enabled at the factory. A locked key gives a long beep when pressed, while a normal beep with no action usually means the indicator is still waiting for the scale to become stable.

ideas.h: Numbers stop at their limits
ideas.text: Option lists are single choice: SEL shows the current setting, EDT cycles the choices, and OK accepts and shows the item name again. Number entries work digit by digit on the flashing digit, and entries outside the allowed upper or lower limits are refused with a row of dashes on the display.

ideas.h: One spare key, many jobs
ideas.text: The f key is a spare that is programmed in setup for the job the scale needs, such as unit switching, counting, manual hold, peak hold, live weight averaging or accumulation. An overlay sticker under the key labels which job was chosen, and some jobs use a long press of the same key.

pre.short: Weigh: gross zero on empty scale. Setup (GRP): step through Groups.
Weigh: auto-tare to Net. Setup (ITM): step Items; accepts and returns.
Setup (SEL): show setting, move to next flashing digit.
Setup (EDT): cycle options/digits 0-9. Weigh: print weight.
Setup (OK): accept setting/number, back to item name.
On = not stable; ZERO/TARE/PRINT wait, then cancel at 10 s.

320IS Plus.name: 320IS Plus
320IS Plus.intro: The 320IS Plus front panel is a large 0.8-inch, six-digit LED display with a 24-button keypad and eight LED annunciators; it is an intrinsically safe indicator in a sealed stainless case (Sections 1.2 and 1.5–1.6, pp.8–10). In setup mode the weigh keys double as menu arrows, and the full keypad types values directly.
menus: The 320IS Plus is configured with a series of menus accessed through the front panel in setup mode: CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR (calibration), SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT, SETPNT (setpoints), DIGIN, ALGOUT, and VERS (Table 3-1, p.26).

Four front panel keys are directional in setup mode: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down to different menu levels, and TARE serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values (Section 1.7, p.11).

To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group appears, then move down to the submenu or parameter; the default or previously selected value appears first. Scroll to view a parameter's values and press Enter (TARE) to select and move back up one level (p.11).

To edit numeric values, use the navigation keys to select the digit and increment or decrement it, or type the value on the numeric keypad; press Enter (TARE) to save and return to the level above (p.11).

Test mode (diagnostics such as the raw A/D count and digital input states) is entered by pressing and holding the setup switch until the display shows TEST; after about three seconds it shifts to A/DTST, and the ZERO key exits test mode (Section 8.8, p.70).

keys.does: Turns the indicator on or off (Table 1-1, p.9).

Returns the gross weight display to zero. In setup mode it moves up (vertically) between menu levels and increments values, and it exits at the top level; in test mode it exits test mode (Table 1-1, p.9).
Toggles between gross, net and piece count mode. In setup mode it moves down (vertically) between menu levels and decrements values (Table 1-1, p.9).
Press to enter an auto tare or keyed tare. In setup mode it is the Enter key for selecting parameter values (Table 1-1, p.9).
Toggles between primary and secondary units. In setup mode it moves left (horizontally) on the same menu level (Table 1-1, p.9).
Prints using the GFMT print format; printing can only be done when the standstill annunciator is shown (Table 1-1, p.9; Table 1-2, p.10). In setup mode it moves right (horizontally).

Works with setpoints from the front panel: display a setpoint value, change it by typing a new value on the numeric keypad and pressing Enter, and turn a setpoint off or back on (Sections 1.8 and 1.8.10, pp.12–13).
Used for time and date entry from the front panel (Table 1-1, p.9).
Displays the current accumulator value (Table 1-1, p.9).
Clears the displayed value, in normal mode and in setup mode (Table 1-1, p.9).
Enters a numeric parameter value directly — for example typing a new setpoint value — instead of stepping digits with the arrow keys (Table 1-1, p.9).

lights.does: Lit when the displayed weight is a gross weight — the whole weight on the scale.
Lit when the displayed weight is a net weight — gross minus the stored tare.
Gross weight is ±0.25 graduations of zero. This annunciator lights when the scale is zeroed.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including tare functions and printing, can only be done when the standstill symbol is shown.
Indicates that a tare value has been entered and is stored.
The Count annunciator is listed on the 320IS Plus panel but is not used on this model (Table 1-2, p.10).
Pounds are the units of the displayed value. If neither primary nor secondary units are lb, kg, oz, or g, the lb annunciator is lit for primary units.
Kilograms are the units of the displayed value; also the secondary units annunciator for unit combinations without their own LED.

ideas.h: Gross or net — the lights keep it honest
ideas.text: The Gross and Net annunciators always say which weight you are reading: everything on the scale, or only what is left after the stored tare is subtracted (net = gross − tare). Check the light before trusting the number.

ideas.h: Standstill gates the action keys
ideas.text: The Standstill annunciator shows the scale is settled within its motion band. Tare functions and printing can only be done while it is shown — the indicator will not take a value from a scale that is still moving.

ideas.h: Zeroed means within a quarter graduation
ideas.text: Center of Zero lights when gross weight is within ±0.25 graduations of zero, and it lights when the scale is zeroed. A graduation is the smallest displayed step, so the light means zero to within a quarter of that step.

ideas.h: Numbers are typed, not scrolled
ideas.text: With the full 24-key pad, parameter values and setpoints can be typed in directly instead of nudging digits one at a time — enter the new value on the keypad and press Enter (TARE) to take it. The arrow keys remain for walking the menu tree.

ideas.h: lb and kg are stand-ins, too
ideas.text: Only lb and kg have their own LEDs. When the configured units are something else — ounces, tons, grams — the lb LED stands in for the primary unit and kg for the secondary, so the lit LED tells you the slot, not always the true unit name.

pre.short: The Enter key in setup — selects and saves values; takes an auto or keyed tare in weigh mode.
Zeroes the gross display; menu up / increment key, and it exits test mode.
Prints the GFMT format when the standstill annunciator shows; menu right key.
Types values directly — test weights, setpoints, and parameters.
Toggles gross, net, and piece count display; menu down / decrement key.
Tare and printing wait for this light — it means the reading is settled.

320IS.name: 320IS
320IS.intro: The 320IS front panel is a large 0.8-inch, six-digit LED display with a 6-button keypad and eight LED annunciators; it is an intrinsically safe indicator in a sealed stainless case (Sections 1.2 and 1.5–1.6, pp.6–8). The symbols above the keys show their second job: in setup mode they become menu arrows.
menus: The 320IS is configured with a series of menus accessed through the front panel in setup mode: CONFIG (configuration), FORMAT (units/display rate), CALIBR (calibration), SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT (print format), DIGIN, ALGOUT, and VERS (version) (Table 3-1, p.23).

Four front panel keys are directional in setup mode: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down to different menu levels, and TARE serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values (Section 1.7, p.9).

To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group appears, then move down to the submenu or parameter; the default or previously selected value appears first. Scroll left or right to view a parameter's values and press Enter (TARE) to select the value and move back up one level (p.9).
To edit numeric values, use the navigation keys to select the digit and increment or decrement its value; press Enter (TARE) to save the value entered and return to the level above (p.9).

Test mode (diagnostics such as the raw A/D count and digital input states) is entered by pressing and holding the setup switch until the display shows TEST; after about three seconds it shifts to A/DTST, and the ZERO key exits test mode (Section 7.8, p.55).

keys.does: Turns the indicator on or off; this is one of the six front panel keys, and the Exit key in test mode (Table 1-1, p.7; p.55).
Returns the gross weight display to zero. In setup mode it moves up (vertically) through menu levels and increments values; in test mode it exits back to the top level (Table 1-1, p.7).

Toggles between gross, net and piece count mode. In setup mode it moves down (vertically) through menu levels and decrements values; it has no function in test mode because the test menu is a single level (Table 1-1, p.7).
Press to enter an auto tare or keyed tare. In setup mode it is the Enter key for selecting parameter values; in count mode it performs the piece count (Table 1-1, p.7).
Toggles between primary and secondary units. In setup mode it moves left (horizontally) on the same menu level (Table 1-1, p.7).

Prints using the GFMT print format (CFMT in count mode). In setup mode it moves right (horizontally) on the same menu level, and printing can only be done when the standstill annunciator is lit (Table 1-1, p.7; Table 1-2, p.8).

Lit when the displayed weight is a net weight — after a stored tare.

Lit to show that the indicator is in piece count mode, showing a quantity instead of a weight.
Pounds are the units of the displayed value. If neither primary nor secondary units are lb, kg, oz, or g, the lb annunciator is lit for primary units.
Kilograms are the units of the displayed value; the kg LED also serves as the secondary units annunciator for unit combinations without their own LED.

ideas.h: Gross or net — the lights keep it honest
ideas.text: The display can show everything on the scale (gross) or what is left after a stored tare (net). The Gross and Net annunciators are always showing which one you are reading, so the number is never a mystery.

ideas.h: Standstill gates the action keys
ideas.text: The Standstill annunciator lights when the scale is settled within its motion band. Tare functions and printing can only be done while it is lit — the indicator will not act on a reading that is still moving.

ideas.h: Zeroed means within a quarter graduation
ideas.text: Center of Zero lights when gross weight is within ±0.25 graduations of zero, and it lights when the scale is zeroed. A graduation is the smallest step the scale can display, so the light means zero to within a quarter of the tiniest step.

ideas.h: Count mode counts from a sample
ideas.text: The Count annunciator lights in piece count mode, where the indicator shows a quantity instead of a weight. The TARE key performs the piece count routine that teaches it the parts, so counting always starts from a real sample.

ideas.h: lb and kg are stand-ins, too
ideas.text: Pounds and kilograms have their own LEDs, but other units do not. For combinations like primary short tons and secondary pounds, the lb LED lights for the primary unit and kg for the secondary — watch which LED is lit, not just which unit you expect.

350/355 IS.name: 350/355 IS
350/355 IS.intro: The 350 IS / 355 IS is GSE's Intrinsically Safe indicator, with a six-digit LED or LCD display and 12 annunciators for weight and status. The 350 IS uses a sealed 5-button elastomer keypad where each key has two distinct functions, while the 355 IS uses a 22-key full numeric elastomer keypad. The same keys do different jobs in Weigh Mode, Count Mode, Setup Mode and Calibration Mode.
menus: The keypad changes meaning by mode: in Weigh Mode the five primary functions are gross zero, print/transmit, units, tare, and toggling the display between GROSS, NET, QUANTITY and setpoint TARGETS if enabled. Secondary functions let you enter target values, perform piece samples, and access setup parameters. (p.1)

In Setup Mode one key advances to the next setup parameter and another returns to the previous setup parameter, so you walk the parameter list up and down rather than typing parameter numbers. A key also advances the cursor to the next entry position and cycles prompts. (p.1)

While entering data in Setup Mode, the print key scrolls through digits during entry and during setpoint entry, the units key advances the cursor and cycles prompts, a key scrolls through parameter sub-set selections, and there are backspace (erase the right-most digit) and absolute-clear (clear an entry or the value of a parameter) functions. Reverse character scroll is also listed for data and sample entry. (p.1)

To accept or leave: one key performs an auto-tare and/or accepts an entry in progress and answers 'YES' to query prompts, while the zero/clear key exits the Setup Mode and/or answers 'NO' to query prompts and clears an entry in progress. In the 355 IS table the sample key also accepts an entry in Setup Mode. (p.1)

Setpoint targets can be changed from Weigh Mode when a check-weigh program is configured: the Targ 1 value becomes an available mode for the display-mode key, you press to view the current target (for example Targ1 250), key in a new value such as 400, and press again to accept it; you can also accept the weight already on the scale as the target instead of keying a value. Lo/Hi or PctLo/PctHi are the subsets under Targ 1. (p.50, p.54, p.64)

keys.does: In Weigh Mode it performs a gross zero and selects the gross mode, and/or clears an entry in progress. In Count Mode it performs a quantity zero and/or clears an entry in progress. In Setup Mode it exits the Setup Mode and/or answers 'NO' to query prompts and/or clears an entry in progress; there is also absolute-clear and backspace behaviour that clears an entry or erases the right-most digit during data entry.

In Weigh Mode it initiates data transmission out the communication port and performs a print function. During data or setpoint entry it 'scrolls' through digits. Setup P210/P230 can be set so the transmission is sent with the [PRINT] key. (also p.31)

In Weigh Mode it toggles the units of measure between lb, kg, g, lb oz and oz, described in the table as toggling between 'lb' and 'kg' and/or advancing the cursor to the next entry position. In Count Mode it toggles through standard sample sizes and/or begins a new sample entry. In Setup Mode it advances the cursor to the next entry position and/or cycles prompts.

In Weigh Mode it tares any displayed weight and selects the net mode; as a secondary function it performs an auto-tare function (if enabled) and/or accepts an entry in progress, and if the tare weight is known you key in the value and press this key. In Setup Mode it accepts an entry in progress and/or 'scrolls' through parameter sub-set selections and/or answers 'YES' to query prompts.

In Weigh Mode it toggles the display between GROSS, NET, QUANTITY and setpoint TARGETS (if enabled), and/or restores power to the indicator if auto-shutoff is enabled. In Count Mode it also toggles between display modes and/or restores power. In Setup Mode it advances to the next setup parameter.

On the 355 IS it performs a sample; if a number is keyed in beforehand it will be used as the sample size. In Setup Mode it accepts an entry. The count examples show pressing a key to perform an auto-tare, the scale prompting to add 10 pieces, then adding pieces and pressing to sample and display the current quantity. (also p.46)

On the 355 IS the number keys make entering a tare value or average piece weight easier. They are used for key-in values generally: the book refers repeatedly to key-in parameters and to keying in a new target value, a known tare value, a sample count such as 36 pieces, or fixed sample counts. (also p.46, p.54)

lights.does: Setpoint #1 activated (relay 1 closed). It is the red annunciator on the left of the display; in absolute check-weighing SP1 illuminated red means OVER.
Setpoint #2 activated (relay 2 closed). It is the green annunciator; in absolute check-weighing SP2 illuminated green means GOOD.
Setpoint #3 activated (relay 3 closed). It is the yellow annunciator; in absolute check-weighing SP3 illuminated yellow means UNDER.
Scale is in motion. Motion-inhibited transmits and motion-inhibited setpoint activation will be delayed until motion ceases.
Lights when the battery reaches a low tolerance — a low-battery warning.
Displayed value represents the current gross weight.
Displayed value represents the current net weight.
Displayed value represents the current piece quantity (Count). The quantity mode is identified by illumination of the QTY annunciator when counting is enabled. (also p.31)

ideas.h: Wait for stillness before acting
ideas.text: If the scale is moving, the indicator holds off things that need a steady reading: motion-inhibited transmits and motion-inhibited setpoint activation are delayed until motion ceases, and the MOTION light tells you why. Send Stability does the same for transmissions, delaying them until a no-motion condition exists, and setpoint activation methods likewise wait for a no-motion condition before activating. (also p.31, p.46)

ideas.h: Setpoints need a real weight, not zero noise
ideas.text: For check-weighing the annunciators or setpoints only activate when the displayed value is at least five graduations above zero. That keeps the OVER / GOOD / UNDER lights (SP1 red, SP2 green, SP3 yellow) from firing on an empty or near-zero scale. The same five-graduation rule is stated for percentage and target-deviation check-weighing. (also p.50, p.64)

ideas.h: Pre-acts stop the fill early on purpose
ideas.text: Pre-acts are control actions taken before the target is reached, to prevent over-filling caused by product flow rate, relay and valve response time, and product still in the air. Pre-act 1 switches a dual-speed fill from fast-fill to slow-fill for the final dribble, and pre-act 2 sets the final cutoff weight to compensate for a dispensing control's closure time and free-fall material still falling after shutoff.

ideas.h: Counting learns from a sample
ideas.text: In count work the scale first auto-tares and prompts you to add a starter sample, usually 10 pieces, then learns the piece weight from what you actually put on. You can toggle the prompted sample amount between 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100, or key in a variable count such as 36 pieces and press to sample that many and display the quantity. On the 355 IS, keying a number before sampling makes that number the sample size. (also p.1)

ideas.h: Targets are compared the way you choose
ideas.text: A setpoint target is not automatically judged against whatever is on screen: the Based selection chooses whether targets are compared to Net, Gross, or Quantity/Count. In the worked fill example Targ 1 = 2000 with Based = Net and a pre-act of 5 closes the fill valve at 1995 lb, and Learn can analyse five previous fills or discharges and auto-adjust the pre-act.

pre.short: Zero first and clear a bad entry — exits Setup / says NO.
Tare it, or press to accept an entry — says YES in Setup.
Print / send when steady — also scrolls digits while keying in.
355 IS: key the value in, then accept it (350 IS scrolls digits instead).
Step GROSS / NET / QTY / TARGETS — in Setup moves to next parameter.
MOTION lit = still moving — transmits and setpoints wait for stillness.

350/355.intro: The GSE Model 350/355 is a digital weigh indicator with a six-digit, 7-segment LED or LCD display and 12 annunciators for weight and status. The Model 350 uses a sealed 5-button elastomer keypad where each key has two distinct functions, and the same keys do different jobs in Weigh Mode, Setup Mode, and Calibration Mode.
menus: The keypad works in three modes: Weigh Mode, Setup Mode, and Calibration Mode. The book says the keys perform different functions in each mode, and their secondary functions let an operator enter target values, perform piece samples, and access setup parameters.

In the Weigh Mode, when a setpoint operation has been set up, one front key cycles through the available modes (Gross, Net, Quantity, Targ 1, and so on). Setpoint-related values such as Targ 1 become available modes automatically once the setpoint program is configured.

To change a target from the Weigh Mode, key in the new value first and then press the key to store it as the new parameter value. Pressing the key alone, with nothing keyed in, moves down into the first subset of the current target: pre-acts and tolerances are subsets of their target values.

For parts counting, the counting parameter must be enabled first. In the book's sampling sequence you press a key until the QTY annunciator is lit, add the sample pieces, and press again to sample and display the current quantity.

Setup values are numbered parameters (for example P110 Full Scale and the P5100 setpoint parameters). The book repeatedly sends keypad data entry to its 'Key-In Parameters' instructions (page 43 in the book) and setup entry to page 40; those step-by-step press sequences are not readable in this extract because the key symbols came through as symbol-font junk.

keys.does: Model 355 keypad only: allows a target value to be entered or viewed (parameter P5000). It only appears when a 355 keypad is detected, and sending %g from a serial device is the same as pressing it.

Model 355 keypad only: pressing Start in the Weigh Mode with setpoints enabled resumes a paused setpoint operation (P5003). In setpoint modes other than check-weighing, Start does the same job as a remote key.
Model 355 keypad only: the Stop key can be enabled or disabled in setup (P5002). Sending %h from a serial device is the same as pressing it.

With the display set to Auto (P420), the display shuts off after the weight has been stable within 6 divisions for 5 minutes. Pressing ON, or changing the weight by more than 6 divisions, turns the display back on.

A remote contact closure whose job is chosen in setup at P800: None, Print, Tare or Zero. If a setpoint is configured to use the remote key as its activation method, that setpoint setting overrides P800.

Zero is one of the functions the book assigns to key operation: P800 lets the Remote Key closure be set to None, Print, Tare or Zero, and the specification page lists ZERO among the remote input functions (TARE, PRINT, ZERO).

Tare is one of the functions the book assigns to key operation: P800 lets the Remote Key closure be set to None, Print, Tare or Zero, and the specification page lists TARE among the remote input functions (TARE, PRINT, ZERO).

Print is one of the functions the book assigns to key operation: P800 lets the Remote Key closure be set to None, Print, Tare or Zero, and the specification page lists PRINT among the remote input functions (TARE, PRINT, ZERO).

lights.does: Setpoint #1 is activated (relay 1 closed). On the LED display SP1 is red; in check-weighing it is the OVER light.
Setpoint #2 is activated (relay 2 closed). On the LED display SP2 is green; in check-weighing it is the GOOD light.
Setpoint #3 is activated (relay 3 closed). On the LED display SP3 is yellow; in check-weighing it is the UNDER light.
The displayed weight is at center-of-zero, within plus or minus one quarter of a display graduation.
The scale is in motion. Motion-inhibited transmits and motion-inhibited setpoint activation are delayed until the motion stops.
The displayed value is the current gross weight.
The displayed value is the current net weight.
The displayed value is the current piece quantity (Count), used in parts counting.

ideas.h: Motion holds the outputs, not the lights
ideas.text: The setpoint annunciator lights themselves are not motion-inhibited, so a light can show a setpoint state while the scale is still moving. The actual relay outputs, though, will not activate until a no-motion condition exists, so the machine does not act on a still-moving scale.

ideas.h: Setpoints stay quiet near zero
ideas.text: For check-weighing, the annunciators and setpoints will not activate until the displayed value is at least five graduations above zero. This keeps an empty or near-empty scale from tripping OVER, GOOD, or UNDER decisions.

ideas.h: Pre-acts are the early cutoff
ideas.text: In a fill, the target is where you want to end up, but the pre-act is the point where the feed actually cuts off or slows down. Pre-act 1 switches a dual-speed fill from fast to slow, and pre-act 2 sets the final cutoff, so material still in flight does not overshoot the target.

ideas.h: The indicator learns from the last five fills
ideas.text: With the Learn feature on, the indicator looks at the final weights of the five previous operations and recalculates the pre-act cutoff on its own. That lets it compensate for things like product viscosity, changes in plant air pressure, and sticky valves without manual re-tuning.

ideas.h: Pause kills every setpoint at once
ideas.text: Pause is a safety and convenience stop for setpoint operations, useful for mid-cycle breaks or mechanical adjustments. When invoked it deactivates all setpoints and the display shows a Tare/Abort prompt: one keypress aborts the current cycle, and any other keypress resumes it.

pre.short: Key in the new value first, then press TARGET; press it alone to open the target's subsets.
On a 355, START resumes a paused setpoint operation.
Zero can be assigned to the remote key at P800 (None, Print, Tare or Zero).
Tare can be assigned to the remote key at P800 (None, Print, Tare or Zero).
Print can be assigned to the remote key at P800 (None, Print, Tare or Zero).
If MOTION is lit, wait: outputs and motion-inhibited transmits hold until motion stops.

370/375.intro: The Model 370 and Model 375 are Precision Counting Scales with a six digit, 7-segment bright green LED display. The display shows weight as alphanumeric data, abbreviated where the six digits require it, and uses 11 annunciators to show weight and status information.
menus: Setup Mode is entered with [ZERO] + [SELECT]. The book also gives [SELECT], [ZERO], [PRINT], [UNITS], [TARE] or, on the Model 375, keying 23640 then [SAMPLE/Enter]. If the unit is in remote display mode, unplug it and press [ZERO] + [SELECT] on power up to reach setup.
In Setup Mode, [SELECT] advances to the next setup parameter. On the Model 375, [PRINT] returns to the previous setup parameter.
Once at a parameter, [TARE] on the 370 and [SAMPLE/Enter] on the 375 scroll through parameter sub-set selections and answer YES to query prompts. [ZERO] answers NO to query prompts.

During data entry, [PRINT] scrolls through digits, [UNITS] advances the cursor to the next entry position, and [ZERO] + [PRINT] works as backspace to erase the right-most digit. [ZERO] + [UNITS] reverses the character scroll direction.
On the Model 375, [ZERO] exits the Setup Mode. The remote-display setup steps end with Save changes and exit the setup mode.

keys.does: Performs a gross zero function in Weigh Mode, a quantity zero in Count Mode, and clears an entry in progress. Hold this key on power-up to turn on the display regardless of P420. In Setup Mode it exits the Setup Mode on the 375, answers NO to query prompts, and clears an entry in progress.
Performs a print function in Weigh Mode and Count Mode, and scrolls through digits during setpoint or time/date entry. In Setup Mode on the 375 it returns to the previous setup parameter.

Toggles between lb, kg or third unit if enabled in Weigh Mode, and toggles through standard sample sizes during a sample in Count Mode. It advances the cursor to the next entry position and cycles prompts, and in Setup Mode on the 375 it shows the current parameter number.

Performs an auto-tare function if enabled and accepts an entry in progress in Weigh Mode and Count Mode. In Setup Mode it accepts an entry in progress, scrolls through parameter sub-set selections, and answers YES to query prompts.

Toggles between display modes and restores power to the Model 370/375 if auto-shutoff is enabled. In Setup Mode it advances to the next setup parameter, and during a sample it toggles through standard sample sizes.

Enters the counting mode and performs a sample for an accurate part count and calculates an average piece weight. It also accepts an entry in progress. In Setup Mode it scrolls through parameter sub-set selections and answers YES to query prompts.
Absolute clear - clears an entry in progress and/or clears the value of a parameter. On the Model 375 it can also abort a sample.

On the Model 375 the number keys are used to manually enter a value for tare weight or target weight, average piece weight, sample size etc. The number keys make entering a tare value or average piece weight easier.

lights.does: Setpoint #1 activated (relay 1 closed). In check-weigh operation this is the red OVER annunciator.
Setpoint #2 activated (relay 2 closed). In check-weigh operation this is the green GOOD annunciator.
Setpoint #3 activated (relay 3 closed). In check-weigh operation this is the yellow UNDER annunciator.
Scale is in motion. Motion inhibited transmits and motion inhibited setpoint activation will be delayed until motion ceases.
Displayed value represents the current gross weight.
Displayed value represents the current net weight.
Displayed value represents the current piece quantity (Count).

ideas.h: Counting from a sample weight
ideas.text: Counting does not count pieces directly. You weigh a known sample of parts, the scale works out the average piece weight from that sample, and after that it turns any total weight into a piece quantity. That is why the SAMPLE key performs the sample and calculates the average piece weight, and why a bigger, stable sample gives a better count.

ideas.h: Gross, tare and net
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale. Tare is the part you tell the scale to ignore, such as a container. Net is what is left, the goods themselves. The TARE key does an auto-tare when enabled, and the GROSS and NET lights tell you which of those values the number on the display really is.

ideas.h: Motion holds up output
ideas.text: If the weight is still moving, the scale waits before it trusts it. When the MOTION light is on the scale is in motion, and motion inhibited transmits and motion inhibited setpoint activation are delayed until motion ceases. In plain terms, let the load settle before you expect a print or a setpoint to fire.

ideas.h: Check-weigh lights need weight on the scale
ideas.text: In check-weighing the SP1, SP2 and SP3 lights act as OVER (red), GOOD (green) and UNDER (yellow) against the target and its tolerances. They do not come alive at zero. The displayed value must be at least five graduations above zero before the annunciators or setpoints will activate.

ideas.h: Zero tracking cleans up tiny drift
ideas.text: Zero tracking is set in numbers of divisions at P112. It eliminates small weight deviations at or near zero, so dust, a bit of product or slow drift does not sit on the display as a false weight. The center-of-zero light shows when the displayed weight is at center-of-zero, within plus or minus one quarter of a display graduation.

Zero the scale, clear entry - in Setup answers NO, 375 exits Setup
Auto-tare the container - also accepts entry, scrolls choices
Print / send data - in Setup (375) back to previous parameter
Change display mode - in Setup moves to next parameter

380.intro: The 380 Synergy front panel is a seven-segment LCD display with six 1.0-inch digits and five flat panel keys, backed by tactile primary scale function buttons with an integrated power button. Annunciators built into the LCD show the units and scale functions (Section 3.0, p.32).
menus: Weigh mode is the default mode: the indicator displays gross or net weight and uses the annunciators to show scale status and the type of weight value displayed (Section 1.3, p.8).

User mode is reached by pressing and holding ZERO for five seconds while in weigh mode; it displays the audit, accumulator, tare and version menus. Hold ZERO five seconds to enter user mode only when the unit is already powered on — do not hold during power up, or the indicator enters update firmware mode (p.32).

Setup mode is entered by pressing ZERO once, momentarily, during the startup sequence — do not hold or double press. Most procedures in the book, including calibration, require setup mode (Section 1.3, p.8).
In menus the five keys work as arrows: ZERO moves up and GROSS/NET moves down through the menu structure, UNITS moves left, PRINT moves right, and TARE confirms (Table 3-1, p.32).

For numeric entry, ZERO increases the selected digit by 1, GROSS/NET decreases it by 1, UNITS deletes the digit and moves left, PRINT moves right one digit, and TARE enters the value (Table 3-1, p.32).

keys.does: Sets the current gross weight to zero, provided the amount of weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion; the zero band defaults to 1.9% of full scale but can be configured up to 100%. Hold five seconds to enter user mode when the unit is already powered on; in menus it moves up, and in numeric entry it increases the digit value by 1.

Switches the display mode from gross to net or from net to gross. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare; gross mode is shown by the G annunciator and net mode by the NET annunciator. In menus it moves down; in numeric entry it decreases the digit value by 1.
Performs one of several predetermined tare functions depending on the mode of operation selected in the TARE FN parameter. In menus it is the Confirm key; in numeric entry it enters the value.

Switches the weight display to an alternate unit, defined in the Configuration menu, which could be kg, g, lb, oz, tn or t. In menus it moves left; in numeric entry it deletes the current digit and moves left.

Turns the unit on and off: if on, press and hold for five seconds to turn off; if off, press and hold for two seconds to turn on. Pressed momentarily, it sends the on-demand print format out the configured port (RS-232 is the default), provided the conditions for standstill are met; if the ~ annunciator is showing, printing only happens if the scale comes out of motion within three seconds (p.35). In menus it moves right.

lights.does: Indicates the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero. A display division is the resolution of the displayed weight value — the smallest increase or decrease that can be displayed or printed.
Gross weight display mode — the full weight on the scale is being shown.
Net weight display mode — the display is showing gross weight minus the stored tare.
Tare annunciator: a push-button tare weight has been acquired and stored in memory.
Preset Tare annunciator: a preset tare weight has been keyed in and stored in memory.
Indicates remaining battery capacity: 3 bars means over 95% remaining, 2 bars means 5–95%, 1 bar means 1–5%, and 0 bars means under 1%.
The scale is unstable or outside the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare and print, can only be done when the unstable annunciator is off.
Shows which unit of measure is being used: lb (pounds), kg (kilograms), t (tonnes), g (grams), tn (short ton), or oz (ounce).

ideas.h: Three modes: weigh, user, setup
ideas.text: Weigh mode is the everyday mode. User mode (hold ZERO five seconds) holds the audit, accumulator, tare and version menus. Setup mode — one momentary ZERO press during startup — is where configuration and calibration live, and most procedures in the book require it.

ideas.h: Net is just gross minus tare
ideas.text: Net mode only exists once a tare value has been entered or acquired; net is the gross weight with the tare taken away. If no tare has been entered, the display stays in gross mode, and the G or NET annunciator always tells you which one you are looking at.

ideas.h: Wait for the ~ to go out
ideas.text: The ~ annunciator means the scale is still moving. Zero, tare and print can only be done when it is off — the annunciator is the scale's way of saying 'not steady yet, don't trust this yet.'

ideas.h: Zero is a band, not a point
ideas.text: ZERO only works when the weight to be added or removed sits inside the zero range and the scale is not in motion. That band defaults to 1.9% of full scale and can be configured as high as 100% of full scale.

ideas.h: A display division is the smallest step
ideas.text: The Center of Zero annunciator lights when the reading is within a quarter of a display division of zero. A division is simply the smallest weight change the display can show, so the light means 'as close to zero as this display can tell.'

pre.short: The confirm key — accepts entries in menus and numeric entry, and takes a tare in weigh mode.
Zeroes the scale inside the zero range when it is not moving; one tap during startup enters setup mode.
Momentary press prints when standstill conditions are met; hold 5 seconds for off, 2 seconds for on.
Switches to the alternate unit; deletes a digit and moves left during numeric entry.
Toggles gross and net display; moves down through menus.
Must be OFF before zero, tare, or print will work — wait for the scale to settle.

420 Plus.name: 420 Plus
420 Plus.intro: The 420 Plus front panel combines a keypad — with arrow symbols printed above the keys for setup mode — and eight LED annunciators that say what kind of value is on the display (Sections 1.2–1.3, p.8). In normal mode the keys weigh, tare, and print; in setup mode the same keys navigate menus, pick digits, and raise or lower values.
menus: In setup mode the front panel opens a menu tree: CONFIG (configuration), FORMAT (units and display rate), CALIBR (calibration), SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT (print format), SETPNT (setpoints), DIG IN, ALGOUT, and VERS (version) (Table 3-1, p.22).

Four front panel keys are directional in setup mode: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down to different menu levels, and TARE serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values (Section 3.1.3, p.22).
To pick a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group you want is on the display, then press down to the submenu or parameter; the default or previously selected value appears first (p.22).

Editing numeric values: move left/right to pick the digit, increment or decrement it with the up/down keys, or type the value on the numeric keypad; press Enter (TARE) to save the value and return to the level above (p.22).

Test mode gives diagnostic functions such as displaying the raw A/D count: press and hold the setup switch until the display shows TEST; after about three seconds it shifts to the first test function, A/DTST, and the ZERO key exits test mode (Section 7.9, p.57). Test mode is intended for factory use only.

keys.does: Zeroes the scale: in gross mode remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, then press ZERO — the center of zero annunciator lights to show the scale is zeroed. In setup mode it moves up between menu levels and increments values.

Switches the display mode from gross to net or from net to gross; if a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. In setup mode it moves down between menu levels and decrements values.

Acquires the tare weight of a container: press TARE and net weight displays with the tare-acquired annunciator lit. In setup mode TARE is the Enter key — it selects parameter values and saves an edited value, returning to the level above.
Switches between primary and secondary units; the appropriate units LED to the right of the display lights. In setup mode it scrolls left on the same menu level.
Print key. In setup mode PRINT scrolls right on the same menu level. Printing is one of the operations that can only be done when the standstill symbol is shown (p.8).
Switches from count display mode back to normal weighing mode so gross and net weight can be viewed while counting parts.

Enters sample acquisition mode for piece counting. Pressing SAMPLE scrolls through the selectable sample quantities (5, 10, 20, 50, 100) or to the PC WGT prompt for entering a known piece weight; ENTER then calibrates the indicator for counting the new parts.
Confirms entries: it accepts the sample in counting, accepts a new date or time typed on the numeric keypad, and accepts a new setpoint value (pp.10–11).
Displays a setpoint value: type the setpoint number on the numeric keypad and press SETPOINT, or press SETPOINT once per number (twice for setpoint 2). Type a new value and press ENTER to change it.

Press once to display the date, a second time to display the time. To set them, show the date or time, type the new value on the numeric keypad (date in the configured MMDDYY/DDMMYY/YYMMDD format, time in 24-hour format), and press ENTER. Time and date are backed up by battery.
Types values directly: custom sample sizes or a known piece weight in counting, new dates and times, setpoint numbers and values, and numeric parameter values in setup mode.

The front panel power switch turns the unit on or off — but only if jumper JMP1 is set to the SW position; otherwise the indicator powers up as soon as AC is applied and the panel power control is bypassed.

lights.does: Lit when the displayed weight is a gross weight — everything on the scale, nothing taken away.
Lit when the displayed weight is a net weight — gross minus the stored tare.
Gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero; this annunciator lights when the scale is zeroed.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including tare functions and printing, can only be done when the standstill symbol is shown.

Pounds are the units of the displayed value. The lb and kg LEDs also work as primary and secondary unit annunciators: if neither configured unit is lb or kg, lb lights for primary units and kg for secondary units.
Kilograms are the units of the displayed value; also used as the secondary units annunciator for unit combinations that have no LED of their own (for example short tons).
Lit to show the indicator is in piece count mode, displaying a part quantity instead of a weight.
Lights to show that a tare value was entered and is stored in the indicator.

ideas.h: Standstill means it can be trusted
ideas.text: The standstill symbol only shows when the scale is settled inside its motion band. Tare functions and printing refuse to work until it appears, so the symbol is the indicator's promise that the reading is steady enough to act on.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: Pressing TARE with a container on the scale stores its weight; the display then shows only what is added after it. GROSS/NET switches back and forth, and the Gross or Net annunciator always says which one you are reading.

ideas.h: The same keys steer the menus
ideas.text: In setup mode the weigh keys turn into arrows: UNITS and PRINT walk left and right, ZERO and GROSS/NET climb up and down levels, and TARE becomes Enter. The arrow symbols printed above the keys are the map.

ideas.h: Zero confirms itself
ideas.text: A proper zero is proven, not assumed: empty the scale, wait for standstill, press ZERO, and the center of zero annunciator lights only when gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero.

ideas.h: Counting starts from a sample
ideas.text: In count mode the indicator does not know what one part weighs until you teach it: put a known sample quantity on the scale (or enter a known piece weight), press ENTER, and the Count annunciator lights while it shows quantities instead of weight.

pre.short: The Enter key in setup — selects and saves parameter values; takes a tare in weigh mode.
Zeroes the scale once standstill shows; menu up key, and it exits test mode.
Prints only when the standstill symbol shows; menu right key in setup.
Types values directly — test weights, setpoints, times, and parameters.
Toggles gross and net display; menu down key in setup.
Must be shown before tare or printing will work — wait for the scale to settle.

480.intro: The 480 Legend Series front panel has a large 0.8-inch six-digit LED display with a seven-button keypad (the 480 Plus has an 18-button full numeric keypad). Four of the keys double as directional arrows for menu navigation.
menus: The 480 has four modes: normal weigh mode (default), configuration mode, user menu setup mode, and test mode. Most procedures, including calibration, require configuration mode (Section 1.5, p.9).

To enter configuration mode, remove the setup switch access screw from the back of the enclosure and press the configuration switch with a non-conductive tool; the indicator displays CONFIG. The user menu (accumulator, audit trail, tare display, unit ID, time & date, setpoints, communications, print formats, firmware version) is opened with the MENU key.

Four front panel keys are directional in menus: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between levels, and TARE serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values (Section 1.7, p.11).

Editing numeric values: select the digit with left/right, increment or decrement with up/down, and press TARE when correct. The 480 Plus numeric keypad embosses the digits so values can be typed instead (Sections 1.7.2-1.7.3, p.12).

keys.does: Power ON/OFF key on the front panel (Figure 1-2).
Allows front panel access to user setup and configuration mode.
Zeroes the scale (Section 1.8.2, p.13). In menus it moves up between levels and increments values.
Toggles units between primary and secondary (Section 1.8.3, p.13). In menus it scrolls left on the same level.
Acquires a tare (Section 1.8.4, p.14) or enters a preset/keyed tare (Section 1.8.5). In menus the Tare key serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values.
Print key. In menus it scrolls right on the same level.

Switches the display mode between gross and net. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. In menus it moves down between levels and decrements values.
480 Plus only: full numeric keypad. When editing numeric values, the method relies on the numbers embossed on the keypad rather than the navigation arrows.

lights.does: Gross weight display mode (or Brutto in OIML mode).
Net weight display mode.
The current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band.
Scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band; some operations, including zero, tare, and printing, can only be done when the standstill annunciator is on.
A push-button tare weight has been acquired and stored in memory.
A preset tare weight has been keyed in or entered and stored in memory.
Displays which unit of measure is being used: lb = pounds, kg = kilograms.

ideas.h: Configuration hides behind a switch
ideas.text: Calibration and most service work require configuration mode, which is entered by pressing the setup switch through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — the display shows CONFIG. Day-to-day functions live in the separate user menu opened with MENU.

ideas.h: Standstill gates the keys
ideas.text: Zero, tare, and printing can only be done when the standstill annunciator is on. If the scale is still moving, those keys wait.

ideas.h: Preset tare is keyed at zero
ideas.text: For a keyed tare, the scale is emptied and zeroed, TARE is pressed, 000000 shows with the focused digit flashing, the value is edited (or typed on the 480 Plus), and TARE accepts it — the display changes to Net mode and the PT LED lights.

ideas.h: Net means gross minus tare
ideas.text: The GROSS/NET key switches between the total weight and the weight after the stored tare is subtracted. Gross/Brutto or Net annunciators show which is displayed.

pre.short: Enter key in menus; also acquires or enters a tare.
Zeroes the scale; menu up/increment key.
Prints; menu right key.
Opens user setup; configuration starts at the rear setup switch.
480 Plus: types values directly instead of arrow-editing.
Must be on for zero, tare, and printing to work.

482-AG.name: 482-AG
482-AG.intro: The 482-AG livestock indicator has an LCD display with annunciators, a numeric keypad for entering values, and function keys built around weighing groups of animals: head count, a shrink factor, and load totals (Sections 1.4–1.6, pp.9–10). The same keys double as menu arrows in configuration mode.
menus: Configuration is entered at the back of the unit: remove the configuration switch access screw, insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch — CONFIG is displayed, and the CALIBR sub-menu is used to calibrate the indicator (Section 4.1, p.42).

Four front panel keys are directional in the menus: scroll left or right to move between menu groups on the same level, then move down to the sub-menu or parameter wanted; the present value displays as you move through parameters (Section 1.7, p.11).
To change a parameter value, scroll left or right to view its values; when the desired value displays, press Tare to select it and move back up one level (Section 1.7, p.11).

Editing numeric values: use the navigation keys to select the digit and to increment or decrement its value, then press to save and return to the level above. Numbers can also be edited directly with the numeric keypad — but the decimal point must match the primary units formatting or the number may be rejected (Section 1.7, p.11).

keys.does: Powers the unit on and off. If power mode is set to manual, the Power key must be used; if power mode is set to auto, the unit powers on when plugged in and can only be turned off by unplugging it (Table 1-1, p.9).

Sets the current gross weight to zero, provided the amount of weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion; the zero band defaults to 2% of full scale and can be configured up to 100%. Also used as the move-up key for menu levels and to increment a number when editing.

Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Configuration menu (kg, g, lb, oz, tn or t). Also used as the scroll-left key in menus and to toggle to another digit when editing a value. Units cannot be changed once a group weighment has been started (p.11).

Sends an on-demand print format out the serial port, provided the conditions for standstill are met; PRINT may display while printing. Also used as the scroll-right key in menus and to toggle to another digit when editing.
In the menus, Tare is the select/confirm key: when the desired parameter value displays, press Tare to select the value and move back up one level (Section 1.7, p.11).
The Menu key (also simulated by the KMENU EDP command) works the menu functions of the front panel in configuration and weigh mode (Table 6-1, p.47).

During a numeric entry it sets the currently selected digit to 0 and advances one digit to the right. When the indicator is in hold mode it can release a held weight and return to live weighing (Table 1-1, p.9).
Enters numeric values directly — such as the head count of animals on the scale — and can edit numbers as an alternative to the arrow method (Sections 1.7–1.7.1, pp.11–12).

Applies the entered head count value (Section 1.8.5, p.13): the number of animals on the scale, typed on the numeric keypad, is applied so the ticket can report the count and the average weight per animal. The head count itself is not displayed while weighing.
Applies the input shrinkage value when weighing animals (Section 1.8.4, p.12), so the load total can be reported with the shrink taken out.

Sums the total animal weight previously weighed and the live weight on the scale — the running total as groups of animals are added — and sends the completed load ticket data to the serial port when all groups are done (Section 1.8.6, p.13; p.44). Also used as the down arrow in menus, decrementing a number when editing.

lights.does: The battery icon indicates the level of the battery.

An arrow annunciator (left of the zero annunciator) showing the indicator is in the middle of collecting data from the groups that make up a load. If standby powers the unit down mid-load, this annunciator comes back on at power-up to show the load is still open — the previous group totals were saved (p.44).
The current weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Standstill is required for some operations, including zero, tare and printing.
Displays which unit of measure is being used: lb = pounds, kg = kilograms, g = grams, oz = ounces, t = short tons or metric tons.

ideas.h: A load is built from groups
ideas.text: A load of animals is weighed group by group: each group is weighed and entered, the group number on the ticket increments, and Load Total keeps adding the live weight to what was already weighed until the whole load is complete. Pressing the total key at the end sends the load ticket — and there is no reprint, so the ticket matters.

ideas.h: The load survives a power nap
ideas.text: While groups are being loaded and unloaded, standby can power the indicator down. The group totals are saved, and when it powers back up the Transaction in Process arrow lights to say the load is still open and waiting.

ideas.h: Standstill is the gatekeeper
ideas.text: Zero, tare and printing all require the scale to be at standstill, inside its motion band. If animals are still moving, those keys simply wait — the light says the reading can be trusted.

ideas.h: Shrink comes out at the end
ideas.text: The shrink factor is applied to the load: a 15,000 lb total group weight with a 2.0 shrink factor prints as 14,700 lb total group weight with shrink. The ticket shows both the live totals and the shrunk result.

ideas.h: Units freeze once a group starts
ideas.text: The alternate unit can be toggled from the front panel, but not in the middle of a job: once a group weighment has been started, units cannot be changed.

pre.short: The confirm key in configuration — selects the displayed value and moves back up one level.
Zeroes the scale inside the zero range when it is not in motion; menu up / increment key.
Sends the ticket out the serial port when standstill conditions are met.
Types values directly — head counts, WVAL test weight values, and parameter numbers.
Works the panel menus; configuration itself starts at the switch on the back of the unit.
Must be lit before zero, tare, or printing will happen — let the load settle.

482.intro: The 482 front panel is a large six-digit LCD with a seven-button keypad (18-button full numeric keypad on the 482 Plus). The keys work the scale in weigh mode and double as menu navigation keys in setup, with TARE serving as Enter (pp.8, 12).
menus: The Menu key allows front panel access to user setup and configuration mode (p.12).

Four front panel keys work as directional keys: Unit and Print scroll left and right on the same menu level, while Zero and Gross/Net move up and down to different menu levels. The Tare key serves as an Enter key for selecting parameter values within the menus (p.12).

To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the desired menu group displays, then move down to the desired sub-menu or parameter. When moving through the menu parameters, the present value displays (p.12).
To change a parameter value, scroll left or right to view the values for that parameter; when the desired value displays, press Tare to select the value and move back up one level (p.12).

To edit numerical values, use the navigation keys to select the digit and to increment or decrement its value, then press Tare (Enter) to save the value entered and return to the level above (p.12). On the 482 Plus, numeric values can be typed on the numeric keypad instead (p.13).

keys.does: Turns the unit on/off. If power mode is set to manual, the Power key must be used to turn the unit on and off; if power mode is set to auto, the unit powers on when plugged in and can only be turned off by unplugging power.
The Menu key is used to access the User Setup menu, and allows front panel access to user setup and configuration mode.

Sets the current gross weight to zero, provided the amount of weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band is defaulted to 2% of full scale but can be configured for up to 100% of full scale. Also used as a move up key to navigate to different menu levels or to increment a number when editing a value.

Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Configuration menu (kg, g, lb, oz, tn, or t). Also used as a scroll left key to navigate to different menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.

Sends an on-demand print format out the serial port, provided the conditions for standstill are met; PRINT may be displayed while printing. Also used as a scroll right key to navigate to different menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.

Performs one of several predetermined tare functions dependent on the mode of operation selected in the TAREFN parameter. Also acts as an Enter key for numeric or parameter entry: in numeric editing, pressing Tare saves the value entered and returns to the level above.

Switches the display mode from gross to net, or from net to gross. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. Gross mode shows the Gross/Brutto annunciator; net mode shows the Net annunciator. Also used as a move down key to navigate to different menu levels or to decrement a number when editing a value.
On the 482 Plus, the numeric keypad is used to enter numeric values directly, relying on the numbers embossed on the keypad rather than using the navigation arrows.

lights.does: Gross weight display mode (or Brutto in OIML mode).
Net weight display mode.

The Center of Zero annunciator indicates that the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or is within the center of zero band. A display division is the resolution of the displayed weight value, or the smallest incremental increase or decrease which can be displayed or printed.
Scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare and printing, can only be done when the standstill annunciator is on.
Indicates a push-button tare weight has been acquired and stored in memory.
Indicates that a preset tare weight has been keyed in or entered and stored in memory. When a preset tare is entered, the display changes to Net mode and the PT annunciator lights.
Displays which unit of measure is being used: lb = pounds, kg = kilograms, g = grams, oz = ounces, t = for either short tons and metric tons.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: GROSS/NET switches the display between gross and net. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare, so the net reading is what the load itself weighs after the container comes off.

ideas.h: No standstill, no zero, tare, or print
ideas.text: The Standstill annunciator says the scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band, and some operations, including zero, tare and printing, can only be done when it is on. If one of those keys seems to ignore you, check for this annunciator first.

ideas.h: Center of zero is a quarter-division promise
ideas.text: The Center of Zero annunciator means the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band. It is the display's way of saying the empty scale is truly sitting on its zero point, not just close.

ideas.h: TARE is the Enter key in menus
ideas.text: The front panel does double duty: Unit and Print scroll left and right, Zero and Gross/Net move up and down, and Tare serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values. In numeric editing, Tare saves the value entered and returns to the level above, so finishing an entry always ends with the same key.

ideas.h: Zero lives inside a band
ideas.text: ZERO sets the current gross weight to zero provided the weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band is defaulted to 2% of full scale but can be configured for up to 100% of full scale, so the same indicator can be strict or generous about what counts as zero.

pre.short: This is the Enter key: it selects values in menus and saves a number you edited.
Zeros the scale inside its zero range; in menus it moves up and raises a digit.
Prints only when standstill conditions are met; in menus it scrolls right.
Opens user setup and configuration from the front panel.
Zero, tare, and print only work when this is on — let the scale settle first.

520.intro: The 520 has a 5-button keypad, a seven-digit 14-segment vacuum fluorescent display, a two-character dot-matrix annunciator field, and a 16-character prompt field. The symbols over the keys describe their setup-mode directions: up, down, enter, left, right.
menus: The 520 has four modes: normal (weighing) mode, setup mode, test mode, and front panel setup mode. Normal mode displays gross or net weight with the secondary display showing scale status (Section 1.1, p.8).

To enter setup mode, remove the large fillister head screw from the enclosure backplate, insert a screwdriver into the access hole, and press the setup switch once; the display shows CONFIG. Setup mode menus include CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT, SETPTS, DIG IN, ALGOUT, and VERSION (Table 3-1, p.24). Test mode is entered by holding the setup switch until the display shows TEST.

Front panel setup mode is entered by holding the UNITS key for three seconds; it changes setpoint and/or checkweigh values and sets time and date. Some configurations require a password or do not allow changes (Section 1.3.8, p.10).

In setup mode four keys are directional: UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between levels, and TARE serves as the Enter key. A label over each key identifies its direction (Section 3.1.3, p.24).

keys.does: Zeroes the scale: in gross mode, remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, then press ZERO; the center of zero annunciator lights to show the scale is zeroed (p.9). In setup mode it moves up between menu levels.

Toggles the display between gross and net mode; gross is shown as Gr (or Br for Brutto in OIML mode) and net as Nt on the secondary display. When piece count mode is enabled, this key (MODE) toggles between Gross/Net/Piece Count.
Tare key. In setup mode the TARE key serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values within the menus.

Scrolls left on the same menu level in setup mode. Holding UNITS for three seconds enters front panel setup mode for setpoints, checkweigh values, and time and date (p.10). In count mode, SAMPLE (UNITS) enters sample acquisition mode.
Print key; scrolls right on the same menu level in setup mode. In count display mode, PRINT sends the CFMT print format data string to the serial port.

lights.does: The letters Gr on the secondary display indicate gross mode (Br for Brutto in OIML mode).
The letters Nt on the secondary display indicate net mode.
Lights to indicate the scale is zeroed after ZERO is pressed at no load.
Standstill annunciator on the secondary display; the book's zero and tare procedures wait for it to light before pressing keys.
Two-digit annunciator shows the units of the displayed value: lb=pounds, kg=kilograms, oz=ounces, T=short tons, t=metric tons, LT=long tons, g=grams, GN=grains, or PC in count mode.

ideas.h: A five-key panel that points the way
ideas.text: In setup mode, labels over the keys show directions: UNITS/PRINT go left and right on a level, ZERO and GROSS/NET move between levels, and TARE is Enter. The same five keys run the scale in weigh mode and drive the menus in setup mode.

ideas.h: Setup is behind a screw
ideas.text: Configuration and calibration require setup mode, entered by pressing the setup switch through the backplate access hole — the display shows CONFIG. Holding the switch longer (about three seconds) enters test mode instead, which shows TEST then A/DTST.

ideas.h: Wait for standstill, then zero
ideas.text: The basic procedures follow a rhythm: remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, then press the key. The center of zero annunciator lighting confirms the zero took.

ideas.h: One key, three displays
ideas.text: With piece count enabled, the MODE (GROSS/NET) key cycles between gross, net, and piece count. In count display mode the annunciator shows PC, and parts counting needs a sample: the indicator shows Addnnn, counts the sample (–CNT–), then displays the part quantity.

pre.short: Enter key in setup menus; panel tare key in weigh mode.
Zeroes at no load once standstill lights; menu up key.
Menu left key; hold 3 seconds for front panel setup mode.
Menu right key; prints the ticket format.
Wait for it before zeroing or taring.

550/570.intro: The 550/570 panel has a large six-digit numeric display with a smaller two-line 10-character dot matrix display to the right of it. The same keypad matrix is used on the U.S. 550 and 570 and the 550i, with some keys differing between the 550 and 570, such as PRINT and ENTER on the 550 and the dual PRINT/ENTER and SAMPLE keys on the 570.
menus: Some keys have additional functions when in the Setup Mode, and the front panel keys take on a different function depending on which indicator, 550 or 570, is selected and depending on which mode is selected. Chapter 5 defines the front panel key operation for the Weigh Mode.

During Setup text entry, the character programmed at the current location is shown in the lower rightmost position of the dot matrix display, with preceding characters shown ahead of it on the second and first lines. Press TARE when the desired character is displayed to shift the chosen character to the left and start the next character as an A, press UNITS to backup through the setup if required, and press ENTER when the text entry is complete to store the data.

In the Custom Transmit Setup, special characters are used for parameters, control codes, ASCII extended codes and the end of the table, and they may be expanded to clarify their use by pressing the PRINT key. ASCII Control Codes (0 to 31) and Extended Codes (128 to 255) can only be programmed by keying in a decimal number, entered as a decimal point plus a three digit decimal number followed by ENTER, for example .090 ENTER for the letter Z.

A variation to the SELECT command, * SELECT, will cause the unit to exit the ID mode if it is currently in an ID mode. The <CR> received via RS-232 acts the same as the front panel ENTER key if the 550 is in an ID mode, such as ID 1-6 data entry, Truck in/out weighing, macro menu or database menu, or if a macro is executing.

To abort the Remote Display operation of the 450 and re-enter the setup mode, press ZERO + SELECT simultaneously and enter the standard 450 access code SELECT ZERO PRINT UNITS TARE. Go to parameter P160 to change the unit back to a standard 450 configuration and key in 9990 ENTER.

Press to enter, store and use the ID parameters. Six identification names can be created to describe part numbers, bin locations, or information titles for your weighing operation.

lights.does: The last three characters of the upper dot matrix line indicate a CENTER ZERO condition when applicable, shown as -->O<--.
The first two characters of the upper dot matrix line will show the weighing units of the displayed data.
The lower line of the dot matrix display will specify Gross when the type of data displayed is Gross.
The lower line of the dot matrix display will specify Net when the type of data displayed is Net.
The lower line of the dot matrix display will specify Tare when the type of data displayed is Tare.

ideas.h: Big numbers, small explainer
ideas.text: The six large numeric digits are used to display numeric data, such as Gross Weight, Net Weight or Tare Weight. The dot matrix display to the right explains that number, typically showing the weighing units in the first two characters of the upper line, the -->O<-- center zero symbol in the last three characters, and the type of data such as Gross, Net or Tare on the lower line, and it is also used for specific messages during operation and setup.

ideas.h: Same keys, different job by mode
ideas.text: The front panel keys take on a different function depending on which indicator, 550 or 570, is selected, and they also take on a different function depending on which mode is selected. Additional scale input boards must be installed and enabled for proper use of the scale select operation, such as scale #1 41 SELECT through scale #4 44 SELECT.

ideas.h: Tare can survive power loss
ideas.text: Determine whether or not you want to save the tare weight value upon power-down, and this feature will prove valuable in applications such as tank weighing because if power is removed while the tank contains material, the net value will not be lost if the unit is set for Tare Saved. The Tare rounding parameter will select whether or not the Tare Weight will be rounded off for calculations, and if the application must be NIST approved this must be set to P163.00 which guarantees that Net + Tare = Gross.

ideas.h: % is a command character
ideas.text: The 550 treats the percent % character as a special character, and whenever the unit receives a percent, the next character is flagged to be processed as a command, so if a percent is to be literally entered two percent characters must be entered. If the character following a percent is not defined as a command the unit will display the message Entry Error for one second, and macros can perform the same operations as any front panel key operation, such as ZERO, TARE, PRINT, etc.

ideas.h: Input waits during macros
ideas.text: Keypad and serial port inputs are not processed during macros, except during macro commands which specifically look for operator input. Any data entered through either of these inputs will be buffered, or saved, until the macro either looks for operator input or the macro completes.
