60 Series.name: 60 Series
60 Series.intro: The 60 Series Weigh Mode is the primary operating mode when the instrument is connected to a scale platform or load cell, and the standard keypad keys take different functions depending on the operating mode. All models have an elastomeric keypad; the book describes a 5-key front panel on the 460, a 22-key keypad on the 560 Series, and a 28-key keypad on the 660 Series, with display options ranging from a 6-digit 7-segment display with dot matrix to graphic LCD/VFD displays.
menus: Setup is accessed on the 460 keypad with the [ZERO] + [SELECT] combination, shown in the Appendix A key-combination table as Access Setup in Gross, Net, Quantity and Weigh modes. When a replacement main board makes the keypad style mismatch P450, the book says you cannot use the conventional method to access setup; instead you hold keys down at power-up to automatically configure P450, holding until "M460 Keypd" (or "M560 Keypd" on the 560 procedure) is displayed, then release.
In a menu, [ENTER] is used to finish and keep the change in the contrast example: press [ENTER] to exit the menu and permanently store the new contrast setting.
For macros, press [ENTER] to execute the displayed macro. In the macro-table example, press [ENTER] to clear the macro table, or press [CLR] to cancel the deletion.

If a macro locks up from an uncleared received character, press [CLR] + [SELECT] to invoke the macro abort menu, choose the suspend macro option to stop execution, then press [CLR] + [SELECT] again and choose resume macro after correcting the problem.

While picking a setup parameter or instance, the book's setup notes say the [UNITS] key will execute the [F2] key function to provide more feedback, and [UNITS] is used to increment through available setup script files. The extract sentence for the matching decrement key is truncated, so no complete scroll pair is claimed here.

keys.does: Press [ZERO] to zero the current quantity/weight reading. In quantity mode it sets the current mode to a gross zero quantity; in weigh mode it sets the current mode to Gross Weight. It is also assignable at P801 as Enabled or to invoke Macro 1 through 15 instead of its standard function.

In quantity mode pressing [UNITS] has no effect. In weigh mode it toggles the display through the available units selections for the selected scale; each scale keeps its own units selection, restored when that scale is selected again. To change a non-selected scale, key the units selection, a decimal point and the scale number, then press [ENTER].

The [SELECT] key function is set at P800 as Enabled or assigned to Macro 1 through 15. In the macro table it is predefined as command %s at P800. On the 460 5-key panel, [ZERO] + [SELECT] accesses Setup.

The [TARE] key function is set at P802 as Enabled or assigned to Macro 1 through 15, with macro command %t at P802. On the 460, the combined [TARE / ENTER] key performs TARE in Gross, Net and Quantity modes and ENTER in Weigh and Setup modes.
The [SCALE SELECT] key function is set at P804 as Enabled or assigned to a macro. On the 460 combination table, [TARE] + [SELECT] performs Scale Select.

The [PRINT] key function is set at P805 as Enabled or assigned to Macro 1 through 15. In the macro table it is predefined as command %p at P805. On the 460, the [PRINT] key alone performs PRINT in Gross, Net and Quantity modes.

On the Alpha Keypad, when the keyed data looks correct, press the ENTER key in the lower right corner to confirm the entry; this transmits the Enter command %e to the Process Controller. The book also uses [ENTER] to execute a displayed macro and to exit a menu while permanently storing the new setting.

The [CLEAR] / [CLR] key function is assignable as Enabled or to a macro, with macro command %c at P808. Press [CLR] to cancel a macro-table deletion, and press [CLR] + [SELECT] to open the macro abort menu.

The [0] through [9] keys are each listed as a Key Function that can be Enabled or assigned to Macro 1 through 15 at P810 through P819. In the macro assignment table they carry ASCII values 48 through 57.

The [ID] key function selections vary by model: 0=None, 1=Menu, 2=Database, 3=Menu & Database, or Macro assignment, with 251=Alpha on the listed series. In the macro table ID/Alpha is predefined as command %i at P806.

lights.does: When the controller is at Center-of-Zero, the international center-of-zero symbol appears on the top line of the dot matrix display. It does not display if the name of a Custom Unit is greater than two characters, and with lb/oz units the upper line is used to show units so there is no center zero symbol.

ideas.h: Keys change with the mode you are in
ideas.text: Weigh Mode is the main working mode with a scale or load cell attached, but it is not the only mode. The book opens the keypad section by saying the standard keys assume different functions depending on the operating mode, so the same key can zero, enter, clear or move you in setup according to where you are.

ideas.h: Units belong to each scale, not just the box
ideas.text: The Units key does not set one global unit for the whole instrument. Each scale has its own units selection, the key only affects the selected scale, and switching to another scale brings back whatever units were in effect the last time that scale was selected.

ideas.h: Almost any key can be turned into a macro key
ideas.text: Any key on the front panel can be used to invoke a macro. Function keys and [START], [STOP] and [SETUP] are predefined, while other keys can be redefined at P800 through P820 to run a chosen macro instead of their original job, which is how the keypad gets completely customized for an application.

ideas.h: A mismatched keypad locks you out of normal setup
ideas.text: All indicators ship with the keypad configured, but a replacement main board may not match the connected keypad style. When that happens the keypad will not work correctly and you cannot use the normal setup route to change P450, so the book has you hold keys at power-up to make the board configure itself to the keypad that is actually attached.

ideas.h: The Alpha Keypad is an add-on typer for the 663
ideas.text: The optional Alpha Keypad for GSE 663 controllers complements the standard keypad instead of replacing it. Its 35 keys are laid out A to Z to make alphabetic data entry and programming easier: type capitals directly, hold the lower-case shift for lower case, and hold 2nd with a key for the gray ASCII character printed on that key.

680.intro: The 680 Synergy Plus front panel has a seven-segment display with seven 0.8-inch digits, 19 flat membrane buttons (six primary scale function buttons, a numeric keypad, and a power button), and eight LED annunciators that tell you what kind of weight value you are looking at.
menus: Weigh mode is the default mode: the indicator shows gross or net weight and uses the annunciators to show scale status. Press the Menu key to open user mode, which shows the audit, accumulator, tare, and version menus.
Most procedures in the book, including calibration, require setup mode. The Menu key can also be set up to open setup mode parameters (Section 4.1, p.34).
Inside menus the scale keys double as arrows: ZERO moves up, GROSS/NET moves down, UNITS moves left, PRINT moves right. TARE works as the enter key for numeric or parameter entry.
To leave a numeric entry, use CLEAR to clear the current value or the selected digit in an alphanumeric entry.

keys.does: Turns the unit on and off. If the unit is on, press and hold for eight seconds to turn it off; if it is off, press and hold for two seconds to turn it on.
Opens user mode (audit, accumulator, tare, and version menus). It can also be set up to open setup mode parameters (Section 4.1, p.34).

Sets the current gross weight to zero, as long as the weight to be added or removed is within the zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band defaults to 1.9% of full scale and can be configured up to 100%. In menus it works as the up key.
Switches the weight display to the alternate unit defined in the Configuration menu (kg, g, lb, oz, tn, or t). In menus it works as the left key, or to move to another digit when editing a value.

Sends the on-demand print format out the configured port (RS232-1 is the default print port), provided the standstill conditions are met. In menus it works as the right key, or to move to another digit when editing a value.
Performs one of several predetermined tare functions depending on the TARE FN parameter, and also acts as the enter key for numeric or parameter entry.
Switches the display between gross and net mode. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. In menus it works as the down key.
Clears the current value in a numeric entry, or clears the currently selected digit in an alphanumeric entry.
Types numbers directly. It is used, for example, to key in a preset tare weight, which is then accepted with TARE; the Net LED and PT LED light to confirm the preset tare was entered.

lights.does: Lit when the display is showing gross weight (Brutto in OIML mode).
Lit when the display is showing net weight (gross weight minus tare).

Lit when the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band. A display division is the smallest weight change that can be displayed.
Lit when the scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare, and print, can only be done when this LED is on.
Shows which unit is on the display: pounds (lb) or kilograms (kg). If the configured units are not lb/kg, lb lights for the primary unit and kg for the secondary unit.
A push-button tare weight has been acquired and stored in memory.
A preset (keyed-in) tare weight has been entered and stored in memory.

ideas.h: Three modes: weigh, user, setup
ideas.text: Weigh mode is the everyday mode and is where the indicator starts. User mode (Menu key) holds audit, accumulator, tare, and version information. Setup mode is where configuration and calibration live, and most service procedures require it.

ideas.h: Standstill means you can trust it
ideas.text: The Standstill LED is lit only when the scale is settled within its motion band. Zero, tare, and print are blocked unless the scale is at standstill, so the light is the scale's way of saying the reading is steady enough to act on.

ideas.h: Net is just gross minus tare
ideas.text: The GROSS/NET key switches between the full weight on the scale (gross) and what is left after a stored tare is taken away (net). The Gross/Brutto and Net LEDs always tell you which one you are looking at.

ideas.h: Zero has a range, not just a point
ideas.text: The ZERO key only works if the weight to be added or removed is inside the zero range and the scale is not moving. The band defaults to 1.9% of full scale and can be set as high as 100% of capacity.

ideas.h: Center of zero, in plain terms
ideas.text: A display division is the smallest step the display can show. The Center of Zero LED lights when the reading is within a quarter of one of those small steps (±0.25 divisions) of true zero.

Zeroes the scale within the zero range when it is not in motion; also the menu up key.
Prints when standstill is met; also the menu right key.

680HE.name: 680HE
680HE.intro: The 680HE front panel is a seven-segment display with six 2.5-inch digits, 18 flat membrane tactile buttons — six primary scale function buttons plus a numeric keypad — and eight LED annunciators for units and scale functions (Section 3.0, p.20).
menus: Weigh mode is the default mode: the indicator displays gross or net weight, using the annunciators to indicate scale status and the type of weight value displayed (Section 1.3, p.8).
User mode is reached with the Menu key and displays the audit, accumulator, tare and version menus. The Menu key can also be set up to access setup mode parameters (Section 4.1, p.27).
Setup mode is where configuration and calibration live: most procedures in the book, including calibration, require the indicator to be in setup mode (Section 1.3, p.8; Section 4.0, p.27).

Inside menus the scale keys double as arrows: ZERO moves up, GROSS/NET moves down, UNITS moves left, PRINT moves right, and TARE acts as the enter key for numeric or parameter entry. CLEAR clears the current value in a numeric entry or the selected digit in an alphanumeric entry (Table 3-1, p.20).

keys.does: Accesses user mode, which displays the audit, accumulator, tare and version menus; it can also be set up to access setup mode parameters (Section 4.1, p.27).

Sets the current gross weight to zero, provided the amount of weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion; the zero band defaults to 1.9% of full scale but can be configured up to 100%. Also used as the up key to navigate menus.

Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Configuration menu (kg, g, lb, oz, tn or t). Also used as the left key to navigate menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.

Sends the on-demand print format out the configured port, provided the conditions for standstill are met; RS-232 Port 1 (RS232-1) is the default print port. Also used as the right key to navigate menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.
Performs one of several predetermined tare functions depending on the mode of operation selected in the TAREFN parameter. Also acts as an enter key for numeric or parameter entry.

Switches the display mode from gross to net or from net to gross; if a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. Also used as the down key to navigate menus.
Clears the current value in a numeric entry, or clears the currently selected digit in an alphanumeric entry.

Types numbers directly — for example, keying in a preset tare weight with the numeric keypad and pressing TARE; the display changes to net weight and the Net and PT LEDs light, confirming the preset tare was entered (p.23).

lights.does: Gross weight display mode (called Brutto in OIML mode) — the whole weight on the scale.
Net weight display mode — gross weight with the stored tare taken away.

The current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band. A display division is the smallest weight change that can be displayed or printed.
Scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare and print, can only be done when the standstill LED is on.

Displays which unit of measure is being used. The lb and kg LEDs act as primary and secondary units annunciators; if neither configured unit is lb or kg, lb lights for the primary unit and kg for the secondary.

ideas.h: Three modes: weigh, user, setup
ideas.text: Weigh mode is the home mode. The Menu key opens user mode (audit, accumulator, tare, version). Setup mode holds configuration and calibration, and most service procedures — calibration included — require it.

ideas.h: Standstill means you can trust it
ideas.text: The Standstill LED lights only when the scale has settled inside its motion band. Zero, tare and print are refused until it is on, so the LED is the scale's word that the reading is steady.

ideas.h: Net is just gross minus tare
ideas.text: TARE stores a weight; the display can then show what remains after that weight is taken away (net) or everything on the scale (gross). The Gross/Brutto or Net LED always tells you which one you are reading.

ideas.h: Zero works inside a band
ideas.text: ZERO will only take if the weight to be added or removed is inside the zero range and the scale is not moving. The band defaults to 1.9% of full scale and can be opened up to 100%.

ideas.h: Center of zero, in small steps
ideas.text: One display division is the smallest step the display can show. The Center of Zero LED lights when the reading is within a quarter of one of those steps of the zero the scale was given — as close to zero as the display can prove.

Zeroes the scale inside the zero range when it is not in motion; menu up key.
Prints when standstill conditions are met; menu right key.

682.intro: The 682 front panel has dedicated buttons for power, menu, zero, units, print, tare, gross/net, and clear, plus configurable softkeys shown at the bottom of the display and pressed with the physical key directly below each label (p.29). The same buttons double as menu arrows, and annunciators on the display tell you the weighing mode and whether the scale is steady.
menus: Press the Menu button to access User mode. The Menu button can also be set up to access Setup mode parameters, which is where configuration and softkey setup live (p.29).
Inside menus, ZERO moves up and GROSS/NET moves down to different menu levels, while UNITS moves left and PRINT moves right on the same menu level (p.29).
TARE acts as the Enter key: use it to take a numeric value or select a parameter value you have dialed in (p.29).
When editing a value, UNITS and PRINT toggle to another digit, and CLEAR clears the current value in a numeric entry or the selected digit in an alphanumeric entry (p.29).
Configured softkeys sit at the bottom of the display. If six or more softkeys are enabled, left and right arrows appear in the outside softkeys to page between the available softkeys (p.77).

keys.does: Turns the unit ON/OFF: if the unit is on, press and hold for eight seconds to turn it off; if off, press and hold for two seconds to turn it on.
Used to access User mode. It can also be set up to access Setup mode parameters.

Sets the current gross weight to zero, provided the weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band defaults to 1.9% of full scale and can be configured up to 100%. Also used as the up button to navigate menus.

Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Configuration menu (kg, g, lb, oz, tn or t). Also used as the left button to navigate menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.

Sends an on-demand print format out the configured port, provided the conditions for standstill are met; RS-232 Port 1 is the default print port. Also used as the right button to navigate menus or to toggle to another digit when editing a value.
Performs one of several predetermined tare functions depending on the mode of operation selected in the TARE FN parameter. Also acts as an enter button for numeric or parameter entry.

Switches the display mode from gross to net, or from net to gross. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. Used as the down button to navigate menus.
Clears the current value in a numeric entry, or clears the currently selected digit in an alphanumeric entry.

Configurable softkeys that can be set to perform a variety of operator functions, selected with the physical key directly below the label on the display. Up to 15 softkeys can be configured, including Time/Date, Display Tare, Setpoint, batch controls, and Print Accumulator.

lights.does: Displays at the left side of the numeric weight area when the indicator is in gross weight display mode.
Displays at the left side of the numeric weight area when the indicator is in net weight display mode.

Indicates the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or is within the center of zero band. A display division is the smallest increase or decrease that can be displayed or printed.
Indicates the scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare and print, can only be done when the standstill annunciator is displayed.
Tare annunciator: indicates a push-button tare weight has been acquired and stored in memory.
Preset Tare annunciator: indicates a preset tare weight has been keyed in or entered and stored in memory.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: Gross is everything on the scale. When a tare value has been entered or acquired, net is what is left after the tare comes off: the net value is the gross weight minus the tare. GROSS/NET flips the display between the two, and the GROSS or NET annunciator tells you which one you are looking at.

ideas.h: Steady first, then zero, tare, or print
ideas.text: The standstill annunciator means the scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare and print, can only be done when that annunciator is displayed, so a moving scale will refuse those keys until it settles.

ideas.h: Zero only works inside the zero band
ideas.text: ZERO sets the current gross weight to zero only when the weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band defaults to 1.9% of full scale, but can be configured for up to 100% of full scale, so a scale that will not zero is often just outside its band.

ideas.h: Softkeys are assigned, not fixed
ideas.text: The softkey row is not one fixed set of buttons: up to 15 softkeys can each be assigned an operator function such as Time/Date, Display Accumulator, Setpoint, Batch Start, or Print Accumulator, and a blank softkey can be used just to create separation between other softkeys.

Zeros the scale inside its zero band; in menus it is the Up arrow.
In menus it moves left and hops to the next digit when you edit a value.
Prints when the scale is steady; in menus it moves right and hops digits.

720i.name: 720i
720i.intro: The 720i universal front panel is a 22-button keypad with an LCD display: four configurable softkeys, four scale function/navigation keys, Menu and Print/Enter keys, and numeric entry keys (the panel mount has a 10-button keypad). It runs in two modes, Weigh Mode and Setup Mode (p.10).
menus: The indicator has two modes of operation, Weigh Mode and Setup Mode. Press the Menu key to show the system menu, and press Menu again to exit the menu structure; while editing a parameter value, Menu functions as Cancel (pp.10, 35).
In setup mode, Units and Tare scroll left and right (horizontally) on the same menu level, while Zero and Gross/Net move up and down (vertically) to different menu levels (p.35).

To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the desired menu group appears, then move down to the desired submenu or parameter. The Print key serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values (p.35).

When moving through menu parameters, the default or previously selected value appears first on the display (p.35). When moving through values below the first menu level, the display can be returned to the level above, and from there to the next parameter on the level above (p.35).

Softkey assignments are listed on the tabs at the bottom of the LCD and are activated by pressing the arrow keys below the tabs. For applications with more than three defined softkeys, a More... key is automatically assigned to the fourth softkey position to toggle between groups of softkeys (p.13).

keys.does: Sets the current gross weight to zero. Also used as the Up key to navigate menus or to edit a value.
Performs a predetermined tare function. Also used as the Left key to navigate menus or to edit a value; in a submenu of Advance Truck Mode, Tare goes back to the previous menu.
Indicates whether the weight value is in Net or Gross mode. Also used as the Down key to navigate menus or to edit a value.
Switches the weight display to an alternate unit. Also used as the Right key to navigate menus or to edit a value.

Sends an on-demand print format out a communications port, provided the conditions for standstill are met. In setup mode the Print key also serves as an Enter key for selecting parameter values within the menus.
Accesses and exits the menu structure. Functions as a Cancel key when editing a parameter value; press it to show the system menu.

Configurable softkeys provide additional operator functions. Assignments are listed on the tabs at the bottom of the LCD display and are activated by pressing the arrow keys below the tabs; examples are Time/Date, Display Tare, Display Accum, Weigh In/Out, Setpoint, and Batch Start/Stop/Pause/Reset.
Works as a backspace when entering numbers or letters.
Inserts a decimal point as needed when entering values.

lights.does: The display marks the weight as gross; the Gross/Net key indicates whether the weight value is in Net or Gross mode, and Advance Mode displays show the weight with a G (for example, 12880 G).
The display shows the weight in net mode when a tare is in effect; the Gross/Net key indicates whether the weight value is in Net or Gross mode.

The indicator displays gross, net, or tare weights as required to indicate scale status and the type of weight value displayed, so a tare weight shown on the display is the stored tare being reviewed.

ideas.h: The same keys steer the menus
ideas.text: In setup, four front-panel keys become directional keys: Units and Tare scroll left and right on the same menu level, Zero and Gross/Net move up and down to different menu levels, and Print serves as the Enter key. Learning the arrows once means the whole menu tree moves the same way everywhere.

ideas.h: Last Zero calibrates around a loaded scale
ideas.text: The calibration softkeys include Last Zero, which recalls the last established zero value to allow calibration without removing test weights or product from the scale. It exists for the real-world case where the scale cannot be emptied before recalibration.

ideas.h: Five points make the line straighter
ideas.text: Five-point linearization using the WLIN parameter provides increased scale accuracy by calibrating the indicator at up to five additional points, instead of trusting one zero and one span point to describe the whole range.

ideas.h: TARE and ZERO change with the legal mode
ideas.text: The function of the front panel TARE and ZERO keys depends on the REGULAT parameter: in NTEP mode, for example, ZERO with a positive weight and a tare in system does one thing, while OIML can make the same keypress clear the tare as well. The same key can legitimately behave differently on two indicators set to different regulatory modes.

pre.short: In setup this is your Enter key — it selects the parameter value; in weigh mode it prints when the scale is steady.
Zeros the gross weight; in menus it is the Up arrow between levels.
Takes the tare; in menus it scrolls left and can back you out of a submenu.
Gets you into and out of the menu structure, and cancels an edit without taking the value.
During calibration the Calibrate softkey is what captures each calibration point.

720i.refs: References: Rice Lake 720i Programmable HMI Indicator/Controller (Doc 103121): Front Panel and modes Section 2.0 p.10, Softkey Operations Sections 2.3-2.4 pp.13, Menu Navigation Section 4.2.1 p.35, Front Panel Calibration Section 5.2 p.61, TARE/ZERO regulatory functions Section 12.2 p.116.

748.intro: The 748 is a Cardinal weight indicating instrument with a six-digit display, a 30-element bar graph, and a full keypad: ON/ZERO, OFF, GROSS, TARE (two keys — blue to view, red to enter), NET, PRINT, ENTER, numeric keys, TIME-DATE, lb/kg, PRESET, BAR, and TEST.
menus: Setup and calibration are worked as a prompt-by-prompt conversation: the display shows a prompt, pressing ENTER displays the current stored value, and pressing ENTER again keeps it. To change a value, type the new value with the numeric keys and press ENTER to save it.
Yes and no prompts are answered with the number keys: press the 1 key to change a display to YES (or on) and the 0 key to change it back to no (or oFF), then press ENTER.
During calibration or review, pressing the PRINT key will step to the bAUd? prompt, moving you through the sequence.

At power-up the 748 runs a display test, then shows the four calibration numbers (C1, C2, C3, and C4) in sequence. Copy these numbers down after calibration and keep them in a safe place — they can restore the calibration later.

keys.does: Performs two functions: pressing it when the 748 is off applies power; pressing it when the 748 is on immediately zeroes the weight display, up to the limit (4% or 100% of capacity) selected during setup and calibration.
Pressing this key turns the 748 off.
The GROSS key returns the weight display to the Gross Weight mode and turns the Gross annunciator on. Pressing it before ENTER can also store the current gross weight as a new tare value.

There are two TARE keys: the top (blue) key momentarily displays the stored tare value, and the red key enters a new tare. If push button tare is enabled, the red key stores the current gross weight as tare and switches to net; otherwise it displays the current tare, which can be kept with ENTER or replaced by keying in a new value and pressing ENTER.
Pressing the NET key enters the Net Weight Display mode and turns the Net annunciator on. If a valid tare weight has not been entered, the 748 ignores this command.

Initiates transmission of weight data via the printer output port. The 748 will not respond unless the weight display is stable and not less than zero; in gross it prints gross only, in net it prints gross, tare, and net. During calibration or review it steps to the bAUd? prompt.
The confirm key everywhere: displays the currently stored value at a prompt, saves a value typed with the numeric keys, and advances to the next prompt or preset.
Type values such as weights, times, dates, and ID numbers. At yes/no prompts, the 1 key means YES (on) and the 0 key means no (oFF).
Displays the current time in 24 hour format; press ENTER to display the date, then the consecutive number. Incorrect values can be corrected with the numeric keys and ENTER.

Changes the weighing units to the alternate units selected during setup. With pounds displayed, pressing it changes to kilograms and turns the kg annunciator on; the feature must be enabled during setup.

If the PWC annunciator is off, this key switches the bar graph to preset weight comparator status and turns PWC on. If PWC is on, it opens entry of the target weights: the display shows PSEtx= for each preset, and ENTER walks you through the preset weight and its Trim value.

Controls the 30-element bar graph. If the bar graph is showing preset comparator status (PWC on), BAR returns it to the weight display mode. If PWC is off, BAR lets you enter the bar graph start weight (StArt=) and stop weight (StoP=) that the analog display spans.

lights.does: Turned on when the display is in the Gross Weight mode (turned on by the GROSS key).
Turned on to show that the displayed weight is the net weight — gross weight less tare weight.
Turned on to indicate that the weight is within +/- 1/4 division of the center of zero.

Identified with two small triangle shapes; turned on when the weight display is stable, meaning the change in successive weight samples is less than the motion limits selected during setup and calibration.
Turned on to indicate that the value displayed is the identification number currently in use; it blinks while the consecutive number is displayed, and flashes during truck ID entry.
Used in conjunction with the Truck Storage feature (see the Truck Storage Operation section).
Turned on when the display is showing either the time or the date, and blinks while time or date is being displayed for review.

Turned on to indicate the bar graph elements under the numerals 1 through 8 are being used to show preset weight comparator status. When it is off, the bar graph presents an analog representation of a selected portion of the weight range.

ideas.h: The C numbers are your calibration in your pocket
ideas.text: After calibration, the 748 shows four calibration or 'C' numbers. Write them down: by entering those four numbers later you can return the 748 to its present calibration settings without using test weights. If the EEPROM checksum error CALb appears, recalibration with 'C' numbers or weight is the corrective action.

ideas.h: Stable is not a suggestion
ideas.text: The STABLE annunciator means successive weight samples changed less than the motion limit set in setup. If you try to power up, print, zero, or take a push button tare while motion is present, the display shows UnStb — wait for a stable weight display before performing the operation.

ideas.h: Trim weight makes up for material still falling
ideas.text: Each preset weight comparator has a Trim value. The trim compensates for material in transit: the preset turns on when the displayed weight equals or exceeds the preset weight less its trim, so the shut-off happens early enough to land on target.

ideas.h: One bar graph, two jobs
ideas.text: The 30-element bar graph either draws an analog picture of the weight between a start and stop weight you choose, or — with PWC on — reports the eight preset comparators, lighting the elements under a preset's number when the weight reaches it. The BAR and PRESET keys trade the graph between those jobs.

pre.short: The confirm key: shows the stored value at a prompt, saves what you typed, and steps on.
Turns the 748 on; with it on, zeroes the display up to the setup zero limit.
Blue key views the stored tare; red key enters a new tare (push-button tare if enabled).
Prints when the weight is stable and not negative; steps to bAUd? during calibration or review.
Type values digit by digit; at yes/no prompts 1 means YES and 0 means no.
Two small triangles: when lit the weight is steady enough to zero, tare, or print (else UnStb).

748.refs: References: 748 Weight Indicating Instrument Technical/Operation Manual, Cardinal Scale Manufacturing Co., Doc 8539-M041-O1 Rev H, Specifications and features p. 1, keypad functions and annunciators pp. 31-38, calibration 'C' numbers and analog output calibration Appendix A (p. 41), Truck Storage Operation section.

8140.intro: The Model 8140 has a six-character green-blue vacuum fluorescent display, six keys (Zero, Test, Tare, Clear, LB/KG, Print), and lighted descriptors above the Zero, LB, KG, Gross, Net and Print legends. The same six keys run both normal weighing and the whole setup programming procedure.
menus: Getting in: jumper W2 on the Main PCB must be shorting the two pins to enter setup mode. On most units, press both the TARE and CLEAR keys, then release at the same time; on units in Tables 2 and 3 the setup mode is accessed immediately when W2 is inserted.

Answering prompts: three keys keep the same function throughout the programming procedure. PRINT accepts the data displayed and proceeds to the next step; at value prompts, TEST accepts the selection shown (yes) and TARE steps to the next selectable choice (no).

Backing up or bailing out: ZERO returns the programming routine to the previous step, but will not function during calibration or when the display shows S FILE. CLEAR accepts the data displayed and goes to the last step, which is S FILE.

Typing a test weight: the blank digit to the left is entered first. TARE increments the blanked digit by one unit until the correct value shows, TEST shifts the weight selection to the next position to the right, and PRINT enters the entire display as the value of the test weights used.

Getting out and saving: at [S FILE], TEST retains the programming in memory (W2 must be inserted to save), TARE uses it only until power loss, and CLEAR disregards the changes and keeps the previously stored setup. At [CAL OFF], remove the W2 jumper and place it on just one pin so it will not be misplaced.

keys.does: Provides rezeroing of the scale over a selectable percentage of scale capacity from zero; the Zero key must be depressed for approximately 2 seconds to initiate this function. In setup programming, ZERO returns to the previous step.

Pressing and releasing the Test key causes the display to blank and then sequentially light each segment of all digits and each descriptor, showing that all drivers and displays operate. In setup prompts, TEST is the accept/yes answer for the value shown.

When the Tare key is depressed with weight on the scale and no weight motion present, the tare weight is subtracted from the gross weight to provide a net weight display of zero; if the weight is removed, the tare weight displays as a negative value. In setup, TARE is the no/next-choice answer.
Clears the tare (tare may also be cleared automatically if Automatic Clear is enabled in setup). In setup programming, CLEAR accepts the data displayed and goes to the last step, S FILE.

An alternate action pushbutton for pounds/kilogram selection. When switching, the increment size is adjusted and the decimal point shifted if required; a setup selection can lock the instrument into LB or KG mode and disable this key.
Initiates a print cycle to an external device; the format of the print is programmed by keyboard setup selection. In setup programming, PRINT accepts the display and proceeds to the next step.

lights.does: Illuminated when the instrument is within plus or minus 0.25 increments of the zero increment and there is no motion.
Illuminated when a tare has been entered.
Lights during data transmission to a printer in demand output mode, or when the PRINT key is depressed in continuous mode.
The 8140 illuminates a pointer above the proper legend for the status of the display; the Gross legend pointer shows the displayed weight is gross, before any tare.
There are lighted descriptors above the LB and KG legends, showing which unit the instrument is weighing in; pushbutton LB/KG switching can be disabled in setup.

ideas.h: Same six keys, two jobs
ideas.text: The book prints a comparison chart of the keyboard in normal operation versus operational programming: Zero becomes Previous Step, Test becomes Yes (1), Tare becomes No (0), LB/KG is not used, and Print becomes Enter. In setup you are not learning a new panel, just a second meaning for the same keys.

ideas.h: Motion freezes the keys
ideas.text: Motion detection disables the Zero, Tare and Print functions (step F6, Motion Sensitivity), and the Zero legend itself only lights when the scale is within a quarter increment of zero with no motion. If the keys seem dead, watch for motion before blaming the keyboard.

ideas.h: The jumper is the lock on setup
ideas.text: Jumper W2 must be shorting both pins before the setup mode can be entered, and it must be inserted again at S FILE before new programming is saved to memory. The book recommends parking W2 on just one pin afterward so inadvertent program changes cannot be made.

ideas.h: Warm it up before you calibrate
ideas.text: The calibration procedure begins with a minimum 15-minute warmup before attempting to calibrate the 8140, to stabilize the electronics and allow the load cell to warm up; units that must remain closed during calibration will drift from air currents over the PCB.

pre.short: In setup: accepts the display and goes to the next step (Enter).
In setup: yes — accepts the selection shown.
In setup: no — steps to the next selectable choice.
In setup: back to the previous step; hold 2 seconds to rezero.
In setup: accept and jump to S FILE to save or exit.
Lit at center of zero (within 1/4 increment) with no motion.

8140.refs: References: Toledo 8140 Technical Service Manual — Section V Operating Instructions (display, legends, keyboard), Programming Procedure (setup entry, prompt answers, S FILE), Section I features.

820i.name: 820i
820i.intro: The 820i is a programmable indicator/controller with a 28-button keypad and a large backlit LCD. Instead of a fixed set of labels, five configurable softkeys along the bottom of the display change with the job, next to five primary scale function keys, four navigation keys, and numeric entry keys.
menus: The indicator is configured through menus reached from the front panel in setup mode. The main menus are SCALES, SERIAL, FEATURE, DISPLAY, PFORMT, SETPTS, DIG I/O, ALGOUT (only if an analog output card is installed), and VERS (Section 3.2, p.26).

Navigation keys move through the menus and softkeys select what is on screen. For example, in Scale Configuration you use the left navigation key to select an A/D, press the center softkey (Add), and press Done to exit (Section 3.1.3, p.25).

The DISPLAY menu adjusts LCD contrast, turns backlighting on or off, and sets how many scale widgets (1 or 2) are shown. The front panel Display button adjusts contrast and backlighting directly (p.8).
Softkey definitions, passwords, and keyboard locks are set in the FEATURE menu, so which softkeys you see is decided by the configuration and program, not fixed by the factory.

keys.does: Five programmable keys whose functions are shown on tabs at the bottom of the LCD and activated by the arrow keys below the tabs. Defined softkeys include Time/Date, Display Tare, Display Accum, Setpoint, Batch Start/Stop/Pause/Reset, Weigh In, Weigh Out, Truck Regs, Unit ID, Select Scale, Diagnostics, Alibi, and F1-F10. If more than five are defined, a More… key toggles between groups.
Zero key function (Alt+Z on a PS/2 keyboard, F6). Its exact behavior with tare present depends on the REGULAT parameter setting (NTEP, CANADA, OIML, NONE, INDUST).
Toggles between gross and net display (Alt+G on a PS/2 keyboard, F7).

Tare key function (Alt+T on a PS/2 keyboard, F8). Whether it tares, clears tare, or does nothing depends on the weight on the scale, whether a tare is already stored, and the REGULAT mode (Table 10-4, p.100).
Units key function (Alt+U on a PS/2 keyboard, F9).
Print key function (Alt+P on a PS/2 keyboard, F10; Print Screen works the same in normal and setup modes).
Four navigation keys used with the LCD menus to move through parameters and select values, together with the softkeys shown on the display tabs.
Numeric entry keys for typing values such as calibration weights and parameters directly.

In the calibration displays (WZERO, WSPAN, WLIN), softkeys do the calibration work: Calibrate performs the calibration for the selected point, +/– toggles negative or positive entry, Last Zero recalls the last established zero, Temp Zero temporarily zeroes a non-empty scale, and Millivolts (or Counts) toggles between A/D counts and millivolts.

lights.does: Front panel power indicator. If it is blinking, the power supply is overloaded — check for shorts in A/D card regulators or in the DC-to-DC converter of installed option cards.

ideas.h: The panel is a small computer screen
ideas.text: Weight information is displayed in two font sizes with a graphical scale, and status areas on the LCD give operator prompts and hold entered data. Because it is a programmable HMI, the softkey tabs at the bottom are defined by the configuration and application program.

ideas.h: Softkeys follow the job, not the factory
ideas.text: The particular set of softkeys on the display is determined by the indicator configuration and program. Truck weighing, batching, and diagnostics all put different softkeys in front of the operator.

ideas.h: Calibration is done with softkeys
ideas.text: Front panel calibration lives in the CALIBR submenu under SCALES. You calibrate zero (WZERO), enter the test weight value (WVAL), calibrate span (WSPAN), and can add up to five linearization points (WLIN), pressing Enter to save each value.

ideas.h: Zero and span are stored as counts
ideas.text: Each calibration point captures an A/D count (or millivolt value). Temp Zero lets you span-calibrate without emptying the scale by using the difference between the temporary zero and the previously calibrated zero as an offset.

pre.short: The softkey that actually performs each calibration point — watch the tab labels.
Panel zero key (Alt+Z on a keyboard); behavior with tare depends on REGULAT mode.
Panel tare key (Alt+T on a keyboard); tares or clears tare per the regulatory mode.
Types test weight and parameter values directly.
Panel print key (Alt+P on a keyboard).

820i.refs: References: Rice Lake 820i Programmable HMI Indicator/Controller: softkeys Table 1-1 p.11, front panel p.8, menu summary Table 3-1 p.26, front panel calibration p.53, PS/2 keyboard functions Table 10-10 p.109, troubleshooting (power indicator) p.96. Note: the extract describes an LCD with display status areas rather than an LED annunciator bank, so lights are thin.

825 Gen2.name: 825 Gen2
825 Gen2.intro: The 825 Gen2 has no fixed keypad — its panel is an interactive touchscreen with a full QWERTY keyboard, a numeric keypad, and Navigation Keys with ENTER. The on-screen Standard Indicator keys (ZERO, TARE, PRINT, UNITS, NET/GROSS) do the weighing, and the annunciators across the weight screen say which mode you are in.
menus: The Start-Up screen offers the Application Program, LEGAL METROLOGY INFORMATION / SETUP and STANDARD INDICATOR selections. For Setup, press the LEGAL METROLOGY INFORMATION / SETUP selection (or press S on the QWERTY keyboard, or highlight it with the Right Arrow and press ENTER), then choose the Setup menu the same way; after logging in, the display changes to the Setup Menu screen (pp.47, 93, 50).

Use the Navigation Keys to select (highlight) the parameter to change. Down Arrow advances to the next parameter selection, Up Arrow backs up to the previous one, Right Arrow advances to the next parameter column, and Left Arrow exits to the previous screen. The Esc key also escapes back to the previous screen (p.47).

Some parameters require pressing the SPACE key to toggle their status or step through the available selections; use the QWERTY keyboard to enter new values, and press BACKSPACE to delete an incorrect value or character. After entering a new value, press Down Arrow to advance, or ENTER to save and return to the previous screen (p.47).

To return to normal operations, step back one screen at a time with the Left Arrow or Esc key: from Diagnostics to the Setup Menu, then to the Legal metrology information / Setup screen, then to the Startup screen and the weight screen (p.170).

keys.does: The Navigation Keys ENTER key is used to select and perform the function of a highlighted soft key or menu selection. This key and the alphabet ENTER key perform the same functions; either can be used (pp.35, 47). Pressing ENTER without entering a new value will retain the current setting and return to the previous screen (p.47).

The Navigation Keys move around and highlight the soft keys and menu selections: Down Arrow moves down to the next parameter, Up Arrow backs up to the previous one, Left Arrow exits to the previous screen, Right Arrow advances to the next parameter column (pp.35, 47).
Pressing the TARE key will act as a pushbutton tare and will store the current Gross weight as the new tare weight, and will switch the display to the Net weight mode (p.40).

Pressing the ZERO key allows the operator to reset the Gross weight to zero. If the gross weight exceeds the zero limit for this key (4% or 100% of capacity, set during setup and calibration), the message CANNOT ZERO is momentarily displayed (p.40).

Pressing the PRINT key will initiate the transmission of weight data to the ticket printer: displaying Gross prints time, date and gross weight; displaying Net prints time, date, gross, tare and net. Negative weight shows Cannot print BELOW ZERO, and unstable weight shows Cannot print MOTION (p.40).

Pressing the UNITS key will change the weighing units to the alternate units if available: with lb (pounds) showing, pressing this key will change the weight units to kg (kilograms). This feature must be enabled during setup and calibration (p.40).

Pressing the NET key (if in Gross mode) or the GROSS key (if in Net mode) will toggle between the Gross weight and Net weight. In Net weight mode, the Gross, Tare and Net weights are displayed; with no valid tare, the message Cannot show net - tare zero is shown (p.43).
In the Application Program keys, pressing this key will change the screen to display the menu selections for the application (p.40).
This key allows the operator to enter an ID (identification) for use in printing (p.43).

Some parameters require pressing the SPACE key to toggle their status or to step through the available selections — for example stepping through Display Mode (LCD Only, HDMI Only, LCD and HDMI) or Baud rate (pp.47, 50).
Press the Esc key to escape (return or backup) to the previous screen (p.47); in Diagnostics, Done or Enter, the Left Arrow, or the QWERTY Esc key returns to the previous menu screen (p.170).

The 825 is turned on by pressing the Push Button Power Switch on the rear enclosure; the display performs a short self-test and then changes to the Start-Up screen (p.47). After a Change Display Mode? Yes, the indicator shuts down and you press the push-button power switch off and on again to restart it (p.50).

lights.does: This is shown on the weight screen to indicate that the displayed (zero) weight is within +/- 1/4 division of the center of zero.
This is shown on the weight screen to indicate that the 825 is in the Gross weight mode.
This is shown on the weight screen when the 825 is in the Net weight mode. The screen will display the Gross, Tare, and Net weights.
This is shown on the weight screen to indicate that a Tare weight has been stored. The Gross and Net weights will also be displayed.
This is displayed on the weight screen to show that the weight unit is pounds.
This is displayed on the weight screen to show that the weight units are kilograms.
This is displayed on the weight screen to show that the weight units are avoirdupois tons.
This is displayed on the weight screen to show that the weight units are tonnes (metric tons).

ideas.h: Three ways to drive the same box
ideas.text: Nearly every setup step can be done three ways: touch the option on screen, press the underlined QWERTY letter, or highlight it with the Navigation Keys and press ENTER. Learn one way and you can work even when another is not handy.

ideas.h: ENTER keeps it or takes it
ideas.text: Pressing ENTER without entering a new value retains the current setting and returns to the previous screen. After a new value, ENTER saves it and returns — and the Down Arrow moves on to the next parameter instead.

ideas.h: Calibration can be locked by a jumper, not a password
ideas.text: Setup and Calibration are done entirely on the touchscreen, but the calibration jumper J11 (CAL INHIBIT) on the circuit board may have to change position depending on sealing law — and the screen will plainly say 'Calibration locked by hardware jumper inside enclosure.'

ideas.h: Gross and Net are one key apart
ideas.text: NET/GROSS toggles between the two. In Net mode the screen shows Gross, Tare and Net together; if no valid tare exists, the box tells you 'Cannot show net - tare zero' instead of showing a made-up net.

pre.short: Selects the highlighted item and saves a new value; with no new value it keeps the current setting.
Arrows highlight items and move between parameters — Left Arrow backs out to the previous screen.
Resets the Gross weight to zero, unless it is over the zero limit set in setup.
Pushbutton tare — stores the Gross weight as tare and switches to Net mode.
Prints the ticket; it refuses with BELOW ZERO or MOTION instead of printing a bad weight.
Shown when the displayed weight is within 1/4 division of center of zero.

825 Gen2.refs: References: 825 Desktop Installation & Technical Manual, Cardinal Doc 8545-1151-0M Rev B — Touchscreen Functions and Navigation Keys p.35 (manual pp.27-28), Standard Indicator keys pp.40, 43-44, Annunciators p.44, Setup navigation p.47, login to Setup Menu p.50, Calibration from the Setup Menu p.93, return to normal operations p.170.

880.intro: The 880 front panel is a six-button keypad with a six-digit, 14-segment LED display; the Universal model adds a numeric keypad. The same keys that run the scale in weigh mode become arrow and enter keys in configuration mode.
menus: In configuration mode the key symbols (up, down, enter, left, right) describe what the keys do: they move through menus, select digits inside numeric values, and raise or lower values (Section 3.2, p.44).
MENU opens the user setup menu. It also works as the cancel key while editing a value, and as the Exit key in the configuration and user setup menus.
After settings are changed, press MENU to return to weigh mode. Setpoint values and preact values may also be reachable from the front panel in weigh mode, depending on configuration and password.

Numeric values can be typed on the numeric keypad (Universal model), or entered by scrolling with the arrow keys. On the panel mount model, select the digit with left/right, then increment or decrement it.

keys.does: Sets the current gross weight to zero. In menus it navigates to other menus or selects another digit when editing a value.
Sends an on-demand print format to a communications port, provided the conditions for printing are met; it can be configured to show PRINT while printing. In menus it navigates or selects digits.
Performs the predetermined tare functions selected by the TAREFN parameter, and acts as the enter key for numeric or parameter entry. Pressing TARE accepts a calibration or edited value.
Toggles the displayed weight between gross and net mode; if a tare has been entered or acquired, net is gross minus tare. In menus it moves to different menus or selects digits.
Opens the user setup menu. It is also the cancel key when editing parameter values, and the Exit key in the configuration and user setup menus.
Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Format menu (lb, kg, oz, metric ton, ton, gram). In menus it navigates or selects digits.
Clears a numeric entry from the display (not available on the panel mount model).
Inserts a decimal point where necessary (not available on the panel mount model).
Types values directly; values may also be entered by scrolling with the arrow keys. The keypad is not available on the panel mount model.

lights.does: The current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center of zero band.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including Zero, Tare, and Printing, can only be completed when this LED is lit.
Gross weight mode is active (Brutto in OIML mode).
Net weight mode is active (gross weight minus tare).
Shows the units of the displayed value: lb lights for pounds (or the primary unit), kg lights for kilograms (or the secondary unit).
A tare has been acquired and stored by the system.
A preset tare weight has been keyed in or received via an EDP command.
Indicates the current range when the scale is configured for multi-range or multi-interval operation.

ideas.h: One keypad, two jobs
ideas.text: In weigh mode the keys run the scale; in configuration mode the symbols printed on them (up, down, enter, left, right) take over. TARE becomes Enter, MENU becomes Cancel/Exit, and the scale keys move you through the menus.

ideas.h: Standstill first
ideas.text: Zero, Tare, and Printing only complete when the standstill LED is lit. If a key seems to ignore you, check whether the scale has settled before assuming a fault.

ideas.h: Net is gross with the tare taken out
ideas.text: When a tare is stored, the GROSS/NET key switches between the full load and the load minus tare. The Gross/Brutto and Net annunciators keep you honest about which value is on screen.

ideas.h: Tare and zero rules change with the regulatory mode
ideas.text: What TARE and ZERO do depends on the REGULA parameter (NTEP, CANADA, OIML, NONE). For example, entering a zero tare cancels the entry, and in OIML mode ZERO can also clear the tare when the weight is within ZRANGE.

pre.short: Enter key — accepts values and confirms calibration points.
Zeroes the scale; also moves through menus and digits.
Prints when print conditions are met.
Opens user setup; cancels an edit or exits back to weigh mode.
Types values such as test weights directly (not on panel mount).
Must be lit for Zero, Tare, and Print to complete.

882D.name: 882D
882D.intro: The 882D belt scale integrator panel is a large back-lit LCD with a seven-digit numeric display, a three-line message area, six primary scale function keys, numeric keys and four function keys (Section 3.0, p.23). The top of the display carries arrow annunciators — Load, Total, Rate, Speed — that name what the numeric window is showing.
menus: Menu navigation uses four keys as arrows: SETPOINT and PRINT move left and right in a menu level, ZERO and MODE move up and down to different menu levels, ENTER selects parameter values or enters a submenu, and MENU enters and exits the menus (Section 4.3, p.28).

To enter a value, use the keypad (0–9 and decimal point) and press ENTER to accept it. When editing an alphanumeric string, the same navigation keys edit the characters, and CLEAR deletes the currently selected character (p.28).

Whether setup can be reached from the front panel depends on the audit trail jumper (JP4): jumper ON makes the Setup Menu visible so calibration and configuration are accessible from the keypad; jumper OFF hides it, and configuration is accessible only by pressing the setup switch (Section 2.8, p.18).

In calibration, F2/Stop cancels the run and the 882D exits; at the end the display shows the previous error and the current error with 'Press Enter To Accept' — ENTER accepts and stores the calibration, MENU rejects it (pp.51–52).

keys.does: Accesses and exits the menu structure; it also works as a cancel key when editing a parameter value. During calibration, pressing Menu rejects the calibration — REJECTED displays (p.52).

Accepts an entry at a prompt or when editing a value. After a calibration run, the display shows the previous and current error and prompts 'Enter Key To Accept'; pressing Enter stores the new calibration (pp.51–52).
In weigh mode it puts the 882D into dynamic zero calibration; it is also used as the up key to navigate menus or edit a value (Table 3-1, p.23).
Switches the weigh mode numeric display between load, totalizer 1, totalizer 2, totalizer master, rate and speed; also used as the down key to navigate menus or edit a value.
Sends print data to a communications port when in weigh mode; also used as the right key to navigate menus or edit a value.
Navigates to the top level setpoint menu at the first defined setpoint; also used as the left key to navigate menus or edit a value.
Resets totalizer 1 or 2 when it is displayed in weigh mode; when editing a parameter or prompt it deletes the currently selected character.
The 0–9 numeric keys are used to enter a numeric value for a parameter or prompt — for example, keying in the pre-weighed material amount during a material calibration (p.51).
Inserts a decimal point when entering a numeric value.

The start key, used for batching and for calibration: pressing F1/Start begins a calibration run — the display shows 'Calibrating...', takes span averages, and shows the weight being totalized at x10 resolution with a progress bar (p.51).
The stop key, used for batching and for calibration: pressing F2/Stop cancels a calibration in progress — 'Canceled' displays momentarily and the 882D exits the calibration (p.52).
The F3 and F4 keys have no pre-defined use, but can be monitored by an iRite application (Table 3-1, p.23).

lights.does: The arrow annunciator for Load is illuminated — the numeric display is showing the load on the belt (p.23).
The arrow annunciator for Total is illuminated — the numeric display is showing a totalizer value (p.25).
The arrow annunciator for Rate is illuminated — the numeric display is showing the rate of material flow (p.23).
The arrow annunciator for Speed is illuminated — the numeric display is showing belt speed (p.23).
The 1 or 2 annunciator names which totalizer is displayed: totalizer 1 or totalizer 2. When neither the 1 nor 2 annunciator is illuminated, the master totalizer is displayed (p.23).
Shows the units on the display: metric units are metric tons, kilograms, meters; imperial units are short tons, pounds, feet; time units are hours, minutes, seconds (p.23).
Displays when the Rate is within the Zero Band — the Zero Band is a percentage of the Max Capacity (Max Rate) and is configurable in the configuration settings (p.23).

ideas.h: One display, six readings
ideas.text: The MODE key walks the numeric window around the belt: load on the belt right now, totalizer 1, totalizer 2, the master totalizer, rate, and belt speed. The arrow annunciators at the top (Load, Total, Rate, Speed) always say which world you are looking at.

ideas.h: Three totalizers, one master
ideas.text: Totalizer 1 and Totalizer 2 can be cleared and restarted for a run or a shift; the master totalizer keeps the grand total of everything. When a totalizer shows, the arrow points at TOTAL and the 1 or 2 annunciator names it — when neither number is lit, you are looking at the master.

ideas.h: Zero is judged as a percent of rate
ideas.text: The Center-of-Zero annunciator does not watch weight, it watches rate: it displays when the rate is within the Zero Band, a percentage of the Max Capacity (Max Rate) set in configuration. On a belt scale, 'zero' means the belt is running true empty.

ideas.h: Calibration measures at ten times detail
ideas.text: During a calibration run the totalized weight shows at x10 resolution with a progress bar in the message area, over the Test Distance (default 20 ft/m). The scale collects span averages and then shows the previous error and the new error side by side before anything is accepted.

ideas.h: A jumper guards the setup door
ideas.text: Where the 3-pin audit trail jumper (JP4) sits decides whether the Setup Menu is visible on the front panel at all. With it OFF, configuration and calibration can only be reached with the setup switch — the front keys will not get there.

pre.short: Accepts an entry or an edit; after a calibration run it accepts and stores the new calibration.
Enters and exits the menus; cancels an edit, and rejects a calibration at the accept prompt.
In weigh mode it runs the dynamic zero calibration; in menus it is the up key.
Starts a batch or a calibration run — the display shows 'Calibrating...'.
Stops a batch, or cancels a calibration in progress.
Type values directly — distances, test amounts, and parameter numbers.

882IS.name: 882IS
882IS.intro: The 882IS and 882IS Plus panels show weight on seven-segment LCD digits with a two-line dot-matrix message area underneath for prompts and errors. Keys printed with up, down, enter, left, and right symbols navigate setup menus and edit values, and the Plus model adds a numeric keypad with Clear and decimal point keys.
menus: Press MENU to open the User Setup menu. The key symbols show the menu jobs of the weighing keys: ZERO up, GROSS/NET down, PRINT right, UNITS moves between menus or digits, and TARE is Enter for numeric and parameter entry.
In Configuration/Setup mode the keys navigate through menus, select the digit within a numeric value, and increment or decrement the value being edited.
MENU backs you out: it cancels an edit while you are changing a parameter value, and it works as the exit key from the Configuration and User Setup menus.
The Test menu holds two diagnostics: Keypad Test, which shows each key press on the display and transmits it on the COM port, and Battery Counts, which shows the battery voltage as counts.
The Keylock menu can lock or unlock individual front-panel keys: Zero, Gross/Net, Units, Print, Tare, Menu, the numeric keypad as a group, and the function keys as a group.

keys.does: Sets the current gross weight to zero. In menus, ZERO is the up key for navigating.

Sends an on-demand print format out a communications port when standstill conditions are met; Print may show on the display while printing if enabled. In menus, PRINT is the right key and selects another digit when editing a value.
Toggles the display between Gross and Net; net is gross weight minus tare when a tare has been entered or acquired. In menus, GROSS/NET is the down key.
Opens the User Setup menu. It also cancels while editing a parameter value and acts as the exit key in the Configuration and User Setup menus.

Switches the display to the alternate unit defined in the Format menu; available units include lb, kg, oz, metric ton, ton, and gram. It also moves between menus and toggles to another digit when editing a value.
Performs the preset tare behavior chosen in the Tare Function parameter. In menus and numeric entry, TARE is the Enter key.
Turns the unit on or off: press and hold to turn on, press momentarily to turn off.
Clears the current value during a numeric entry. Available on the 882IS Plus.
Inserts a decimal point where needed during numeric entry. Available on the 882IS Plus.
Types numeric values directly instead of scrolling digit by digit. Available on the 882IS Plus.

lights.does: Gross or Brutto weight mode is displayed.
Net weight mode is displayed.
The current gross weight reading is within plus or minus 0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero, or within the center-of-zero band.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including zero, tare, and printing, can only be done when the standstill LCD is on.
A Peak Hold value is being displayed.
A tare has been acquired and stored by the system.
A preset tare weight has been keyed in or entered with an EDP command.

ideas.h: Standstill gates the working keys
ideas.text: The standstill annunciator says the scale is settled inside its motion band. The book only allows operations such as zero, tare, and printing while that sign is on, so a moving scale simply refuses the key.

ideas.h: Center of zero is a quarter-division promise
ideas.text: The center-of-zero sign means gross weight is within plus or minus 0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero. A display division is the smallest weight step the display can show or print.

ideas.h: Regulation quietly rewrites ZERO and TARE
ideas.text: The Features menu Regulation setting changes what the front-panel ZERO and TARE keys do under NTEP, CANADA, OIML, and NONE. The same press can key a tare, clear a tare, zero the scale, or do nothing, depending on the mode, the weight on the scale, and whether a tare is already in the system.

ideas.h: The Plus model is the one with a keypad
ideas.text: The base 882IS works through its named function keys, while the 882IS Plus adds a numeric keypad, a Clear key, and a decimal point key for typing values directly. F1 through F4 are marked as future enhancements in this book, not working keys.

pre.short: TARE runs the tare function; in menus it is ENTER.
MENU opens User Setup; it cancels edits and exits menus.
ZERO sets gross weight to zero; menu UP key.
PRINT sends a print format when standstill is met.
Standstill on means zero, tare, and print are allowed.

920i.name: 920i
920i.intro: The 920i front panel (p.13) has navigation keys, an Enter key, numeric entry keys, Clear and Decimal, plus Print, Units, Tare, Gross/Net, and Zero keys and a row of configurable softkeys. Symbols on the display area show standstill, center of zero, and tare status alongside the weight.
menus: In setup mode the 920i is configured through a series of front-panel menus: SCALES, SERIAL, FEATURE, PFORMT (print format), SETPTS, DIG I/O, ALGOUT, FLDBUS, and VERSION (p.36).

The navigation keys scroll through the menus and are also used to enter values; ENTER saves entries made from the numeric keypad, and CLEAR works as a backspace when entering numbers or letters (p.13).

Softkey assignments are listed on the tabs shown at the bottom of the LCD display and are activated by pressing the arrow keys below the tabs (p.15). The FEATURE menu is used to enable softkeys (p.15).
If more than five softkeys are defined, the More... softkey is automatically assigned to the fifth position; press More... to toggle between groups of softkeys (p.15).
In setup-mode editors such as print format strings, position the cursor in the string and press Enter to save the edited format; a Cancel softkey exits without saving changes (p.87).

keys.does: Sets the current gross weight to zero.
Performs a predetermined tare function as set in the TAREFN parameter in the Scale menu. A T means a pushbutton tare is in the system; PT means a keyed tare.
Toggles the weight display between gross and net mode. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare.
Switches the weight display to an alternate unit.
Sends an on-demand print format out a communications port, provided the conditions for standstill are met.
Saves entries made from the numeric keypad.
Works as backspace when entering numbers or letters.
Used to enter values and scroll through menus. On the front panel figure these are the arrow keys surrounding the Enter key.

Keys that can be configured to provide additional operator functions. Assignments are shown as tabs at the bottom of the LCD display and are activated by pressing the arrow keys below the tabs; examples include Time/Date, Display Tare, Setpoint, Batch Start/Stop, Weigh In/Out, and Alibi.

lights.does: Standstill symbol: the scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band.
Center of Zero symbol: the current gross weight reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero.
Tare symbol T: a pushbutton tare has been acquired and stored in the system.
Tare symbol PT: a keyed tare has been entered and stored in the system.
Units indicator: shows the current unit of display next to the weight.
Gross/Net indicator: indicates whether the weight value is in Net or Gross mode.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: The Gross/Net key toggles the weight display between gross and net mode. If a tare value has been entered or acquired, the net value is the gross weight minus the tare, so net only exists when a tare is in the system.

ideas.h: Print waits for standstill
ideas.text: The Print key sends an on-demand print format out a communications port, provided the conditions for standstill are met. The standstill symbol on the display is the scale saying the weight has settled enough to be captured and printed.

ideas.h: Last Zero and Temp Zero work around a loaded scale
ideas.text: The calibration softkeys include Last Zero, which recalls the last established zero value to allow calibration without removing test weights or product from the scale, and Temp Zero, which temporarily zeros a non-empty scale so the difference becomes an offset after span calibration. Both exist for scales you cannot empty.

ideas.h: The softkey row is set by the configuration
ideas.text: The displayed softkeys are determined by the indicator configuration and program, and softkeys are enabled in the FEATURE menu. More than five defined softkeys automatically puts a More... softkey in the fifth position to toggle between groups, so the row on one 920i may not match the row on another.

pre.short: Saves the value you typed on the numeric keypad — press it after every entry.
Sets the current gross weight to zero before you capture the zero point.
Takes or clears the tare depending on the TAREFN setup; watch for the T or PT symbol.
Prints only when standstill conditions are met, so let the scale settle first.
The scale is settled when this symbol shows — captures and prints wait for it.

920i.refs: References: Rice Lake 920i Programmable Indicator/Controller: Front Panel Section 2.1 p.13, Softkey Operations Section 2.5 p.15, Main Menu Section 4.5 p.36, Front Panel Calibration Section 5.2 p.64, string editor save/cancel softkeys p.87.

CW-90.name: CW-90
CW-90.intro: The CW-90/90X is a checkweigher: its panel is built around setting a target weight with OVER and UNDER tolerance values, and lights that tell the operator whether a package is under, accept, or over. It has function keys plus an ID key and a bar graph display.
menus: Press MENU to enter Menu mode; in Menu mode MENU works as a back button. The menu offers AUDIT, CALIBR (calibration), SETUP, TEST, EXIT, T&D (time & date), ACCUM, BRIGHT, and ID (Section 3.1, p.23).

In Menu mode the keys navigate: OVER moves up/increments a value, UNDER moves down/decrements, TARGET moves right/next, ID moves left/previous, ENTER accepts the value and moves down the menu, and MENU enters/exits configuration (Figure 3-1, p.23).

When adding or editing data: press OVER or UNDER to edit a flashing digit, ID or TARGET to move through digits, ENTER to accept and return to the next menu item. On the CW-90 the numeric keys can insert a digit to the right of the blinking digit (Section 3.1.1, p.23).
To exit, navigate to the EXIT menu and press ENTER to return to the weigh screen.

keys.does: Enters the Menu mode; used as a back button while in Menu mode.
Displays the current over tolerance value, or allows setting the over tolerance value. In Menu mode it moves up and increments values.
Displays the current under tolerance value, or allows setting the under tolerance value. In Menu mode it moves down and decrements values.
Acquires a weight value and assigns it as the desired target value. In Menu mode it moves right to the next digit or item.
Selects a particular over/under/tare/units register set to be retrieved and used. In Menu mode it moves left to the previous digit or item.
Accepts entries and moves down in Menu mode. During calibration it is the data entry confirmation and EXECUTE key, and accepts the value if calibration was successful.
Performs predetermined Tare functions depending on the mode of operation selected with the TAREFN parameter; also used to view a stored tare.
Sends on-demand serial information out the serial port, provided the conditions for standstill are met; PRINT displays while printing.
Switches the weight display to an alternate unit defined in the Setup menu. Conversions of the weight reading, the tare value, and the Over and Under values occur when the unit of measure is changed.

Sets current gross weight to zero, provided the weight to be removed or added is within the specified zero range and the scale is not in motion. The zero band defaults to +/-1.9% of full scale (1.9% is required for Legal-for-Trade) and can be configured up to 100%.
Clear key (front panel CLR), used for clearing entries; on the CW-90 the ZERO or CLR key can be used as a backspace. In Menu mode CLR serves as backspace on entries.
Enters values directly (CW-90 only). In Menu mode the numeric keys insert a digit to the right of the blinking digit.

lights.does: Bar graph value (0-1023) showing how the weight falls in the under zone of the checkweigh band.
Bar graph value (0-1023) for the accept zone — the weight is within the target tolerance band.
Bar graph value (0-1023) showing how the weight falls in the over zone of the checkweigh band.

In Gross mode, the displayed weight is within ±0.25 display divisions of the acquired zero or within the center of zero band; in Net mode, the net reading is within ±0.25 display divisions of the center of net zero.
Weight is displayed in Gross mode (or Brutto in OIML mode).
Weight is displayed in Net mode (gross weight minus a tare weight).
A tare has been acquired and stored.
A preset tare weight has been keyed in or entered via the EDP serial port.

ideas.h: Checkweighing is a band, not a number
ideas.text: The CW-90 judges each package against a target with under and over tolerances. The LIGHTS setting shows this as a solid light bar for over and under weights, or as a graph that lights in increments as the weight gets closer to the acceptance band (Section 1.8, p.11; CHKWGH menu p.35).

ideas.h: Two ways to set the band
ideas.text: VALSET can be KEYED (type the accept band values), PUSH (place actual weights on the scale and capture them), BOTH (capture, then edit), or RDONLY (look but not change). This decides whether operators set tolerances by keypad or by putting real product on the scale.

ideas.h: Standstill still rules printing
ideas.text: PRINT sends the on-demand print only when the conditions for standstill are met, and PRINT shows on the display while printing. The ZZ command reports SS (standstill) among the lit annunciators, so the panel's lights are the same story as the scale's status.

pre.short: Accepts entries; in calibration it is the confirmation/EXECUTE key.
Zeroes within the zero range when the scale is not in motion.
Tare functions per TAREFN; also views a stored tare.
Prints when standstill conditions are met.
Enters Menu mode; back button while in menus.
Types values directly (CW-90 only).
