DC-200/300.name: DC-200/300
DC-200/300.intro: The DC-200/300 console is a full counting-scale workstation: an alphanumeric keyboard, a numeric keypad, and a row of annunciators that report zero, net, counting, and mode status. Almost every key changes jobs depending on which mode the scale is in.
menus: The MODE key walks the scale through its modes in a ring: Operation for weighing and counting, Report for printing item and inventory reports, Program for entering item data, Password for protecting functions, and Service for dealer setup and troubleshooting. Watch the right side of the display: S means Program, X means Report, Z means Service, and no letter means Operation.

For setup from the keyboard, press and hold REZERO and key in 141 for customer specifications (SPEC 00-71) or 142 for weight and measurement specifications (SPEC 600-646). The current SPEC and its setting appear on the two display lines.

Inside the SPEC settings, use >> and << to scroll through the choices for a setting, press + (plus) to store the change to temporary memory and move to the next SPEC, and - (minus) to step to the previous SPEC without saving. Keying a SPEC number and pressing REPRINT jumps straight to that specification.

To save and leave programming, press the CODE key; the data is stored and the scale heads back to the Operation standby screen (pressing MODE three times from programming also returns there). To leave without saving, press PIECES then CLEAR, as the book shows for the date and time screen.
Service Mode holds the hardware tests: press MODE until SERVICE MODE shows and the Z annunciator lights, then hold REZERO and press 001 to cycle through RAM, RS-232/Ethernet, and ROM checksum tests.

keys.does: Turns the scale display on or off.

Cycles between the modes: Operation (weighing and counting), Report (print reports), Program (enter item data), Password, and Service (setup and troubleshooting by an authorized dealer or technician). Press it repeatedly to walk the modes; pressing it three times from Programming returns to the Operation standby screen.

Resets the scale to zero; it does not work while the scale is in motion. Held down while keying 141 or 142, it opens the specification (SPEC) settings; held with 001 in Service Mode it opens the hardware tests.
In Operation Mode, sets and clears tare weights. In Program Mode it makes an item test print. In other modes it selects No.
In Operation Mode, clears keyed-in data from the display starting with the last digit entered. In other modes it selects Yes.

In Operation Mode, computes the unit weight by sampling: press it after placing a 10-piece sample on the platform (or after keying in the sample size). In other modes it escapes the programming screen without saving data.
In Program Mode, stores the programmed data. It also saves settings, such as the date and time, and returns toward the standby screen.
In Operation Mode, prints a label or report; in Report Mode it prints the report. In Program Mode it stores entered information into temporary memory.

Scroll specifications and stored items: plus selects the next programming item or SPEC number, minus selects the delete function or steps back. In SPEC setting, plus stores the change into temporary memory and moves to the next SPEC code.
Move the cursor and change the entry left or right. In SPEC setting mode they cycle forward and backward through the choices for the setting on display, and toggle AM/PM in time entry.
Enters the digits of a value. A numeric value is entered first, then the function key that uses it; a decimal value needs the 0 first, so a quarter is keyed as 0.250.
Feeds label or receipt paper. (DC-300 only.)

lights.does: Gross weight is zero.
The display is showing net weight, because a tare weight has been entered or recalled.
Unit weight recomputing is possible.
Net weight is below the specified percentage of scale capacity.
Memory indicator: quantity accumulation is being done.
Paper end.
The scale is in Programming Mode. (Registration/Operation Mode shows no letter; X is Report Mode, Z is Service Mode.)
The scale is in Service Mode, used by the dealer or authorized technician for setup and troubleshooting.

ideas.h: This is a counting scale first
ideas.text: Most of the keyboard exists to manage counting: sampling a few pieces to learn the unit weight, entering a known unit weight, and accumulating quantities. Plain weighing is only part of the job this panel was built for.

ideas.h: The mode letters tell you which machine you are running
ideas.text: The same keys do different jobs in Operation, Report, Program, and Service modes. The annunciators on the right of the display (S, X, Z) show which mode is live, and the book warns to check the mode before trusting a key.

ideas.h: SPEC codes are the setup language
ideas.text: Customer specifications (SPEC 00-71, access code 141) and weight and measurement specifications (SPEC 600-646, access code 142) are how this scale is configured from the keyboard. The 142 group is the weighing heart of the machine and is meant for the dealer or technician.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: When a tare weight is entered or recalled, the display shows net weight and the NET annunciator lights. Zero is separate: the arrow-zero annunciator only lights when the gross weight is at true zero.

pre.short: The zero key - resets the scale to zero (it will not work while the scale is moving).
Walks the modes - keep pressing until you reach the mode you need; Service Mode is the Z light.
Types the numbers; hold REZERO and key 141 or 142 to get into the SPEC setup settings.
Plus stores the change and moves to the next SPEC; minus steps back without saving.
Saves the data and gets you out of programming.
Lit when gross weight is truly at zero - the sign the scale is empty and settled at zero.

E1010.name: E1010
E1010.intro: The E1010's front panel (manual pp.5-6) is a keypad of weighing keys that double as menu arrows, plus F1, MODE, ESC, ENTER and a numeric keypad. It is a battery-powered indicator, and behind the ESC key sit three password-protected menus.
menus: Access the menus by pressing and holding the ESC key for 3-5 seconds until PASS_ is displayed, then key in the password of the menu you want and press ENTER. You must key in the password within 10 seconds or the display returns to normal operation mode (p.1).

The three menus are the User menu (password 111), the Service menu (password 0101), and the Supervisor menu (password 1793) — Service covers calibration and configuration, Supervisor covers time/date and the PLU database (p.1).

Scroll through the choices by using the UNITS key or TARE key and press the ENTER key to accept the displayed choice (p.35). Inside the menus the other weighing keys act as arrows: TARE left, SELECT up, PRINT down, UNITS right (p.1).
In the Service menu, press the ZERO key and the indicator returns to normal weighing mode (p.44). The ESC key escapes a function or returns to normal operation mode at any time (p.1).

keys.does: Press the TARE key to perform a tare function. Also acts as a left arrow key when in the menu structure.

Press the SELECT key to toggle between Gross, Tare, Net, Count, Gross Accumulator, Net Accumulator, Transaction Counter, Piece Weight, and Peak, depending on the current application. Also acts as an up arrow key when in the menu structure. Press and hold to access the outputs function.
Press the ZERO key to zero the display. Pressing ZERO in the Service menu returns the indicator to normal weighing mode (p.44).
Press the PRINT key to send information to a peripheral device through one of the communication ports. Also acts as a down arrow key when in the menu structure.
Press the UNITS key to scroll through the available units of measure while in normal operating mode. Also acts as a right arrow key when in the menu structure.
Press the ENTER key to accept displayed choices.
Press the ESC key to escape a function or return to normal operation mode. Press and hold for 3-5 seconds to access the password display for the menu structure.
Press the F1 key to select application specific choices. Also used to access PLU (Product Look Up) memory channels.
Press the MODE key to scroll through the enabled applications. The application name is briefly displayed when the key is released.
Press the C/CE key to clear entries.
To turn the unit on, press and hold the ON/OFF key until the backlight turns on. To turn the unit off, press and hold the ON/OFF key until the unit turns off.

lights.does: The center-of-zero annunciator lights when the weight falls within the center-of-zero window size (set to ±1/4 or ±1/2 division).
In checkweighing mode the ABOVE annunciator comes ON (with its output and TIU3 relay) when the weight is above the configured value.
In checkweighing mode the OVER annunciator comes ON (with its output and TIU3 relay) when the weight is above the configured value.
In checkweighing mode the ACCEPT annunciator comes ON (with its output and TIU3 relay) when the weight is in the accept condition above the configured value.

ideas.h: Three doors, three passwords
ideas.text: The User menu (111), Service menu (0101) and Supervisor menu (1793) are opened with the same move — hold ESC, key the password, press ENTER — but each password unlocks a deeper level, from viewing and testing up to calibration, configuration and PLU setup.

ideas.h: The weighing keys double as arrows
ideas.text: TARE is left, SELECT is up, PRINT is down and UNITS is right when you are in the menu structure. The same five keys you weigh with are the keys you steer the menus with.

ideas.h: SELECT is the dial for what you are looking at
ideas.text: SELECT toggles between Gross, Tare, Net, Count, the accumulators, Transaction Counter, Piece Weight and Peak, depending on the application. When the number on screen confuses you, SELECT is usually the key that changes what it means.

ideas.h: Center of zero has a window, not a point
ideas.text: The center-of-zero window is ±1/4 or ±1/2 division. When the weight falls within the window the annunciator lights, so 'zero' really means 'close enough to zero that the box will call it zero.'

pre.short: Accepts the displayed choice — the take-it key after you scroll to what you want.
Escapes a function back to normal operation; hold it 3-5 seconds to open the password screen.
Zeroes the display, and in the Service menu it is the way back out to normal weighing.
Performs a tare; in the menus it is the left arrow.
Sends information out a communication port; in the menus it is the down arrow.
Lit when the weight is inside the center-of-zero window — the settled sign.

E1010.refs: References: Model E1010 Indicator Service Manual, Avery Weigh-Tronix Doc AWT35-500132 — Front Panel and Keys (manual pp.5-6, PDF p.1), Menu access and passwords p.1, Center of Zero window p.24, SERIAL submenu navigation p.35, Outputs/annunciator operation p.44.

EK/EW-i.name: EK/EW-i
EK/EW-i.intro: The EK/EW-i is a small compact balance. This maintenance manual describes its handful of keys — ON/OFF, SAMPLE, PRINT, MODE, RE-ZERO and the CAL switch — mostly as tools for calibration, function settings and the check mode, rather than as a day-to-day front panel tour.
menus: To enter check mode, hold the ZERO and CAL keys then press the ON/OFF key. The software version and model type appear, then all segments appear (p.22).
In check mode, press the ZERO key to enter the function setting group or the MODE key to enter the adjustment group (p.22).
When changing a value, SAMPLE selects the digit blinking to change and RE-ZERO sets the value of the digit selected; PRINT stores the change to EEPROM and MODE cancels without storing (pp.9, 27).

keys.does: Hold the ZERO and CAL keys, then press the ON/OFF key to enter check mode: the software version and model type appear, then all segments light (p.22).

To select the digit blinking to change when setting a calibration weight or gravity value (p.9). In the internal data display it changes the display item, cycling weight A/D count, temperature, internal count and battery voltage (p.23).
Press the PRINT key to weigh and input the calibration weight, and to store values to EEPROM (pp.9-10, 27). In the key/port check, PRINT starts the key and port check (p.23).

To cancel the value and return to the previous step (p.9). Remove the calibration weight and press the CAL switch or MODE key to return to the weighing mode (p.10). In check mode, MODE enters the adjustment group (p.22).
To set the value of the digit selected (p.9). In the internal data displays it displays zero (p.23), and in check mode the ZERO key enters the function setting group (p.22).

The CAL switch is used with the calibration procedure: after the weight is stored, remove the weight and press the CAL switch or MODE key to return to the weighing mode (p.10). Hold CAL (with ZERO) while pressing ON/OFF to enter check mode (p.22).

lights.does: With the comparator conditions set (compare all data, stable data, or data beyond ±4 divisions), the HI result is one of the comparator/BZ outputs shown in the key and port check (p.23).
With the comparator conditions set, the OK result is one of the comparator/BZ outputs shown in the key and port check; the buzzer can be set to sound at OK (pp.23, 30).
With the comparator conditions set, the LO result is one of the comparator/BZ outputs shown in the key and port check; the buzzer can be set to sound at LO (pp.23, 30).
The function settings include conditions to turn on the stability mark: stable when within ±0.5d, ±1d or ±2d in 0.5 second (p.30).
In the battery voltage internal display, the lower indication shows LO for low battery and HI for high battery (p.23).

ideas.h: Calibration lives behind the CAL switch
ideas.text: This balance is calibrated through the CAL switch, not a menu tour: set the weight value, place the calibration weight, and PRINT weighs and stores it. MODE or the CAL switch brings you back to the weighing mode.

ideas.h: A gravity number can stand in for a weight
ideas.text: If the balance is moved and you have no calibration weight, you can change the stored gravity acceleration value to the new area's value instead. It is not required when you calibrate with a weight where the balance will be used.

ideas.h: The balance tells you when it is settled
ideas.text: The function settings include conditions to turn on the stability mark and filter choices (Fast/sensitive or Slow/stable). On a small balance, that mark is the difference between a real reading and a wobbling one.

ideas.h: Check mode is the service door
ideas.text: Holding ZERO and CAL while pressing ON/OFF opens check mode, where the ZERO key leads to the function setting group and the MODE key to the adjustment group — and the book warns not to press PRINT in the wrong place, because internal data may get damaged.

pre.short: Weighs and stores the calibration weight, and stores changed values to memory.
Cancels a value, and after calibration returns you to the weighing mode.
Sets the value of the blinking digit; also zeroes the internal data displays.
The calibration switch — starts calibration with ON/OFF held, and returns you to weighing when done.
Selects the blinking digit to change, and cycles the internal data displays.
Comes on when the balance is stable within the set window — wait for it before trusting a reading.

EK/EW-i.refs: References: EK-i/EW-i Series Compact Balances Maintenance Manual, A&D Doc WT+PD4000657A — calibration weight setting p.9, CAL switch return and gravity correction p.10, gravity value setting p.11, calibration data input pp.19-21, Check mode flow and key/port check pp.22-23, internal data displays p.23, EEPROM store/cancel p.27, function setting list (stability mark, comparator, buzzer) p.30. This is a maintenance manual: the keys are described for calibration, function and check modes, and there is no front-panel tour or annunciator table — that is why this book rates THIN.

IND560.name: IND560
IND560.intro: The IND560 panel is a 128 by 64 graphic vacuum fluorescent display with three dedicated scale function keys (Zero, Tare, Print), a 12-key numeric keypad, five navigation keys, and five softkeys whose labels show at the bottom of the screen. Up to 15 softkeys can be programmed in three sets of five.
menus: Getting in: the Home screen is the only screen that provides operator access to the programmable softkeys, and the Setup softkey opens the setup pages from there. The Setup and Information Recall softkeys are always assigned and cannot be deleted.

Moving in the menu tree: the RIGHT navigation key expands the setup options in the menu tree and the LEFT navigation key collapses them; the arrows also move the cursor in text areas and scroll screens.

Editing a value: the ENTER key opens the setup page for viewing and editing, moves the focus from a field label to the setup value for that field, and accepts new values and moves the focus to the next field label.

Getting out: press the EXIT softkey to return to the menu tree. If you are halfway through typing a value, the ESCAPE softkey exits the data entry without accepting any of the new data; the field reverts to the original data.

More softkey rows: space at the right of the softkey icons shows a MORE UP or MORE DOWN indicator when additional softkey selections are available; press the UP or DOWN navigation key to page between the three sets of five.

keys.does: Opens the setup page for viewing and editing setup parameters, moves the focus from a field label to the setup value for that field, and accepts new values entered in a field and moves the focus to the next field label.

The LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys expand (RIGHT) or collapse (LEFT) the setup options in the menu tree, move the cursor position to a specific character in text areas, and enable left and right scrolling on a screen.
One of the three dedicated scale function keys to the right of the display; these provide the interface to zero the scale.
One of the three dedicated scale function keys to the right of the display; these provide the interface to tare the scale.
One of the three dedicated scale function keys to the right of the display; initiates a print.
The terminal's 12-key numeric keypad, on the upper-right side of the front panel, is used to enter data and commands. Position the cursor in the field, then press the numeric keys.
Press the DECIMAL key to enter decimal points where necessary while entering numeric data.

Functions like a backspace key: press CLEAR once for each character to be deleted. When first entering a data entry box, the previous entry is in focus and pressing CLEAR at this point clears the entire previous entry.

Exits the data entry process without accepting any of the new data typed; the data in the entry field reverts to the original data. Pressed during any step of a calibration test, it aborts the test and returns to the Run Calibration Test screen.
Returns from diagnostics and setup screens such as Display Test, Keyboard Test, and Calibration Values to the menu tree.
Navigation softkeys provide quick access to setup pages. The Setup softkey must always be assigned a position (default position 10, with Information Recall) and cannot be deleted.

Opens the recall screens; ID fields entered in setup display in the information recall when the SYSTEM INFORMATION softkey is pressed after the RECALL softkey. It must always be assigned a position and cannot be deleted.

lights.does: Shown in the space to the right of the softkey icons when additional softkey selections are available by pressing the DOWN navigation key. A total of 15 softkeys can be presented in three sets of five.
Shown in the space to the right of the softkey icons when additional softkey selections are available above; press the UP navigation key to view them.
A system line is reserved at the top of the display to show system messages and any asynchronous errors; the Home screen shows a message in this line when the terminal needs to tell you something.

A graphical visualization in the middle of the display that represents measured values: a bar graph in material transfer mode, or an over/under display in over/under mode, sized None, Small, Medium or Large.

ideas.h: An icon is not an enabled function
ideas.text: Adding a softkey to the home pages of the terminal does not automatically enable the softkey's function; most softkeys must also be enabled in setup too. Adding the UNIT SWITCHING softkey, for instance, does not enable units switching until the units are enabled in the Scale branch of setup.

ideas.h: Your calibration numbers can move to a new board
ideas.text: The Calibration Values screen displays the current calibration values configured for the scale. These values can be recorded and then manually entered into a new replacement board should a failure ever occur, which eliminates having to recalibrate the scale with test weights, although it is not as accurate as placing test weights on the scale.

ideas.h: ENTER runs all of setup
ideas.text: One key drives the whole setup conversation: ENTER opens the setup page, moves the focus from the field label to its value, accepts the new value, and moves on to the next field label. If you know what ENTER will do next, you know where you are in setup.

ideas.h: Two softkeys can never be deleted
ideas.text: The INFORMATION RECALL and SETUP softkeys are automatically placed in the softkey setup and must always be assigned a position. They can be moved or copies can exist, but they cannot be deleted, so there is always a way into setup and recall.

pre.short: Opens the page, moves label to value, and accepts the new value.
Dedicated scale function key; zeroes the scale.
Dedicated scale function key; initiates a print.
Quick access into the setup pages; always assigned.
Returns to the menu tree from setup and diagnostics screens.
Backspace for entries; clears a whole previous entry when a box opens.

IND560.refs: References: METTLER TOLEDO IND560 Technical Manual 71209394 — Chapter 1 Display and Keyboard, Chapter 2 Operation (navigation interface, home screen, numeric keys), Chapter 3 Configuration (diagnostics), Appendix E Softkey Mapping.

IND570.name: IND570
IND570.intro: The IND570 has five softkey buttons along the bottom of the display, each identified by the graphic icon shown directly above it, plus a 12-key alphanumeric keypad. Up to 15 softkey functions can be shown on three separate rows.
menus: Getting in: the SETUP softkey enters the setup menu. Together with INFORMATION RECALL it must always be present on the home screen; they are in positions 9 and 10 by default.
Moving around: press the UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys to move the focus. As a different position gains the focus, its assignment is shown in text toward the bottom of the screen.
Changing a setting: press the ENTER key to open the assignment selection box, use the UP or DOWN navigation keys to scroll until the desired selection is in focus, then press ENTER to select it.

Getting out: the EXIT softkey returns from an edit screen to the previous setup screen. If you are typing letters and chose the wrong group, the ESCAPE softkey ends the entry without accepting any of the new data.

More softkey rows: a MORE DOWN symbol at the lower-right corner of the screen means more softkey selections are available. Press the DOWN navigation key to display the additional screens, and UP to come back.

keys.does: Press ENTER to open the assignment selection box, then press ENTER again to select the assignment that is in focus. In data entry, press ENTER to accept the entries.
The UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys move the focus among positions and screens. The assignment of the position in focus is shown in text toward the bottom of the screen.
Enters the setup menu (listed in the icon table as 'Enter Setup Menu'). It must always be present on the home screen and cannot be removed from it.
Opens the information recall options: Weight Recall, Metrology Recall, System Information Recall, Service Information Recall, and Print.
Returns from an edit screen to the setup screen you came from, for example from the Softkey Edit screen back to the Softkeys Setup Screen.
Ends a data entry without accepting any of the new data typed. The data in the entry field reverts to whatever was in the entry box before the entry was started.
While entering data, the CLEAR key can be used to delete unwanted characters in the entry box.
The terminal's Zero key (listed as key code 30 in the manual's key code table). In calibration, the Capture Zero function captures the zero point of the scale.
The terminal's Tare key (key code 24 in the manual's key code table). The TARE TABLE softkey opens the tare table search screen for stored tare records.
The Print function appears among the Information Recall options for printing records; the keypad Print key is key code 23 in the manual's key code table.

lights.does: Displayed on the lower-right corner of the screen, to the far right of the softkey icons, when more softkey selections are available. Press the DOWN navigation key to display additional softkey screens.
Shown when previous softkey screens are available above the current one. Press the UP navigation key to display the previous softkey screen.
Status messages appear in the terminal's system line; for example, 'Keypad disabled' appears there when remote key control (K_3) blocks the keypad.

ideas.h: An icon is not an enabled function
ideas.text: Adding a softkey to the home pages of the terminal does not automatically enable the softkey function; most functions must also be enabled in setup. If a softkey has been added but does not appear on the home page, check that the setup parameters for that function have been enabled.

ideas.h: Calibration sits behind an access level
ideas.text: In the default settings table, Capture Zero, Capture Span and Step Calibration are Administrator-level functions, while things like Weight Rate are Maintenance level. If calibration functions will not run, check who is signed in before suspecting the scale.

ideas.h: The terminal keeps a calibration memory
ideas.text: The Information Recall options include a Metrology Recall alongside Weight Recall and System Information Recall. The recall screens are the terminal's own record of its metrology information, kept separate from normal weighing.

pre.short: Opens the selection box and accepts the entry in focus.
Enters the setup menu; always present on the home screen.
Returns to the previous setup screen.
Zero key; in calibration, Capture Zero captures the zero point.
Prints records and test results to the attached device.
Move the focus; also page between rows of softkeys.

IND570.refs: References: METTLER TOLEDO IND570 Terminal User's Guide 30205308 | U | 01/2024 — Chapter 2 Operation (softkeys and icons, data entry), Chapter 3 Configuration (softkeys), Appendix A Default Settings, Appendix C key codes.

IND780.name: IND780
IND780.intro: The IND780 front panel is a color graphic display with five softkeys along the bottom, four application keys (A1 to A4), a 12-key numeric keypad, and five navigation keys. The icons on the screen tell you what the softkeys do on that screen.
menus: Getting in: the SETUP softkey is always on the home screen. Press it to open the setup parameters and procedures of the instrument. The SETUP and INFORMATION RECALL softkeys can be moved to other positions, but they can never be deleted.

Moving around: the five navigation keys move the focus through the setup menu tree and within setup and application screens. As a different position gains the focus, its assignment is shown in text near the bottom of the screen.
Changing a setting: press the ENTER key to open the selection box, use the UP or DOWN navigation keys to scroll until the focus is on the desired selection, then press ENTER again to take it.
Getting out: the EXIT softkey saves any changes and returns to the setup menu tree.

More softkey rows: when more softkeys are defined than fit on one row, a MORE DOWN or MORE UP symbol shows at the lower right of the home screen. Press the DOWN navigation key for the next row of softkeys, and UP to come back.

keys.does: The take-it key. Press ENTER to open a selection box and to accept the assignment or selection that is in focus; setup steps throughout the book are confirmed with ENTER.

Five navigation keys sit below the numeric keypad. They move you through the setup options in the menu tree and within setup and application screens, and page between rows of softkeys on the home screen.
Provides access to the setup parameters and procedures of the instrument. This softkey is always present; it can be moved to another position but not deleted.
Provides access to the Recall screens: Weight Recall (current gross, tare and net values), System Information, Metrology Recall, and Totals Recall.
On setup screens, EXIT saves any changes and returns to the setup menu tree.
Four keys below the softkeys that can be defined to perform functions including display adjustments, calibration testing, triggering custom outputs, and switching between units.
The terminal's 12-key numeric keypad, on the right side of the front panel, is used to enter data and commands. Alphanumeric data may also be entered using the softkeys or an external USB keyboard.
One of the scale function keys (an external keyboard's F7 also works as Zero). In calibration, Capture Zero resets the zero condition of the scale.
One of the scale function keys (an external keyboard's F8 also works as Tare). Softkey assignments for tare functions are configured on the Application Keys setup screen.
Prints the selected memory or report to an attached peripheral. After a calibration test runs to completion, the PRINT softkey prints the calibration test report.

lights.does: Displayed at the lower-right corner of the Home screen, to the far right of the softkey icons, when more softkey selections are available. Press the DOWN navigation key to display the additional softkey icons.
Displayed on the last available screen of softkeys when more softkey selections are available above. Press the UP navigation key to return to the previous set of softkey icons.
A line reserved at the top of the display to show system messages and any asynchronous errors. This is where the terminal reports problems while you work.

ideas.h: Softkeys are labels, not fixed buttons
ideas.text: The five keys along the bottom of the display do whatever the icons above them say on that screen. Three sets of five softkeys can be configured, up to 15 functions, and they are paged with the UP and DOWN navigation keys.

ideas.h: An icon on the home page does not switch the function on
ideas.text: Adding a softkey to the home pages of the terminal does not automatically enable the softkey's function; most softkeys must also be enabled in Setup. For example, adding the UNITS SWITCHING softkey does not enable units switching unless the units are also enabled in the Scale branch of setup.

ideas.h: The terminal remembers its last calibration
ideas.text: Metrology Recall, reached from the INFORMATION RECALL softkey, shows the firmware version number and the time and date of the last calibration. When a scale's calibration history is in question, that screen is the first place to look.

ideas.h: Two keys can never be deleted
ideas.text: There must always be one instance each of the INFORMATION RECALL and SETUP softkeys. They can be moved, and copies can exist, but the original cannot be deleted until the same softkey has been assigned in a new position, so the terminal always keeps a door into setup.

pre.short: Opens the selection box and takes the choice in focus.
Always on the home screen; opens the setup parameters.
Saves changes and returns to the setup menu tree.
Zero key; in calibration, Capture Zero resets the scale's zero condition.
Move the focus through menus and screens; page softkey rows.
Prints the calibration test report when the test is complete.

IND780.refs: References: METTLER TOLEDO IND780 Technical Manual 64057242 | 15 | 05/2021 — Chapter 1 Display and Keyboard, Chapter 2 Operating Instructions (icons and functions, keyboard), Chapter 3 Configuration (softkeys), Appendix E Softkey Mapping.

IQ 210.name: IQ 210
IQ 210.intro: The IQ Plus 210 front panel has a six-digit LED weight display, seven LED annunciators, and only two piezo keys. The same two keys do the normal weighing jobs and, in setup mode, move through menus and edit numbers.
menus: To enter setup mode, remove the large fillister-head screw from the enclosure backplate, push a screwdriver or similar tool into the access hole, and press the setup switch once. The display changes to CONFIG.

The setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, DIG IN, DEFLT, and VERS. UNITS/RIGHT moves right on the same menu level, wraps from VERS back to CONFIG, and scrolls parameters; ZERO/ENTER moves down into parameters and values.
At the value level, UNITS/RIGHT scrolls through the values and wraps back to the first value. ZERO/ENTER chooses the value shown and returns to the parameter prompt.
For a number, UNITS/RIGHT chooses the flashing digit and ZERO/ENTER changes it. After the last digit, UNITS/RIGHT stops the flashing; ZERO/ENTER saves the number and returns to the level above.

keys.does: In normal use, remove all weight, wait for the Motion LED to go out, then press ZERO to zero the gross weight. The Zero annunciator lights when the scale is zeroed; in setup mode this key is ZERO/ENTER.
Press UNITS to change the display between primary and alternate units when alternate units are configured; if none are configured, the display does not change. In setup mode this key is UNITS/RIGHT.

lights.does: The displayed value is negative.
The scale is within 0.25 graduations of zero, and it lights when the scale is zeroed.
The scale is in motion, outside the specified motion band. Zeroing and print operations happen only when the Motion LED is off.
The displayed weight is in pounds.
The displayed weight is in kilograms.
The displayed weight is in ounces; lb and oz lit together mean pounds and ounces.
The displayed weight is in grams.

ideas.h: Two keys, two jobs
ideas.text: The panel only has ZERO and UNITS, so setup mode gives those same keys second jobs. UNITS becomes RIGHT for scrolling, and ZERO becomes ENTER for moving down a level, choosing a value, and changing a digit.

ideas.h: Wait for Motion to go out
ideas.text: The Motion annunciator means the scale is still moving outside its motion band. The book's zeroing step is to clear the scale, wait until Motion goes out, and only then press ZERO.

ideas.h: Menus wrap around
ideas.text: The setup display moves in levels: menus across the top, parameters below them, and values below the parameters. Scrolling right can wrap from the last item back to the first instead of stopping at the end.

pre.short: ZERO zeroes the scale; in setup it is also ENTER.
UNITS changes units; in setup it moves RIGHT.
Zero light on means the scale is zeroed.
Wait until Motion is off before zeroing or printing.

IQ 210.refs: References: IQ Plus 210 Installation Manual: Overview and front panel PDF p.7, Operations and LED annunciators PDF p.8, Front Panel Configuration PDF p.17, and Front Panel Calibration PDF p.25.

IQ 310A.name: IQ 310A
IQ 310A.intro: The IQ 310A can be configured and calibrated entirely from its five front-panel keys once the rear Operate/Setup Switch is placed in SETUP. The same five keys have one set of jobs in Operate mode and a different set of menu jobs in Setup mode.
menus: Put the rear-panel Operate/Setup Switch in SETUP to enter SETUP mode. In SETUP, the front-panel keys stop doing their Operate jobs and become menu keys.
The menu has three levels: Menu Heading, Parameter Name, and Parameter Selection. Left and right arrows move across a level; up and down arrows move between levels.

Setup key map: ZERO moves up, GROSS/NET moves down, TARE is ENTER, UNITS moves left, and PRINT moves right. Press TARE/Enter to enter a value, and TARE also moves to the next parameter; pressing UP or DOWN also selects and enters a parameter.

For a numeric value, left and right choose the digit to change and the chosen digit blinks. Up and down raise or lower that digit, and TARE stores the entry; to leave an XX... value unchanged, press TARE before touching the up or down keys.

TEST is entered only from SETUP by pressing TARE and UNITS together, and PRINT exits TEST. Do not press TARE and UNITS together again while TEST is displayed: that replaces stored data with defaults and loses calibration constants.

keys.does: In Operate mode, sets the scale display to 0 while in Gross mode and within the zero band/range. In Setup mode, ZERO is the Move UP key.
In Operate mode, toggles between Gross and Net weight display. In Setup mode, GROSS/NET is the Move DOWN key.
In Operate mode, performs Auto Tare or Tare In/Out as selected in Setup. In Setup mode, TARE is ENTER for menu selections and stored values.
In Operate mode, toggles between lb and kg when either LB or KG is selected in Setup. In Setup mode, UNITS is the Move LEFT key.
In Operate mode, sends print data to the printer when the scale is not in motion and gross weight is above zero and below full scale. In Setup mode, PRINT is the Move RIGHT key.

lights.does: A tare has been acquired and stored by the system.
A preset tare was keyed in at the front panel or entered through an EDP command.
A solid rhombus means tare was acquired by a front-panel key or digital input; a blinking rhombus means the tare was keyed in or acquired through EDP.
The scale is at standstill, not in motion.
The displayed weight is net weight.
The displayed weight is Gross/Brutto weight.
Gross or net weight is within plus or minus 0.25 display divisions of zero.
The unit annunciators show whether the displayed weight is in pounds or kilograms.

ideas.h: The rear switch changes the keys
ideas.text: The five front keys do not keep one fixed job. In Operate mode they zero, tare, change units, switch gross/net, and print; in SETUP mode they become up, down, enter, left, and right for the menu flowchart.

ideas.h: TARE is the Enter key
ideas.text: Setup navigation is built around TARE. It enters a shown value and also steps on to the next parameter, while the up and down keys can also select and enter a parameter when you move off it.

ideas.h: Standstill and zero range gate the keys
ideas.text: Front-panel zero only works inside the zero range, and the motion band decides when the scale counts as stable. That is why PRINT refuses to send while the scale is moving and ZERO refuses outside its allowed band.

ideas.h: The tare lights tell where tare came from
ideas.text: T means a tare is stored, pT means it was keyed in or sent by EDP, and the rhombus adds the same story: solid for a key or input acquisition, blinking for a keyed or EDP tare.

pre.short: TARE tares in Operate; in Setup it is ENTER.
ZERO zeroes in Gross within the zero range; Setup UP.
PRINT prints when still; in Setup it moves RIGHT.
GROSS/NET switches weight mode; Setup DOWN.
UNITS changes lb/kg; in Setup it moves LEFT.
Standstill on means the scale is not in motion.

IQ 310A.refs: References: IQ 310A manual: Keyboard Functions and annunciators PDF p.5-6, Using the IQ 310A Menu in SETUP Mode PDF p.17, Calibration menu instructions PDF p.27, and Test Menu warning PDF p.26.

IQ 355.name: IQ 355
IQ 355.intro: The IQ plus 355 is a single-channel digital weight indicator with a large six-digit LED display and a five-button front-panel keypad. Eight LED annunciators show mode, zero, standstill, and units next to the weight.
menus: In setup mode, the five weighing keys take on the arrow jobs printed under them: up, down, enter, left, and right. Read the symbol under each key before moving, because the same keys navigate menus, choose digits inside numbers, and raise or lower values.
The top-level setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, P FORMT, DIG IN, ALGOUT, and VERSION.

Test mode is entered by pressing and holding the setup switch until the display shows TEST; after about three seconds it shifts to A/DTST. Because the Test Menu functions are all on one level, the GROSS/NET key has no function there, and the ZERO key exits test mode.

keys.does: In gross mode, remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, then press ZERO to zero the scale. The center-of-zero annunciator lights to show the scale is zeroed.
Switches the display between gross and net weight. When a tare has been entered or acquired, net weight is gross weight minus the tare.
Performs the front-panel tare operation and acquires a tare, the same operation the KTARE EDP command requests.
Switches the displayed weight between the configured primary and secondary units, shown by the lb and kg unit annunciators.
Sends formatted weight data to the serial ports, the operation requested by the KPRINT EDP command; printing is one of the operations the book ties to the standstill annunciator.

lights.does: The displayed weight is gross weight.
The displayed weight is net weight.
Gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero; it lights when the scale is zeroed.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Some operations, including tare and printing, can only be done when standstill is shown.
Pounds unit annunciator; it can also serve as the primary-units LED for tn, t, and NONE unit setups.
Kilograms unit annunciator; it can also serve as the secondary-units LED for tn, t, and NONE unit setups.
The displayed weight is in ounces.
The displayed weight is in grams.

ideas.h: Keys wear two sets of labels
ideas.text: The normal-mode name is printed on each key, and the setup-mode arrow is printed under it. In setup, those arrows move through menus, pick the digit to change, and raise or lower the value.

ideas.h: Net is gross minus tare
ideas.text: The GROSS/NET key only changes what you are looking at. If a tare is in the system, the net display is the gross weight with that tare subtracted.

ideas.h: Standstill is the green light for work
ideas.text: The standstill annunciator says the scale is settled inside its motion band. The book makes operations such as tare and printing wait for that sign instead of trusting a moving number.

ideas.h: Unit LEDs can be stand-ins
ideas.text: For lb and kg setups the unit LEDs mean pounds and kilograms directly. For tn, t, or NONE setups, the lb LED marks primary units and the kg LED marks secondary units.

pre.short: ZERO zeroes the scale in gross mode.
TARE acquires a tare from the front panel.
GROSS/NET switches between gross and net.
UNITS switches primary and secondary units.
PRINT sends formatted weight data to the serial ports.
Standstill shown means tare and print are allowed.

IQ 390-DC.name: IQ 390-DC
IQ 390-DC.intro: The IQ plus 390-DC is a battery-powered single-channel indicator with a 1-inch six-digit LCD and a six-button keypad. The panel runs normal weighing, piece counting, and setup menus, and it can run on six C batteries or an AC adapter.
menus: To enter setup mode, remove the large fillister-head screw from the enclosure backplate, push a screwdriver or similar tool into the access hole, and press the setup switch once. The display shows CONFIG.

The main setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, P FORMT, and VERSION. UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same level; ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down to different levels; TARE is Enter.
To pick a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group shows, then move down into the submenu and parameter. The first value shown is the default or the value chosen before.
To change a parameter value, scroll left or right through the choices. Press the key shown under the value to select it and move back up one level.
Numeric values are edited right on the panel with the keypad keys; the prompt area shows the value while you work through its digits.

keys.does: Sets gross weight to zero. In setup mode, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between menu levels.
Switches between gross, net, and piece count modes. With a tare entered or acquired, net weight is gross weight minus tare; the same key returns from counting to normal weighing.
Acquires a tare in normal weighing. In setup mode, TARE is the Enter key used to select parameter values.
Switches the display between primary and secondary units. In setup mode, UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level.
Sends data to the serial port; on a print ticket, wait for the standstill annunciator and then press PRINT. In setup mode, PRINT scrolls right with UNITS.
Turns the indicator power on and off.

lights.does: The displayed weight is gross weight.
The displayed weight is net weight.
Gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero; it lights when the scale is zeroed.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Zero, tare, and printing can only be done when standstill is shown.
A tare value has been entered using the TARE key or the KTARE EDP command.
Battery charge is low.
Top arrow for primary units, set up as pounds in the book's example.
Middle arrow for secondary units, set up as kilograms in the book's example.

ideas.h: MODE is really GROSS/NET
ideas.text: The same GROSS/NET key is also the MODE key. From normal weighing it enters piece count mode, where the display shows a count and the bottom arrow points to PC instead of showing weight.

ideas.h: A weak sample gets refused
ideas.text: Piece counting trusts the sample you teach it. If the sample weight is too small, the indicator asks for a larger sample instead of building a count on a shaky average piece weight.

ideas.h: Standstill gates the everyday keys
ideas.text: Zero, tare, and printing all wait for the standstill annunciator. The display is telling you the scale is settled enough for the number to mean something.

ideas.h: Setup hides behind a screw
ideas.text: Most configuration and calibration work is locked behind setup mode, and getting in is physical: remove the backplate screw, reach through the access hole, and press the setup switch until CONFIG shows.

pre.short: TARE acquires tare; in setup it is ENTER.
ZERO sets gross weight to zero.
PRINT sends data to the serial port.
UNITS switches units; setup scrolls left/right.
GROSS/NET switches weighing and count modes.
Standstill must show before zero, tare, or print.

IQ 510.name: IQ 510
IQ 510.intro: The IQ plus 510 front panel pairs a five-button keypad with a seven-digit vacuum fluorescent weight display, a two-character units annunciator field, and a sixteen-character prompt field. Normal mode weighs; setup mode, reached with a switch behind the backplate, configures and calibrates.
menus: Most procedures, including configuration and calibration, need setup mode. Remove the large fillister-head screw from the backplate, push a screwdriver or similar tool into the access hole, and press the setup switch once; the display shows CONFIG.

Setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT, DIG IN, ALGOUT, and VERSION. UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same level; ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between levels; TARE is Enter.
To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group shows, then move down to the submenu and parameter. Default values and previously chosen values appear first.
To change a value, scroll left or right through the choices and press the Enter key (TARE) to select it. Numeric values are edited from the front panel keys, digit by digit.
Test mode is diagnostic and is entered with the setup switch by holding it until TEST shows. The Test Menu is all on one level, GROSS/NET has no function there, and ZERO exits test mode.

keys.does: Sets the gross weight to zero; the center-of-zero annunciator lights when the scale is zeroed. In setup mode, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between menu levels.
Switches the displayed weight between gross and net. When a tare is in the system, net is gross weight minus tare; in setup mode it moves between menu levels with ZERO.
Acquires a tare. In setup mode, TARE is the Enter key for selecting parameter values.
Switches the weight display between primary and secondary units. In setup mode, UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level.
Sends print data from the indicator. In setup mode, PRINT scrolls left and right through menus, parameters, and values with UNITS.

lights.does: The displayed weight is gross weight, shown as Brutto in OIML regulatory mode.
The displayed weight is net weight.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band; operations such as zero, tare, and printing wait for standstill.
The gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of acquired zero; it lights when the scale is zeroed.
Two-character units annunciator for the displayed weight: lb, kg, oz, T, t, LT, g, or GN, and it can be set to NONE.
Shown in the secondary display area along with lb or oz when troy pounds or troy ounces are configured as primary or secondary units.

ideas.h: Regulation rewrites TARE and ZERO
ideas.text: TARE and ZERO do not have one fixed behavior. Under NTEP, CANADA, OIML, or NONE, the same press can acquire a tare, clear a tare, zero the scale, or do nothing, depending on weight and whether a tare is already in the system.

ideas.h: OIML changes the rules and the label
ideas.text: In OIML mode the scale must be in gross mode before ZERO will zero it; pressing ZERO in net mode clears the tare instead. OIML also swaps the Gross annunciator for Brutto.

ideas.h: Three display areas, three jobs
ideas.text: The big seven-digit area carries the weight, the two-character field carries units, and the sixteen-character prompt field talks to you. Mode and status signs such as Gross, Net, standstill, and center of zero ride in the display fields with the weight.

ideas.h: Setup is a physical switch, not a key combo
ideas.text: Configuration and calibration sit behind the setup switch in the backplate access hole. Once the seal is on and the indicator is back in normal mode, the panel is for weighing only.

pre.short: TARE acquires tare; in setup it is ENTER.
ZERO sets gross weight to zero.
PRINT sends print data; setup scrolls with UNITS.
UNITS switches units; setup scrolls left/right.
GROSS/NET switches gross and net display.
Standstill means the scale is settled for key work.

IQ 590-DC.name: IQ 590-DC
IQ 590-DC.intro: The IQ plus 590-DC is a portable counting indicator with a 1-inch six-digit LCD and a 19-button keypad, powered by six C batteries or an AC adapter. The panel weighs in gross and net, counts pieces from a taught sample, and runs setup menus from the same keys.
menus: To enter setup mode, remove the large fillister-head screw from the enclosure backplate, push a screwdriver or similar tool into the access hole, and press the setup switch once. The display shows CONFIG.

The main setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, P FORMT, and VERSION. UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same level; ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between levels; TARE is Enter.
To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the desired menu group shows, then move down to the submenu and parameter. The default or previously selected value appears first.
To change a parameter value, scroll left or right through the values, then press TARE (Enter) to select the value and move back up one level.
Numeric values are typed with the numeric keypad instead of scrolled digit by digit.

keys.does: Sets gross weight to zero. In setup mode, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between menu levels.
Switches between gross, net, and piece count modes; if piece counting is disabled, it switches only between gross and net. With a tare in the system, net weight is gross weight minus tare.
Acquires a tare. In setup mode, TARE serves as the Enter key for selecting parameter values.
Switches the display between primary and secondary units. In setup mode, UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level.
Sends data to the serial port. In count mode, PRINT sends the CFMT print format; in setup mode it scrolls left and right with UNITS.
Types numbers directly for values, including sample sizes, piece weight, and numeric parameter entries in setup and counting.
In piece count mode, displays the current piece weight; the same DISPLAY TARE key is used to view the stored tare information for the scale.
Turns the indicator power on and off.

lights.does: The displayed weight is gross weight.
The displayed weight is net weight.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band. Zero, tare, and printing can only be done when standstill is shown.
Gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero; it lights when the scale is zeroed.
A tare value was entered using the TARE key or the KTARE EDP command.
Battery charge is low.
The right-side lb arrow marks primary units, pounds in the book's setup.
The right-side kg arrow marks secondary units, kilograms in the book's setup; the third arrow position is the PC piece-count marker.

ideas.h: Counting is taught, not guessed
ideas.text: The indicator counts by learning an average piece weight from a sample. SAMPLE steps through sample sizes of 5, 10, 20, 50, or 100, the keypad can key a custom sample size, and the display shows a counting prompt while it acquires the sample weight.

ideas.h: A bad sample gets sent back
ideas.text: If the sample weight is too small or unstable, the indicator asks for more pieces or a larger quantity instead of counting from a weak sample. Insufficient sample weight means the requested sample count was not reached.

ideas.h: The 19 keys change jobs in setup
ideas.text: The five weighing keys become the menu controls: UNITS and PRINT go left and right, ZERO and GROSS/NET go up and down, and TARE is Enter. The numeric keypad keeps its plain job and types values directly.

ideas.h: Standstill still runs the panel
ideas.text: Battery power and counting do not change the weighing rule. Zero, tare, and printing wait until the standstill annunciator shows the scale has settled.

pre.short: TARE acquires tare; in setup it is ENTER.
ZERO sets gross weight to zero.
PRINT sends data; setup scrolls left/right.
Keypad types sample sizes and numeric values.
GROSS/NET switches gross, net, and count modes.
Standstill must show before zero, tare, or print.

IQ 710.name: IQ 710
IQ 710.intro: The IQ plus 710 front panel is a 29-button keypad with a seven-digit vacuum fluorescent weight display, a two-character annunciator field, and a sixteen-character prompt field. Beyond the five weighing keys it carries a numeric keypad, setpoint and time/date keys, macro keys, and alpha entry for setup work.
menus: Most procedures, including configuration and calibration, need setup mode. Remove the fillister-head screw from the backplate, push a screwdriver or similar tool into the access hole, and press the setup switch once; the display shows CONFIG.

The main setup menus are CONFIG, FORMAT, CALIBR, SERIAL, PROGRM, PFORMT, SETPTS, DIG IN, ALGOUT, and VERSION. UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same level; ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between levels; TARE is Enter.
To select a parameter, scroll left or right until the menu group shows, then move down to the parameter. Scroll left or right through its values and confirm with TARE to select.

Numbers are typed on the numeric keypad: key the value, then press ENTER or a function key to accept it. Front-panel print-format editing uses the same keypad, with CLEAR erasing digits and SETPOINT, ENTER, and the decimal point handling characters.
Keyboard locks live in the Program menu: the keypad can be fully active, macro-only, zero-only, or fully disabled, and alpha entry can be switched off, which also disables the ALPHA ENTRY key.

keys.does: Zeroes the scale: in gross mode, remove all weight, wait for the standstill annunciator, then press ZERO and the center-of-zero annunciator lights. In setup mode, ZERO and GROSS/NET move up and down between menu levels.
Switches the display between gross and net weight; net is gross minus tare when a tare is in the system. In setup mode it moves up and down between menu levels with ZERO.
Acquires a container tare: place the container, wait for standstill, and press TARE. In setup mode, TARE is the Enter key for selecting parameter values.
Switches the weight display between primary and secondary units. In setup mode, UNITS and PRINT scroll left and right on the same menu level.
Sends print data from the indicator. In setup mode, PRINT scrolls left and right through menus, parameters, and values with UNITS.
Types numbers for values such as setpoints and numeric setup entries; each number is keyed in and then accepted with a function key or ENTER.
Accepts a keyed value, such as a new setpoint value typed on the numeric keypad. The ENTER digital input and EDP key give the same function as the front-panel ENTER key.
Erases digits and special-function values. With a setpoint displayed, CLEAR turns the setpoint off; in panel editing it backs out and clears alpha entry.
Shows setpoint values so they can be viewed, changed with the numeric keypad and ENTER, or turned off with CLEAR. Repeated presses step through the setpoints.
Press once to display the date and a second time to display the time.
Puts the panel into alpha entry for text-style entries; in that mode the front-panel keys work like a telephone keypad to pick letters.
Programmable macro keys F1 through F4. Under the MACONLY keyboard lock, these are the only front-panel keys allowed in normal mode.

lights.does: The displayed weight is gross weight; shown as Brutto in OIML regulatory mode.
The displayed weight is net weight.
The scale is at standstill or within the specified motion band; zero, tare, and print style operations wait for it.
The gross weight is within 0.25 graduations of zero; it lights when the scale is zeroed.
Two-character annunciator showing the unit of the displayed weight: lb, kg, oz, T, t, LT, g, or GND, and it can be set to NONE.
Shown in the two-digit annunciator field in addition to lb or oz when troy pounds or ounces are configured.
Numeric entry mode: the two-digit annunciator field shows NE while the panel is taking a number for some operations.
Alpha entry mode: the two-digit annunciator field shows AE while the panel is taking letters for some operations.

ideas.h: The display has a prompt line, not just digits
ideas.text: The seven big digits carry the weight while a sixteen-character prompt field talks back with menu names and entry prompts. A two-character field shows units, or NE and AE when the panel is taking numeric or alpha entry.

ideas.h: Regulation rewrites TARE and ZERO
ideas.text: As on its smaller siblings, the TARE and ZERO keys change behavior with the REGULAT setting. A press can acquire tare, clear tare, zero the scale, or do nothing at all, depending on the mode and whether a tare is already in the system.

ideas.h: Keys can be locked down
ideas.text: The Program menu can disable the whole keypad, allow only the F1-F4 macro keys, or leave only ZERO alive. A dead key on this panel may be locked on purpose, not broken.

ideas.h: Setpoints are front-panel work
ideas.text: Setpoint values can be viewed, changed with the numeric keypad and ENTER, and turned off with CLEAR right from the panel. Some configurations lock that ability or put it behind a password.

pre.short: TARE acquires tare; in setup it is ENTER.
ZERO zeroes the scale in gross mode.
PRINT sends print data; setup scrolls menus.
Keypad types setpoints and numeric values.
ENTER accepts a keyed value.
Standstill means the scale is settled and ready.

IQ 800/810.name: IQ 800/810
IQ 800/810.intro: The IQ 800/810 front panel combines direct function keys, a numeric keypad, and LED annunciators, and it can run up to four scale channels plus a total channel. The panel handles weighing, tare entry, accumulators, setpoints, time and date, and truck in/out ID work.
menus: Numbers are entered on the numeric keypad digit by digit, and the entry only counts when ENTER or a function key follows it. If no confirming key is pressed within several seconds, the display reverts to the previous mode and the number is ignored; pressing G/N on an unconfirmed number erases it and returns to normal mode.

The configuration menu map runs CONFIG, SETALG, FORMAT, SETPNTS, SERIAL, PFORMT, DIG IN, ALGOUT, BARGF, CALIBRT, and VERSION. The Print Format menu's own first level is GFMT, NFMT, TRWIN, TRWOUT, and SPFMT.

Print formats can be edited at the panel: SETPOINT and CLEAR raise and lower the ASCII character value, DISP ACCUM and DISP ROC scroll the format string, and the numeric keypad, ENTER, and decimal point enter characters and numbers directly.

SETPOINT is its own front-panel routine: press SETPOINT to see SP 1 and its value, press again to step through setpoints, key a number and press ENTER to change a value, and press CLEAR to turn a setpoint off.
Accumulators are worked from the panel with DISP ACCUM to view, PRINT to print the displayed accumulated weight, and DISP ACCUM then CLEAR twice to clear a register; G/N cancels the clear prompt.

keys.does: Used to enter numeric values such as tare weights and ID numbers. Each digit appears on the display as it is entered; follow the number with ENTER and/or a function key or it is ignored after several seconds.
Accepts a keyed number or a function value. It stores a new setpoint value, accepts new date and time entries, and displays a stored truck weight from the DISP TARE lookup.
Resets the scale gross weight to zero. It cannot be used when the scale is in motion or when the displayed weight is outside the configured zero range.

Toggles between Gross and Net display modes, lighting the G or NET annunciator. It also returns the panel to normal weighing mode from another mode and erases a keyed number that has not been confirmed.

Captures the current gross weight as tare and switches to net mode; gross weight must be positive and the scale at standstill. Tare values can also be keyed with the numeric keypad and TARE, or supplied by EDP.
Toggles between primary and secondary units; the standard key label shows pounds/kilograms, though other units can be defined in setup.
In normal mode with the scale at standstill, sends data to the serial port. From normal weighing, PRINT also adds the displayed weight to the total accumulator.

In normal weighing mode, displays the current tare register weight and lights the T annunciator. In truck in/out mode, key a truck ID and press DISP TARE to look the truck up; ENTER then displays its stored weight.

Erases digits from a numeric entry, one digit per press, and clears special-function values. It clears accumulators and the tare register through a two-press confirm prompt, and turns off displayed setpoints.

Displays the current accumulator register weight and lights the accumulator annunciators one at a time. Press repeatedly to scroll the five accumulators, or enter an accumulator number 0-4 and press DISP ACCUM.
Shows defined setpoint values, starting with SP 1, then steps through the rest. Key a new value and press ENTER to change it; press CLEAR to turn a setpoint off until OFF appears.
Selects the individual scale channel or the total channel for display. The scale number LED lights for the channel shown, and more than one LED lights when sources are totaled together.

lights.does: Pounds unit LED. When pounds are the primary units, the Lb LED is the primary units annunciator.
Kilograms unit LED. When pounds are primary, the Kg LED serves as the secondary units annunciator, and the roles swap when kilograms are primary.
The displayed weight is gross weight.
The displayed weight is net weight.
A tare is in the system.
The tare in the system was manually entered with the numeric keypad or supplied by EDP, rather than captured from the scale.
Rate-of-change LED: lights when the rate of change feature is active.
Accumulator annunciator: lights with the accumulator displays to show which accumulator register is being viewed.

ideas.h: A keyed number expires
ideas.text: The numeric keypad writes each digit to the display as you type, but the number is not real until ENTER or a function key takes it. Wait several seconds and the panel throws the number away and returns to the previous mode.

ideas.h: T and pT tell how tare got there
ideas.text: A plain T with the rhombus means a tare is in the system from a weighed capture, keyed entry, or EDP. The pT annunciator narrows it down: that tare was keyed in by hand or sent through EDP.

ideas.h: Printing an accumulator is not adding to it
ideas.text: With an accumulator displayed, PRINT prints the accumulated weight but does not add the current scale weight to it. Accumulating happens from normal weighing, when PRINT adds the displayed value to the total accumulator.

ideas.h: The total accumulator is its own register
ideas.text: Accumulator 0 is called the total accumulator, but it is not the sum of accumulators 1 through 4. Weight lands in it only when an add is directed to accumulator 0.

pre.short: ENTER accepts a keyed number or value.
Keypad types tare weights, IDs, and values.
ZERO resets gross weight to zero in range.
TARE captures a positive, still gross weight as tare.
PRINT sends data when the scale is at standstill.
G/N switches Gross/Net and cancels entries.

Panther.name: Panther
Panther.intro: The PANTHER terminal has a seven-character, seven-segment vacuum fluorescent display and a six-function membrane keypad. The harsh environment model adds five multi-colored LEDs that show over or under tolerance conditions for manual checkweighing.
menus: Walking the blocks: programming is a chain of F-blocks. At a block prompt such as [F6], press PRINT to continue into the block, or press SELECT to skip to the next block, for example from [F6] to [F7].
Answering a prompt: PRINT accepts the value shown and goes to the next prompt. CLEAR zeroes the display so you can start entry of a new value.
Backing up: ZERO backs up to the previous prompt, such as from [P1] back to [SP2]. Note that you cannot use the ZERO key to back up through the setpoints.

When the numbers fight: if a new setpoint value is less than the existing preact value, or a preact is greater than its setpoint, [E 20] is displayed for approximately 2 seconds to flag the error, and then the display returns to the entry prompt.
Reading a capture: calibration and analog output captures show a countdown display such as [15 CAL] while the reading is taken. Pressing CLEAR during the countdown aborts the span adjust.

keys.does: The proceed key of the programming language: accepts the entry shown and goes to the next prompt. At capture prompts such as [0 Ld], press PRINT to acknowledge that the desired weight is on the scale.
Zeroes the display and starts entry of a new value. At some prompts CLEAR instead skips ahead to the next sub-block, and during a span-adjust countdown CLEAR aborts the adjustment.
Backs up to the previous programming prompt (for example, [P1] back to [SP2], or [SP2] back to [F5.7]). It cannot be used to back up through the setpoints.
Skips ahead without entering the current block, for example SELECT at [F6] skips to [F7], and at setpoint entry SELECT moves to the other setpoints.
Pushbutton tare. The serial input commands duplicate the front panel keyboard functions, and the T command takes a pushbutton tare, which is always active.
Pushbutton target in over/under mode only; the serial X command duplicates this front panel function.

lights.does: One of the five multi-colored zone status LEDs on the harsh environment terminal, which indicate over or under tolerance conditions for manual checkweighing. The low zone width is edited at F5.8.4.
One of the five zone status LEDs; its zone width is edited at F5.8.3 (EDIT LOW ACCEPT ZONE). In setpoint applications, the LEDs instead indicate the status of the individual setpoints.

The center zone status LED of the five: checkweighing gives each target five zones, and the LEDs show which side of tolerance the weight falls on. In setpoint applications the same LEDs show setpoint status.
One of the five zone status LEDs; its zone width is edited at F5.8.2 (EDIT HIGH ACCEPT ZONE).
One of the five zone status LEDs for the over-tolerance side; its zone width is edited at F5.8.1 (EDIT HIGH ZONE).

ideas.h: Four keys are the whole programming language
ideas.text: Every programming prompt in the book is answered with the same small vocabulary: PRINT accepts and proceeds, SELECT skips to the next block, ZERO backs up one prompt, and CLEAR wipes the entry so you can type fresh. Learn those four and the F-blocks stop being a maze.

ideas.h: Setpoint math: cutoff equals setpoint minus preact
ideas.text: Values entered for preact adjust the corresponding cutoff action: setpoint actuation equals setpoint entry minus preact entry. If the numbers are inconsistent, the terminal flags [E 20] for about two seconds and returns to the prompt instead of accepting them.

ideas.h: No motion, no print
ideas.text: All demand mode printing is inhibited during motion and when the weight is under gross zero. If the printer will not print, look at the scale state first; the terminal is refusing on purpose.

ideas.h: Diagnostics live in F6
ideas.text: The F6 Diagnostics block holds the expanded display, the Edit Calibration Factors sub-block (zero factor and span factors available for numeric data editing), display of individual load cell counts on DigiTOL, Print Setup, and Reset to Factory Defaults.

pre.short: Accepts the entry and proceeds; acknowledges weight at capture prompts.
Backs up to the previous prompt (not through setpoints).
Zeroes the entry for a fresh value; aborts a capture countdown.
Skips to the next block or the next setpoint.

Panther.refs: References: METTLER TOLEDO PANTHER Terminal Technical Manual E14957000A (10/2008) — Chapter 1 (display/keypad, zone LEDs), Chapter 3 Programming and Configuration (F5 Weigh Mode, F6 Diagnostics, F7 Analog Output), Chapter 11 serial input commands.

SCT-1100.name: SCT-1100
SCT-1100.intro: The SCT-1100 front panel is a six-digit display, six LED annunciators, and a five-key keyboard. The same five keys run weighing, setup, and number entry, so the book defines each key by the mode you are standing in.
menus: To get into setup, press TARE for a moment during startup. To see the quick setup menu instead, press MODE for a moment during startup; pressing ZERO during startup just displays the current settings.

In setup, ZERO scrolls down through parameters (and lowers a digit while typing), TARE scrolls up (and raises a digit). MODE jumps to the first step of a menu and picks which digit you are editing, left to right.
MODE or PRINT enters a parameter or confirms the setting on display; while typing a number, they confirm the entry you made.
C gets you out: one press exits a step without confirming, pressing it repeatedly brings up the SAvE? prompt. While typing a number, a momentary C press clears the value.

The setup tree itself is short: ConfiG for the scale, SeriaL for communications, inputs and output for the I/O, An.out for the analog output, diAG for diagnostics, and DeFAU to restore defaults, which the book warns cancels the present calibration.

keys.does: Clears the displayed gross weight up to plus or minus 2 percent of capacity, and cancels a tare. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays the current settings. In setup it scrolls parameters; in numeric input it decreases the digit being changed.

A momentary press executes a semiautomatic tare; it also cancels a tare. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays setup mode. A long press allows entering a manual tare from the keyboard. In setup it scrolls parameters; in numeric input it increases the digit.

Executes the specific function assigned in setup. A long press toggles the displayed channel in independent-channels mode. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays the quick setup menu. In setup it enters a parameter or confirms a setting; in numeric input it confirms the entry.

Executes the function assigned in setup, and performs a printout or data transmission on the printer serial port. In setup it enters a parameter or confirms a setting; in numeric input it confirms the entry.

Turns the instrument on and off (press and hold the C side). In setup, press it repeatedly to reach the SAvE? prompt, or press once to exit a step without confirming the setting. In numeric input, a momentary press clears the present value.

lights.does: The weighing system is within a quarter division of zero. If this is not lit, the scale is not at true zero.
The weight is unstable. Readings taken while this is lit are still moving.
A tare is established and the display is measuring net weight.
Lit when the instrument's specification function is active, and whenever a key is pressed. Blinking means the function is active for five seconds.
The first output (Sp1) is activated.
The second output (Sp2) is activated.

ideas.h: Every key does two or three jobs
ideas.text: This transmitter only has five keys, so each one changes meaning with context: at power-up, in weighing, in setup, and while typing a number. Most panel mistakes on this box are just pressing the right key in the wrong moment.

ideas.h: The panel is a window into the load cell
ideas.text: The diagnostic menu shows the converter's microvolts and A/D points for the weight on the scale. That lets you judge what the load cell is actually sending instead of guessing from the weight number alone.

ideas.h: Zero at startup is automatic, within limits
ideas.text: At power-up the instrument zeros itself if the weight on the scale is within plus or minus 10 percent of capacity. Outside that window it shows ZERO, waits, and then displays the weight as it is.

ideas.h: A tare can be locked or fleeting
ideas.text: A locked tare stays in place and shows as a negative value when the scale is unloaded; an unlocked tare cancels itself every time the scale is unloaded. Which kind you have decides what the scale does between loads.

pre.short: Confirms the entry - in setup and number typing, this is the key that takes the value.
One press takes a tare; a press during startup opens setup.
Backs out without saving; press it more than once to reach the SAvE? prompt.
Zeroes the empty scale (up to 2 percent of capacity) and scrolls down in setup.

SCT-20.name: SCT-20
SCT-20.intro: The SCT-20 is a small DIN-rail weight transmitter with an LCD display and a four-key membrane keypad. This extract preserves its LED meanings and its weighing operations, but the individual key labels are thin compared with the larger transmitters, so this draft is deliberately smaller.
menus: Configuration and calibration are gated by the jumper inside the unit: closed, the SCT-20 can be calibrated and configured; removed and sealed, it is locked for Legal for Trade use. In weigh mode the LED annunciators scroll continually to show the jumper is in place.

The calibration menu carries the scale's identity: divisions (resolution), maximum capacity, ZERO for capturing deadload, an estimated dead load value for product that cannot be removed, WEIGHT for span calibration with test weights, and the unit of measure with its display coefficient.
The ZERO menu can also be entered directly from weighing mode to compensate for zero drift, without walking the whole setup tree.
To leave the set-up menu, press the exit key twice, as shown in the unit-of-measure procedure.

The keypad can protect itself: the lock settings can leave the keys free, lock the keypad (a press shows BLOC), or lock keypad and display so the weight is hidden and the model shows instead. Menu items can be locked the same way, and a locked item announces itself with the BLOC alarm.

keys.does: Press and hold for three seconds (or close the Net/Gross input) to capture a semi-automatic tare: the instrument displays the net weight at zero and the NET LED lights. Hold again for three seconds to display the gross weight once more. The semi-automatic tare value is lost when the instrument is turned off, and the operation is not available if the gross weight is zero.
While a tare is active, press and hold to display the gross weight temporarily; when the key is released, the net weight is displayed again.

The ZERO parameter captures the deadload of the scale system with the scale empty, zeroing off the displayed value. The book notes this menu can also be reached directly from weighing mode to compensate for zero changes or variations, and pressing the key there displays the accumulated deadload that has been zeroed off.
Setup is left by pressing the exit key twice to leave the set-up menu, per the unit-of-measure procedure.

lights.does: A tare has been entered and the display is showing net weight. It turns off when the gross weight is displayed again.
The weight is within plus or minus 0.25 divisions of zero. As a secondary function, lit means output 3 is closed.
The weight on the scale is stable. As a secondary function, lit means output 2 is closed.
The unit of measure is kilograms. As a secondary function, lit means output 1 is closed.
The unit of measure is grams. As a secondary function, lit means input 2 is closed.
The unit of measure is pounds. As a secondary function, lit means input 1 is closed.

ideas.h: The LEDs moonlight as I/O indicators
ideas.text: Each front LED has two jobs. Normally they show NET, zero, stability, and the unit; press and hold one key then press another and the same LEDs report output and input states instead. The panel tells you which mode it is in by context, not by extra lights.

ideas.h: The jumper is the gatekeeper
ideas.text: A sealed jumper decides whether the SCT-20 can be calibrated and configured at all. With the jumper closed it ships ready to calibrate; for Legal for Trade use the jumper comes out and a self-destructive seal goes on, and while the jumper is in place the LED annunciators scroll in weigh mode to prove it.

ideas.h: Theoretical calibration versus real weights
ideas.text: The scale can be calibrated from numbers alone: load cell sensitivity and full scale set the span without a single test weight. The book is clear that if theoretical full scale and capacity match, the calibration in use is theoretical; a Weight (span) calibration with real test weights replaces it.

ideas.h: Converted units are not legal weights
ideas.text: A display coefficient can turn kilograms into liters, bar, pieces, and other units. The book warns those converted values have no legal value, and the active LEDs flash while such a value is displayed so nobody mistakes it for a true weight.
