SCT-2200.name: SCT-2200
SCT-2200.intro: The SCT-2200 front panel is a six-digit LED display, six LED annunciators, and a five-key keyboard. The same five keys handle weighing, setup entry, and number entry, so the panel only makes sense once you know which mode each key is serving.
menus: Getting in happens at power-up: press TARE for a moment during startup for setup mode, MODE during startup for the quick setup menu, or ZERO during startup just to display the current settings.

In setup, ZERO and TARE scroll through the parameters; while typing a number they decrease and increase the digit being changed. MODE quickly positions at the first step of a menu and selects the digit to edit, left to right.
PRINT (or MODE, per the setup table) enters a parameter or confirms the setting; while typing, it confirms the entry made.

C is the way back: it exits a step without confirming the setting, and pressing it multiple times displays the SAvE? prompt so you choose whether changes are kept. While typing a number, C clears the present value.
The setup tree runs ConfiG, dsp.rf (display refresh), SeriaL, ini.aL (alibi memory), inputs, output, An.out, and DeFAU, which restores default settings and cancels the present calibration.

keys.does: Clears the displayed gross weight up to plus or minus 2 percent of capacity, and cancels a tare. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays the current settings. In setup it scrolls parameters; in numeric input it decreases the digit being changed.

A momentary press executes semiautomatic tare and cancels a tare. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays setup mode. A long press allows entering a manual tare from the keyboard. In setup it scrolls parameters; in numeric input it increases the digit.

Executes the specific function assigned in setup. At power-up, a momentary press during startup displays the quick setup menu. In setup it quickly positions at the first step of a menu; in numeric input it selects the digit to be modified, moving left to right.

Executes the function assigned in setup, and performs a printout or data transmission on the printer serial port. In setup it enters a parameter or confirms a setting; in numeric input it confirms the entry.

Turns the instrument on and off. In setup, pressing it multiple times displays SAvE? and pressing it exits a step without confirming the setting. In numeric input a momentary press clears the present value; a long press past the off display shows scale information such as capacity, division, and channels.

Lit when the weight is unstable; the reading is still moving.
Lit when a tare is established and the display is measuring net weight.

ideas.h: Diagnostics show the cell, not just the weight
ideas.text: The diagnostic menu displays microvolts, A/D points, calibration points with their weights, and audit counters for configuration and calibration changes. That is the evidence trail for judging a load cell and for seeing whether settings have been touched.

ideas.h: Startup zero is automatic, within limits
ideas.text: The instrument zeros itself at startup when the weight detected is within plus or minus 10 percent of capacity. If it is outside that window, it shows ZERO and after ten seconds displays the weight as it lies.

ideas.h: Tares come in locked and unlocked kinds
ideas.text: A locked tare shows as a negative value when the scale is unloaded and stays until you cancel it; an unlocked tare cancels itself each time the scale is unloaded. The kind in use decides what happens between loads.

SCT-40.name: SCT-40
SCT-40.intro: The SCT-40 is a signal conditioning transmitter/indicator with a small five-key panel: ESC, TARE, PRINT, MENU, and a TEST key. The same five keys run the weighing functions and, with press-and-hold combinations, open and move through all the setup menus.

Inside a menu level, press TARE or PRINT to step through the parameters until the one you want is displayed, then press MENU to select it and move to the next level of configuration.

When setting a value, MENU confirms and advances; ESC escapes from a parameter, cancels, or returns to the previous menu or operation mode. Work your way out by pressing ESC as many times as the procedure shows (often two or three presses).
While you are in the menus, the display symbols light in sequence to remind you that you are looking at a setting, not a weight.

Short press captures the tare; a long press removes the tare, switching between Gross and Net. Inside setup menus it moves to the previous parameter or setting, or scrolls to the next digit when setting a parameter value.
Short press prints the weight; a long press runs the mV load cell test. Inside setup menus it moves to the next parameter in a level, or increments a value when setting a parameter.

Short press sets setpoints and hysteresis. Inside setup menus it moves to the next level of configuration or selects and edits a parameter. Held with ESC it opens the general parameter setup, and held with TARE it opens the preset tare setup.
Press this key to display the load distribution — the top of the display shows the weight on the scale and the bottom shows the load percentage on each active channel.

lights.does: This annunciator indicates a net weight when a semi-automatic tare or preset tare has been set.
The 0 annunciator indicates center of zero, with a deviation from zero of not more than +/- 0.25 divisions.
This annunciator indicates scale stability — the weight is steady enough to trust.
Indicates the unit of measure is kilograms.

ideas.h: One key, two jobs: tare and zero
ideas.text: Semi-automatic tare means one press of TARE takes whatever is on the scale as the tare and shows net; ESC does the same idea for zero. A long press of TARE removes the tare and returns to gross. The NET annunciator tells you which world you are in.

ideas.h: TEST shows how the load is shared
ideas.text: The SCT-40 can watch several load cell channels at once. Pressing TEST shows the total weight on top and each channel's percentage of the load underneath, so a cell that is carrying too much or too little stands out. The same percentages are checked on zero, and a load percentage error raises the ERDIAG alarm.

ideas.h: The keypad can lock itself
ideas.text: Locking parameters can freeze just the keypad, or the keypad and display together; with the lock on, pressing a key shows BLOC. That keeps a running installation from being changed by an accidental key press.

ZM510.name: ZM510
ZM510.intro: The ZM510 front panel is a full keypad: five weighing keys, F1 through F5 softkeys whose labels live on the display, and an alphanumeric keypad for typing. Most keys do two jobs — one in weighing, another in the menus.
menus: Menus are moved with arrow, enter and escape keys. The TARE, SELECT, ZERO, PRINT and UNITS keys also carry navigation arrows (up, down, enter, left, right), and when both are available either set can be used (p.17).
The SETUP key can be used to perform custom application functions, and it can also be used to view the password entry screen for menu access (p.15).
The F keys sometimes take on the arrow and enter functions, and then they are shown on-screen (p.17).

To exit a menu, use the ESC softkey first if one is on the screen. When that key is no longer available, use the up arrow repeatedly until you are asked if you want to save any changes made; use the Up or Down key to choose and press ENTER to accept. The indicator reboots and returns to the startup screen with the new changes active (p.18).

keys.does: Press the TARE key to perform a pushbutton tare function. In the menus it acts as an up arrow key for menu navigation.
Press the SELECT key to toggle between the active display values. In the menus it acts as a down arrow key for menu navigation.
Press the ZERO key to zero the display. In the menus it acts as an ENTER key to accept a displayed value or function.
Press the PRINT key to send information to a peripheral device through a configured communications port. In the menus it acts as a left arrow key for menu navigation.
Press the UNITS key to scroll through the available units of measure while in normal operating mode. In the menus it acts as a right arrow key for menu navigation.
Use the F1 through F5 keys as defined by the label above each one on the display. The functions change according to program need.
Press the ENTER key to accept a displayed choice or access a lower menu level. It duplicates the function of an on-screen softkey Enter arrow.
The SETUP key can be used to perform custom application functions. It can also be used to view the password entry screen for menu access.
If enabled by the program, press the SCALE key to switch between active scales. It also acts as an ESCAPE key when in an entry function or in the menus.

Use the alphanumeric keypad for entering text or numbers. The CAPS key makes one upper case letter (hold it to lock CAPS), and the Num Lock key types a single number or, held down, locks the number function.
Press the START key to start a process defined by the active program.
Press the STOP key to stop a process defined by the active program.

lights.does: The zero annunciator on the display is lit when the weight is inside the center-of-zero window (0.25 or 0.50 division, set in the Display menu). If the Center of Zero light is on all the time the scale is stable; if it blinks, more filtering is required (p.35).
The SP1 annunciator on the display turns on and off with output 1, so you can watch an output work during the output test.
If M-Dash is enabled, the display shows dashes during motion instead of a weight.
CAP appears on the screen when CAPS is armed for one upper case letter, or when the CAPS lock is on.
NUM on the screen means a single number will be typed; solid NUM means the Num Lock is on, so the number function stays locked.

ideas.h: One key, two jobs
ideas.text: The weighing keys carry a second set of jobs in the menus: TARE is up, SELECT is down, ZERO is enter, PRINT is left and UNITS is right. Learn the arrows and you can drive the whole menu system without the F keys.

ideas.h: In the menus, ZERO means take it
ideas.text: On the weight screen ZERO zeroes the display, but inside the menus that same key is the ENTER — it accepts the value or function showing. ENTER on the keypad does the same job.

ideas.h: The softkeys are whatever the screen says
ideas.text: F1 through F5 have no fixed jobs. Each one does what the label above it on the display says, and the functions change according to program need — so read the screen, not the key.

ideas.h: Center of zero tells you the scale has settled
ideas.text: When you are tuning filtering, watch the Center of Zero annunciator in normal weight mode: lit all the time means the scale is stable, blinking means more filtering is required.

pre.short: Zeroes the display on the weight screen — and inside the menus it is the ENTER that takes the value.
Accepts the choice on screen, or steps into the next menu level down.
Pushbutton tare on the weight screen; the up arrow when you are in the menus.
Sends the weight out to a printer or other device; the left arrow in the menus.
Scrolls through the units of measure; the right arrow in the menus.

iQUBE2.name: iQUBE2
iQUBE2.intro: The iQUBE2 is a digital diagnostic junction box, not an indicator. It has no display, no keypad, and no weighing panel of its own; all of its weighing, configuration, and calibration happens through a connected host indicator such as the 920i or the 1280. This short card covers the only hardware on the box itself.
menus: There are no menus on this box. Setup, calibration, and everyday weighing all happen on the connected host indicator, so open the host's own book and use its panel card instead.

keys.does: The one button on the board. Press and release it to assign the board ID; press and hold it for five seconds to reset the board to its defaults.
A small switch block on the board that sets how the box starts up. The box only reads it at power-up, so set it with the power off, then turn the power on.

lights.does: The box's one message light. Blinking once a second means normal operation; if the blinking stops or changes, the box is telling you something is wrong before the host ever sees it.

ideas.h: The panel lives on the host
ideas.text: The iQUBE2 turns load cell signals into digital weight data and hands it to a host indicator such as the 920i or 1280. Every key you will ever press for this system is on that host, which is why this book's panel card is short and the host's card does the talking.

ideas.h: One blink a second means healthy
ideas.text: With no display of its own, the HB1 heartbeat LED is how the box says it is alive. A steady once-a-second blink is normal operation.

iQUBE3.name: iQUBE3
iQUBE3.intro: The iQUBE3 is a digital diagnostic junction box that streams weight data to whatever it is connected to. It has no front panel, display, or keypad of its own; configuration is done from a connected 1280 indicator, from Revolution software, or with serial commands through a command terminal. This short card covers the only hardware on the box itself.
menus: There are no menus on this box. Setup and calibration happen on the connected 1280, in Revolution on a computer, or by typing serial commands, so open the 1280's book and use its panel card instead.

keys.does: Buttons on the four-channel board inside the box, used during board assignment when the system is installed. They are setup hardware for the installer, not buttons an operator presses to weigh.

lights.does: Small lights on the board that show board assignment and activity while the system is being set up. They are the box's only signs, and they speak during installation, not during weighing.

ideas.h: The panel lives on the host
ideas.text: The iQUBE3 sends weight data to whatever it is connected to and takes its orders from there: a 1280 indicator, Revolution software, or serial commands. Every key you will ever press for this system is somewhere else, which is why this book's panel card is short.

ideas.h: Set up through the 1280 wizard
ideas.text: When the host is a 1280, a setup wizard on the 1280 walks through the iQUBE3's configuration. The box itself never asks you anything.

IND570 Install.name: IND570 Install
IND570 Install.intro: The IND570 has five softkey buttons along the bottom of the display, each identified by the graphic icon shown directly above it, plus a 12-key alphanumeric keypad. Up to 15 softkey functions can be shown on three separate rows.
menus: Getting in: the SETUP softkey enters the setup menu. Together with INFORMATION RECALL it must always be present on the home screen; they are in positions 9 and 10 by default.
Moving around: press the UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys to move the focus. As a different position gains the focus, its assignment is shown in text toward the bottom of the screen.
Changing a setting: press the ENTER key to open the assignment selection box, use the UP or DOWN navigation keys to scroll until the desired selection is in focus, then press ENTER to select it.

Getting out: the EXIT softkey returns from an edit screen to the previous setup screen. If you are typing letters and chose the wrong group, the ESCAPE softkey ends the entry without accepting any of the new data.

More softkey rows: a MORE DOWN symbol at the lower-right corner of the screen means more softkey selections are available. Press the DOWN navigation key to display the additional screens, and UP to come back.

While entering data, the CLEAR key can be used to delete unwanted characters in the entry box.
The terminal's Zero key (listed as key code 30 in the manual's key code table). In calibration, the Capture Zero function captures the zero point of the scale.
The terminal's Tare key (key code 24 in the manual's key code table). The TARE TABLE softkey opens the tare table search screen for stored tare records.

ideas.h: Calibration sits behind an access level

ideas.h: The terminal keeps a calibration memory
ideas.text: The Information Recall options include a Metrology Recall alongside Weight Recall and System Information Recall. The recall screens are the terminal's own record of its metrology information, kept separate from normal weighing.

ideas.text: In the default settings table, Capture Zero, Capture Span and Step Calibration are Administrator-level functions, while things like Weight Rate are Maintenance level. If calibration functions will not run, check who is signed in before suspecting the scale.

IND570xx.name: IND570xx
IND570xx.intro: The IND570 has five softkey buttons along the bottom of the display, each identified by the graphic icon shown directly above it, plus a 12-key alphanumeric keypad. Up to 15 softkey functions can be shown on three separate rows.
menus: Getting in: the SETUP softkey enters the setup menu. Together with INFORMATION RECALL it must always be present on the home screen; they are in positions 9 and 10 by default.
Moving around: press the UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys to move the focus. As a different position gains the focus, its assignment is shown in text toward the bottom of the screen.
Changing a setting: press the ENTER key to open the assignment selection box, use the UP or DOWN navigation keys to scroll until the desired selection is in focus, then press ENTER to select it.

Getting out: the EXIT softkey returns from an edit screen to the previous setup screen. If you are typing letters and chose the wrong group, the ESCAPE softkey ends the entry without accepting any of the new data.

More softkey rows: a MORE DOWN symbol at the lower-right corner of the screen means more softkey selections are available. Press the DOWN navigation key to display the additional screens, and UP to come back.

keys.does: Press ENTER to open the assignment selection box, then press ENTER again to select the assignment that is in focus. In data entry, press ENTER to accept the entries.
The UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT navigation keys move the focus among positions and screens. The assignment of the position in focus is shown in text toward the bottom of the screen.
Enters the setup menu (listed in the icon table as 'Enter Setup Menu'). It must always be present on the home screen and cannot be removed from it.
Opens the information recall options: Weight Recall, Metrology Recall, System Information Recall, Service Information Recall, and Print.
Returns from an edit screen to the setup screen you came from, for example from the Softkey Edit screen back to the Softkeys Setup Screen.
Ends a data entry without accepting any of the new data typed. The data in the entry field reverts to whatever was in the entry box before the entry was started.
While entering data, the CLEAR key can be used to delete unwanted characters in the entry box.
The terminal's Zero key (listed as key code 30 in the manual's key code table). In calibration, the Capture Zero function captures the zero point of the scale.
The terminal's Tare key (key code 24 in the manual's key code table). The TARE TABLE softkey opens the tare table search screen for stored tare records.
The Print function appears among the Information Recall options for printing records; the keypad Print key is key code 23 in the manual's key code table.

Shown when previous softkey screens are available above the current one. Press the UP navigation key to display the previous softkey screen.

IND246.name: IND246
IND246.intro: The IND246 front panel (p.18) is a graphic LCD with a white LED backlight and 25 keys: the ON/OFF key, four scale function keys, three operational keys and the Print/Enter key under the display, navigation keys at the bottom right, and an alphanumeric keypad at the right of the display for typing numbers and letters. There are no separate annunciator lamps on this terminal - its signs are icons drawn on the display itself.
menus: Setup is worked from the front panel: the navigation keys and the Print/Enter key are used to enter the setup menu, and the book's Chapter 3, Configuration, walks through the setup screens themselves.
Use the navigation arrow keys to move to the setup element you want, then press Print/Enter to select it - Print/Enter is the key that picks things and takes values in setup.
Type values with the alphanumeric keypad at the right of the display. While you type, your entry shows on the data-entry line at the bottom of the normal weighing display.
The bottom line of the weighing display is the data-entry line. If you are not sure whether the terminal took what you typed, that is the line to watch.

keys.does: Turns the terminal on and off. It is one of the keys positioned under the display.
Zeroes the scale. Zero is one of the basic weighing functions (zero, tare, clear, unit switching and print) that have their own front panel keys on this terminal.

Tares the scale, storing the container weight so the display shows net. A tare value can also be typed in with the alphanumeric keypad, which is there for simple, quick entry of tare and identification information.
The clear key, one of the basic weighing functions given its own front panel key, alongside zero, tare, unit switching and print.
Switches the weight units between the primary and secondary units picked in setup. The primary unit can be grams, kilograms, pounds, tons or metric tons; the secondary unit adds ounces to that list.
Prints, and works as the Enter key in setup: together with the navigation keys it is used to enter the setup menu, to select setup elements, and to enter values in setup.
The arrow keys at the bottom right of the display. They move you around inside the setup menu so you can reach and highlight the setup elements you want.

The number and letter keys at the right of the display, for simple, quick entry of tare values and identification (ID) information. What you type appears on the data-entry line at the bottom of the weighing display.

lights.does: The single line at the top of the display. It shows terminal status and operator error displays and messages; time and date and the status of the Digital I/O can also be displayed in this area when so configured in setup.
Shows whether the big weight reading is Gross or Net. The weight legend sits on the line below the weight display, and tare values also appear on this line, to the left of the display.
An icon on the line below the weight display. It shows when the scale is sitting at the center of zero - the empty scale is truly at zero.
An icon on the line below the weight display, next to the center of zero icon. It shows when the scale is in motion, so the weight on screen is still moving.
The weight units shown on the line below the weight display, so you always know whether the number is pounds, kilograms, grams, tons, metric tons or ounces before you believe it.

ideas.h: Gross, net, and tare
ideas.text: The big weight display shows either Gross or Net weight. Gross is everything on the scale; net is what is left after the tare (the container weight) is taken away. The legend line under the weight tells you which one you are looking at, and the tare value itself appears on that same line at the left, so you never have to guess which number is on screen.

ideas.h: The system line is the terminal's message strip
ideas.text: The single line across the very top of the display is where the terminal talks to you: it shows terminal status and operator error messages. If something is wrong, look there first. When set up to do so, it can also show the time and date and the status of the digital inputs and outputs.

ideas.h: Icons instead of lights
ideas.text: This terminal draws its signs on the display instead of lighting separate lamps. The center-of-zero icon says the empty scale is truly at zero, and the motion icon says the weight is still moving. Both sit on the line under the weight, next to the units and the gross/net legend.

ideas.h: Settings can be backed up off the terminal
ideas.text: Configuration and calibration settings can be backed up and restored using an SD memory device or the InSite SL PC tool that comes with the terminal. A backup taken after a good calibration means a swapped or repaired terminal can be brought back to the same settings.

ideas.h: Approved scales are sealed scales
ideas.text: When the IND246 is used in a metrologically approved (legal-for-trade) application, the metrology security switch SW1-1 must be in its ON position and the enclosure protected with the wire security seal. If that seal is broken, the scale's approved status is in question until it is checked and resealed properly.

Move through the setup menu to the item you want.
Types the values - calibration weights, IDs, and setup numbers.
Zeroes the scale; the empty-scale starting point of any calibration.
Shows the weight is still moving - wait until it clears before trusting a reading.

SCT-3300.name: SCT-3300
SCT-3300.intro: The SCT-3300 is an analog load cell transmitter, not an indicator. It has no display, no keypad, and no weighing panel of its own. It takes the load cell signal in and sends out an analog signal (milliamps or volts) to a host indicator or PLC, and that host is where the weight is read (p.6). This short card covers the only adjustments on the unit itself.
menus: There are no menus on this unit. Adjustment is done with the on-board potentiometer and jumper (p.6), and reading, zero, and calibration are watched at the host indicator or PLC that takes its analog output.

keys.does: The stability adjustment (the analog filter). If the displayed weight is not steady, turn P3 clockwise to reduce the oscillations. To deactivate the filter, remove the J2 jumper.
Switches the analog filter off when removed. Leave it in place to keep using the P3 filter adjustment; take it out to deactivate the filter.

ideas.h: The panel lives on the host
ideas.text: The SCT-3300's terminals take load cell excitation and signal in and send an analog output (mA or volts) out. Whatever is wired to that output — an indicator or a PLC — is where weight is displayed and where zero and span calibration are watched, which is why this book's panel card is short.

ideas.h: Shaky weight? Reach for the filter
ideas.text: If the weight reading on the host will not sit still because of vibration, the fix on this box is the analog filter: turn potentiometer P3 clockwise to calm the oscillations, or remove the J2 jumper to switch the filter off entirely.

SCT-3300.refs: References: Rice Lake SCT-3300 manual: Weight Oscillations (Vibration) — analog filter potentiometer P3 and J2 jumper, and the analog output (mA/volt) terminals — p. 6. Short card by design: this book describes no display, keypad, or annunciators, so there is no front-panel calibration path (pre is empty); panel work happens at the host indicator.

SCT-4XD.name: SCT-4XD
SCT-4XD.intro: The SCT-4XD is a belt scale integrator: it reads the load on a moving conveyor belt and the belt's speed, and keeps flow rate and running totals. Its front panel is an LED display with a small keypad — the book's key table (p.16) gives each key one job in the configuration menus and another in weighing, and long presses open the doors.
menus: Two doors in: hold the up (increase) key while powering up to open the configuration menu, or hold PRINT to open the User menu, where Dynamic Zero Capture lives (p.16, p.27-28).

Typing a number: press C first to clear the old value — the book insists on this before entering new data — then MODE picks the digit to change, the up and down keys change it, and PRINT confirms it (p.16, p.26).
PRINT enters a step and confirms a value; the key table also has a key that exits a step without saving, and one that drops the unit to Standby in weighing (p.16).

Test Weight Calibration (p.26) holds the test weight value, the delay for positioning the test mass, the test distance (or time, when no encoder is fitted), and the test weight material correction factor.

Diagnostics (p.32) shows the program version, live A/D millivolts, counts and weight, and the stored calibration points, and can test every LED segment and every key. Alarms (p.30) cover belt off-track, flow overload, flow-rate and weight out of range, an external alarm, and load cell overload.

keys.does: Enters a step and confirms a value. Held down, it opens the User menu; in that menu a further press begins Dynamic Zero Capture with the belt running empty, and with test weights applied to the running belt a press begins the Test Weight Procedure (p.16, pp.27-28).

Selects which digit of a number you are changing — for example, picking the digit of a temporary test weight. In weighing it steps the display through the belt scale data: flow rate, load, speed, partial total, and general total (p.16, p.30).
Clears what is on the display before you type. The book's rule for front-panel entry: press C to clear the previous data before entering new data (p.26).
Increases the digit being changed and scrolls up through menus. Held down at power-up, it accesses the configuration menu (p.16).
Decreases the digit being changed and scrolls down through menus. A long press begins Dynamic Zero (p.16).

lights.does: The flow-rate reading — how fast material is moving over the belt. This is what the display shows on start-up, before you step to anything else.
The load reading: the material weight the integrator is measuring on the belt.
The active encoder speed — how fast the belt itself is travelling, shown in 0.01 m/s (0.1 ft/min).
The partial total: the running total you can watch (and use to check repeatability run to run) alongside the general total.
The general total: the grand accumulated tonnage the integrator has counted.

ideas.h: It weighs a belt that never stops
ideas.text: A belt scale integrator does not weigh a still load. It combines the load on the belt with the belt's speed from the encoder to get flow rate, and keeps counting into a partial total and a general total. On start-up the display shows flow rate; MODE steps through load, speed, and the two totals.

ideas.h: Zero means an empty, moving belt
ideas.text: Dynamic Zero Capture teaches the integrator what 'nothing on the belt' looks like while the belt runs. Hold PRINT for the User menu until ZEr.CAP shows, then press PRINT to begin; WAIT shows during capture, and when it finishes the unit returns to normal operating mode with any displayed belt load adjusted to zero.

ideas.h: Test weights teach it the correction factor
ideas.text: Calibration hangs a known test weight on the running belt: the Test Weight Calibration menu holds the weight value, a delay to position it, and the test distance or time. Press PRINT to start the capture; the indicator displays Factor briefly, then the new calibrated correction factor. If the displayed test weight does not match the applied weight, the material factor (t.W.Mat.F) corrects it.

ideas.h: A trickle does not count
ideas.text: Below the dead band — a percentage of maximum flow-rate set in Belt Parameters — the totals do not increase, so dribbles and dust do not add phantom tonnage. And if 'store totals' is set to YES the totals are saved to permanent memory every few seconds; set to NO, they are lost when the power goes off.

pre.short: Hold for the User menu; starts zero and test-weight captures; confirms values.
Picks the digit you are changing; walks the display data in weighing.
Press before typing — clears the old value.
Increases the digit; hold at power-up for the configuration menu.
Decreases the digit; long press begins Dynamic Zero.

WI-127.name: WI-127
WI-127.intro: The WI-127 front panel is a set of job keys - SELECT, UNITS, TARE, PRINT, ZERO, ENTER, MENU, F1, F2, F3 and a numeric keypad - plus the display annunciators (the little signs that light beside the weight): the unit labels lb, kg and oz, the ACCEPT sign, and the checkweigh signs Under, Accept and Over. Almost everything else on this indicator lives in its menu trees (the book covers the 110 and 127 menu structures), and those same front panel keys do the menu work too.
menus: Two menu trees run this indicator - the book covers both the 110 and the 127 structures. Scale sets units, capacity, division size, zero and motion behavior; Options sets what the front panel buttons do and what gets printed; Serial sets the ports; and service items like the loadcell counts display live in these trees too.
To get out of a menu, press SELECT to return to normal weighing. If SAVE? is displayed, press ENTER to save the changes you made - SELECT gets you out, ENTER keeps the work.
Numbers are typed with the numeric keypad and taken with ENTER: capacity, division size, zero-range percentages, update rate and averaging values all go in that way.

The lists themselves can be edited from the panel: press + / - to insert a display mode or a unit into the SELECT or UNITS cycle (the ACCEPT annunciator lights while you insert), and press ZERO to delete the item showing.

Every front panel key can be turned on or off in Options > Buttons - SELECT, UNITS, TARE, PRINT, ZERO, F1, F2 and F3, and access to the User menu. If a key seems dead in the field, it may simply be switched off in there.

keys.does: Steps the weight display through its display modes - the default list is Gross, then Tare, then Net, in that order, and the list can be customized. It also gets you out: press SELECT to exit back to normal weighing mode, and press ENTER while SAVE? is displayed if you need to save changes first.

Steps the displayed weight through the units of measure list (Unit 1, Unit 2, Unit 3 by default). It also lets you view settings like capacity and division size in the other units of measure, and in the loadcell view it toggles between raw counts and the mV/V reading.

The pushbutton tare key: tares the scale so the display shows net weight. Tare can be limited in the Options menu - pushbutton tare can allow all nonnegative values, exclude zero, or be disabled - and a tare value can also be typed in when numeric tare entry is enabled.

Zeroes the scale, within the zero range set in the Scale menu (the -Range and Range items, a percent of capacity referenced from the deadload; 100% is the default). It also deletes: with an item displayed while editing the display-mode or units lists, pressing ZERO deletes that item from the list.

Prints. Which layouts go to which ports for a pushbutton print is picked in the Options menu (the default group sends Gross, Tare and Net). If group print entry is enabled, key in the number of the group you want and press PRINT to print that group from the front panel.

The take-it key: accepts the value you keyed in. With CAPACity displayed, for example, you key in the new capacity on the numeric keypad and press ENTER to accept it. When SAVE? is displayed on the way out of a menu, pressing ENTER saves your changes.
Works during label and text entry: pressing MENU accepts the character value on the display and moves you to the next character position.

Inserts while you edit: with an item displayed in the display-mode or units list, press + / - to insert a new item ahead of it (the ACCEPT annunciator lights while you do this). It also inserts a new character ahead of the one showing during label entry.
The first function key. Its default job is to open the tare registers so you can view and edit the 10 stored tare registers. It can be enabled or disabled in Options > Buttons.
The second function key. Its default job is identification number entry - the ID number you can view and edit. It can be enabled or disabled in Options > Buttons.
The third function key. Its default job is to open the cutoff values - the Under, Target and Cutoffs registers used by the checkweigh outputs. It can be enabled or disabled in Options > Buttons.

Types numbers: capacity, division size, zero ranges, filter and averaging values are all keyed in with the numeric keypad and then accepted with ENTER. Type leading zeroes too if you want them in printouts.

lights.does: The three unit annunciators on the front panel, labeled lb, kg and oz. Whichever one is lit tells you the unit of the weight on display. In the Scale menu each annunciator can be assigned a different unit of measure (or none), so the lit label is the setup's word for the unit, not just the printing on the bezel.

Lights while you are inserting an item into the display-mode list or the units list with the + / - key - it is the indicator's way of saying the insert is armed and it is waiting for you to pick what to add.

The checkweigh signs. The onboard cutoff outputs follow them: Cutoff 1 follows the Under annunciator, Cutoff 2 follows Accept, and Cutoff 3 follows Over, so the signs tell you at a glance whether the weight is under, inside, or over the target band.

Annunciator 5, used in the in-motion (conveyor) weighing application: it shows that the display is holding the current in-motion weighment, which stays on screen for seven seconds after each weighment is calculated or until the next one begins.

ideas.h: Gross, tare, net - and SELECT walks between them
ideas.text: Repeatedly pressing SELECT cycles the weight display through its mode list, in the default order Gross, Tare, Net. One catch built into the indicator: SELECT by itself cannot switch the display into net mode - but taring a nonzero value puts the indicator into net mode temporarily, so you can see the net weight it is working with.

ideas.h: The unit labels on the panel can be re-assigned
ideas.text: The three unit annunciators on the front panel are labeled lb, kg and oz, but in the Scale menu each one can be assigned a different unit of measure - pounds, kilograms, grams, ounces, tons, tonnes, or none - and you can even build a custom unit, like a stone (14 pounds equals 1 stone), with its own serial label. The label on the bezel may not be the unit the indicator is really using, so check before you believe a reading.

ideas.h: Averaging is how this indicator steadies a shaky weight
ideas.text: The indicator converts the load cell signal 60 times a second, and the Average setting decides how many of those conversions are averaged into each displayed weight - set either as display intervals (x disp.) or as an exact number of A-D conversions (x a-ds). More averaging means a steadier display; the book suggests display intervals because the average then always stays a multiple of the display rate.

ideas.h: Write down the calibration numbers
ideas.text: The calibration menu's Print item prints the calibration information out of port 1. Those numbers can be valuable if you ever have an indicator failure - they are the record of how this scale was taught its weights, the same reason you keep calibration constants written down for any indicator.

ideas.h: Reset is the factory starting over point
ideas.text: The calibration menu's Reset item puts the calibration points back to factory default values: 0 lbs at 0 mV/V and 5000 lbs at 1 mV/V. The book offers it for when the calibration values have been confused and you would like to put working values back in - after a reset, the scale needs to be calibrated again before you trust it.

pre.short: The take-it key - accepts every value you key in, and saves at the SAVE? prompt.
Steps the display between Gross, Tare and Net; also the way out of menus.
Types the numbers - capacity, divisions, and the calibration values.
Shows the weight - and settings like capacity - in the other units.
Zeroes the scale inside its zero range; the empty-scale starting point.
